author: Tobias Sennhauser
title: Rückblick auf die Sommersession 2026
content:
Mercosur-Freihandelsabkommen


Das Freihandelsabkommen zwischen den EFTA-Staaten und Mercosur (

26.033

) soll den Handel mit Brasilien, Argentinien, Paraguay und Uruguay öffnen. Der Nationalrat lehnt die Vorlage mit 96 zu 86 Stimmen bei 9 Enthaltungen knapp ab. Zuvor waren mehrere Begleitmassnahmen gescheitert: die Übernahme der EU-Entwaldungsverordnung (108 zu 83 Stimmen), ein Agrarkredit von 880 Millionen Franken über acht Jahre (94 zu 91 Stimmen) sowie Anträge zu einem Amazonienfonds und gegen Zwangsarbeit. Nun ist der Ständerat am Zug.


SP und Grüne stimmten gegen die Vorlage, dafür waren FDP und GLP. Den Ausschlag gaben einige Nein-Stimmen aus der SVP- und der Mitte-Fraktion. Der Schweizer Bauernverband warnte vor zusätzlichen Importen und Druck auf die einheimischen Märkte. Der Wirtschaftsdachverband economiesuisse spricht hingegen von einem «fatalen Zeichen für den Wirtschaftsstandort» und fordert eine Korrektur durch den Ständerat.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF):

 Dieses Abkommen hätte Importe von Fleisch aus Ländern mit tieferen Tierschutz- und Umweltstandards erleichtert. Dieses Fleisch käme aus Produktionssystemen, die mit Entwaldung und Massentierhaltung verbunden sind. Wir lehnen das Freihandelsabkommen mit den Mercosur-Staaten ab und appellieren an den Ständerat, der grossen Kammer zu folgen und die Vorlage zu versenken.


Stopfleber-Initiative


Die Volksinitiative «Ja zum Importverbot für Stopfleber» (

24.089

) will die Einfuhr von Stopfleber verbieten. Nachdem sich der Nationalrat in der Frühjahrssession als Erstrat für einen indirekten Gegenentwurf (25.404) aussprach, folgte ihm nun der Ständerat mit 24 zu 15 Stimmen bei 3 Enthaltungen. Der Gegenentwurf verzichtet auf ein Importverbot und setzt stattdessen auf die bereits eingeführte Deklarationspflicht: Ab 2027 müssen Produkte von gestopften Enten und Gänsen den Hinweis tragen, dass sie unter für Tiere schmerzhaften Bedingungen erzeugt wurden. Der Bund soll die Importe beobachten und dem Parlament alle fünf Jahre Bericht erstatten.


Die bürgerliche Mehrheit und der Bundesrat lehnen ein Importverbot ab und verweisen auf internationale Handelsverpflichtungen und die schwierige Kontrolle verarbeiteter Produkte.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF):

 Eine Deklarationspflicht ist ein Hohn angesichts des Leids der Tiere. Wir halten an der Initiative und damit auch am Importverbot fest.


Importverbot für tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelze


Der Bundesrat verlängert am 5. Juni 2026 die Übergangsbestimmungen des Pelz-Importverbots, das am 1. Juli 2025 in Kraft getreten ist. Neu dürfen tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelzerzeugnisse erst ab dem 1. Juli 2029 nicht mehr eingeführt und ab dem 1. Juli 2030 nicht mehr verkauft werden. Die Pelzbranche soll damit Zeit erhalten, ihre Produktionssysteme an ein geplantes Zertifizierungsprogramm für angeblich nicht-tierquälerisch erzeugte Pelze anzupassen.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF): Für uns ist unverständlich, wieso die Pelzindustrie mehr Zeit erhält. Die Produktion von Pelzen geschieht meist in tierquälerischer, in der Schweiz verbotenen Haltungsbedingungen. Für die sogenannten Pelztiere bedeutet jeder Tag, an dem wir warten, Leid und Tod.


Kultiviertes Fleisch


Eine Motion (

23.3941

) verlangt, die Zulassungs- und Bewilligungsverfahren für neuartige Lebensmittel, insbesondere kultiviertes Fleisch und Produkte aus Präzisionsfermentation, zu vereinfachen und zu beschleunigen. Der Nationalrat hatte den Vorstoss in der Sondersession vom Mai 2025 mit 94 zu 87 Stimmen bei 8 Enthaltungen angenommen. Der Ständerat lehnte ihn am 8. Juni 2026 auf Antrag seiner Kommission und des Bundesrates stillschweigend ab. Damit ist die Motion erledigt.


Einschätzung von Tier im Fokus (TIF):

 Kultiviertes Fleisch könnte dazu beitragen, die Tötung von Tieren mittelfristig stark zu reduzieren. Für uns ist es deshalb unverständlich, gewaltfreie Alternativen zu blockieren. Die Ablehnung dieser Motion zementiert den Status quo der Tiernutzung.


Tiertransporte


Ab dem 1. Juli 2026 dürfen Tiere neu auch nachts sowie an Sonn- und Feiertagen transportiert werden. Bisher waren nur Transporte von Schlachttieren und Sportpferden vom Nacht- und Sonntagsfahrverbot ausgenommen; alle anderen Lebendtiertransporte brauchten eine kostenpflichtige Sonderbewilligung mit 48 Stunden Vorlauf. title: Katjes: Naschen ohne Tierversuche!
content:
Die Katjes Fassin GmbH + Co. KG, der Anbieter hinter den leckeren veganen Fruchtgummis in süßer, saurer oder Lakritz-Variante, ist PETAs Programm „Eat Without Experiments“ beigetreten und wendet sich damit von

Tierversuchen

 ab. Auch die bekannte Ahoj-Brause sowie die Wick-Hustenbonbons gehören zu dem Unternehmen.


Das Programm macht es Verbraucher:innen leicht,

Lebensmittel- und Getränkehersteller

 zu finden, die keine Tierversuche durchführen.


Die „Eat Without Experiments“-Datenbank kategorisiert Hersteller und Marken nach ihrer Politik in Bezug auf Tierversuche: von Unternehmen, die Tierversuche durchführen, bis hin zu solchen, die wie die Katjes Fassin GmbH + Co. KGdie PETA-Verpflichtung unterzeichnet haben, keine Tierversuche durchzuführen, sofern dies nicht ausdrücklich gesetzlich vorgeschrieben ist – oder im besten Fall auch diese unter keinen Umständen zulassen. Untersuchungen zeigen, dass sich 74 Prozent der Verbraucher:innen eine größere Transparenz wünschen, was die Haltung von Unternehmen zu wichtigen Themen wie Tierversuchen betrifft. [1] Unternehmen, die sich PETAs „Eat-Without-Experiments“-Programm anschließen, nehmen das ernst und tragen maßgeblich zu einer tierfreundlicheren Gesellschaft und ethischem Konsum bei.


Jetzt lesen


Produktentwicklung


Diese großen Lebensmittelhersteller sind tierversuchsfrei


Auch für Lebensmittel werden Tiere in Tierversuchen gequält. Jetzt lesen, welche Unternehmen und Lebensmittelhersteller tierversuchsfrei sind!


Jetzt lesen


Helfen Sie mit, Tierversuche auch für Haushaltsprodukte zu beenden


Tierversuche werden nicht nur für Nahrungsmittel durchgeführt. Sie stecken hinter weit mehr Produkten, als viele Menschen vermuten. Vielen ist nicht bewusst, dass beispielsweise auch Haushaltsprodukte wie Wasch- und Reinigungsmittel oft an Tieren getestet werden.

author: webadmin
title: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs uncover horrific scenes at industrial-scale gamebird rearing site
content:
Dead gamebirds burned in bonfire pits in breach of animal by-product regulations


Guest post by Wiltshire Hunt Sabs: In July, after being alerted alerted to illegal practises at a local shoot, they paid a visit to the Fonthill Estate in Wiltshire and what they found was truly horrific – a bonfire full of dead charred birds, set next to the industrial sized operation.


To understand the significance of this site, some background is necessary.


The Fonthill Estate extends to around 10,000 acres and has been owned by the Morrison family since 1830. The current owner, Alastair Morrison, 3rd Baron Margadale, inherited both the estate and the title following the death of his father, Major James Morrison, in 2003. Although hereditary peers lost their automatic seats in the House of Lords following the House of Lords Act 1999, Lord Margadale was later appointed Deputy Lieutenant of Wiltshire.


This bonfire had clearly been used for some time, possibly thousands of birds ended up here.


His first wife, Lady Sophia Cavendish, is the daughter of Andrew Cavendish, 11th Duke of Devonshire, and Deborah Mitford, one of the famous Mitford sisters. The family’s connections illustrate how closely this estate is intertwined with Britain’s landed aristocracy and establishment.


Bordering the estate is

Stockton Wood and Down

 a 61.5 hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), situated within approximately 500metres of the rearing pens. The site supports a diverse range of flora, including several rare and notable plant species, while its birdlife includes buzzards, green and great spotted woodpeckers, nuthatches, nightingales, lesser whitethroats and grasshopper warblers.


The rearing pens and bonfire were situated within 500m of the SSSI.


The environmental impacts of intensive pheasant releases are well documented. High densities of released gamebirds can alter woodland ecosystems, damage sensitive ground flora, enrich soils with excessive nutrients and cause long-term degradation around release pens. Guidance recommends rotating pen locations to allow habitats to recover and to provide fresh ground for successive flocks.


This site has to be seen to be believed. The scale is enormous, with many thousands of pheasants and partridges held within the rearing pens. Historic Google Earth imagery indicates that these pens have been used for many years and have expanded significantly over time, with little evidence that the release areas have been moved to allow environmental recovery.


The pens in 2019


The pens more recently, each housing hundreds if not thousands of birds.


As with any intensive bird-rearing operation, mortality rates are unavoidable. High stocking densities, parasites, disease, stress, feather pecking and predation all contribute to a continual accumulation of dead birds requiring lawful disposal.


A view in one of the pens.


Until they are released, these birds are legally classified as livestock, meaning their disposal is governed by strict animal by-product legislation designed to protect public health and prevent the spread of disease.


Fresh bags – many filled with dead birds piled onto the remains of the previous victim – you can see how close to the foliage the bonfire will be, and gas canisters store just behind that tree.


The law is clear. Fallen birds that have died other than by slaughter are classified as Category 2 animal by-products. They must be collected without undue delay, stored securely in sealed, leak-proof containers, and kept away from other animals before collection. Disposal must take place through licensed routes, such as approved rendering plants, incinerators, maggot farms or collection schemes operated through the National Fallen Stock Company.


Just incredible.


The

Direct Burial Or Burning On Farms

 is forbidden.


All video and imagery has been passed to the local authority ANIMAL HEALTH team within Public Health for investigation and the premises are under investigation.


Remains after one bonfire


Beyond the legal implications regarding public health, the disregard for basic fire safety was astonishing. Bonfires were observed on dry, sun-scorched grassland, surrounded by equally dry vegetation and in close proximity to numerous gas cylinders, during one of England’s hottest and driest summers. Such conditions present an obvious and serious fire risk, with potentially severe consequences for people, wildlife and the surrounding countryside.


Truly …

author: Jake Johnson
title: Ocean Temperatures in July Broke Record Due to Fossil Fuel-Driven Super El Niño
content:
“With Big Oil’s earnings skyrocketing while a global food crisis looms, now is the time to act,” said one activist.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Last month’s average global ocean surface temperature was the hottest ever recorded in the month of July, fueled in part by uniquely intense, fossil fuel-driven El Niño conditions that have wreaked deadly havoc around the world this summer.

The European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) said Monday that last month — which ranked as the second warmest July on record — “saw exceptionally high temperatures for the month across a large portion of the tropical Pacific, an area where El Niño conditions are present and forecast to further strengthen in the coming months.” Average global sea surface temperatures (SSTs) were 20.96°C last month, surpassing the July 2023 record of 20.89°C.

“Around Europe, SSTs reached record highs for July along the Atlantic coast and western Mediterranean, associated with widespread strong or severe marine heatwave conditions,” C3S said.

Brian O’Donnell, director of the Campaign for Nature, said the latest Copernicus data “is more than another climate milestone; it is a warning that the natural systems we depend on are being pushed closer to their limits.”

“Governments have become very good at documenting these records. Now they need to become much better at safeguarding the forests, wetlands, and oceans that help regulate the climate and protect communities from the impacts of warming world,” said O’Donnell. “With land and ocean temperatures across Europe breaching records, governments should be investing far more and delivering on their global commitment to protect at least 30% of land and ocean by 2030.”

The new analysis was released as western Europe and other regions faced deadly heat, wildfires, drought, and other extreme weather as the international community, including the US and other leading polluters, fails to rein in fossil fuel use — and as oil and gas giants reap record profits.

“Our leaders’ response has to be swifter and stronger than El Niño,” Anne Jellema, executive director of the environmental group 350.org, said Monday. “We already know that global heating is supercharging extreme weather damage, and the public wants polluters to pay for it. With Big Oil’s earnings skyrocketing while a global food crisis looms, now is the time to act. The only way to stave off a humanitarian disaster is to make those causing it pay upfront — before even more damage is done.”

Scientists have characterized this year’s El Niño, which officially began on June 11, as historically strong and dangerous, earning it the informal “Super El Niño” label.

The Washington Post reported Monday that the 2026 El Niño is “on track to become the strongest ever recorded, with cascading effects on global climate peaking late this year and into next.”

“El Niño’s effects have already been felt around the planet,” the Post observed. “The higher frequency of heat domes worldwide, the nonstop temperature records in Peru and deadly storms in Chile can all be linked to this pattern. As can the destructive typhoons in the western Pacific Ocean and the relative calm of the Atlantic hurricane season so far.”

United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres warned in remarks to reporters last month that El Niño is no longer just “on our doorstep.”

“It is inside the house — and turning up the heat,” said Guterres. “We have already endured a summer of extremes — record-shattering heat domes, apocalyptic wildfires raging in Spain, France, and far beyond. Thousands of lives lost in the scorching conditions.”

“But according to the latest science,” he added, “this is only a warm-up act.”

We are fundraising right now to cover our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: The Canadian Press
title: UBCIC calls on Carney, Smith to halt pipeline advancement
content:
A group that advocates for First Nations across British Columbia is calling on Ottawa and Alberta’s government to halt efforts to advance the

West Coast

 pipeline, saying expanding the oil industry will accelerate climate change and disasters.


“The destructive and disastrous consequences of expanding fossil fuel production extend far beyond any single territory,” the Union of British Columbia Indian Chiefs (UBCIC) said in a letter addressed to Prime Minister Mark Carney and Premier Danielle Smith.


“From catastrophic wildfires to destructive floods and rising seas, the impacts of climate change are already being felt across this country. Every new fossil fuel project deepens that crisis.”


The letter is signed by the group’s heads, including Grand Chief Stewart Phillip, and it said B.C. Premier David Eby also has a copy of it.


The letter came Sunday, a day after the B.C. government issued a state of emergency as more than 100 wildfires burned across the province, with one forcing nearly 25,000 people across two communities east of Vancouver to flee. Nearly half of the wildfires were burning out of control.


The

UBCIC

, a political advocacy group, said it was also publishing the letter on International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples on Sunday.


The group said it wanted to reaffirm that it’s against the pipeline because government has not consulted and co-operated in good faith with the First Nations, noting government has already developed the project’s corridor, named prospective development partners and is publicly promoting its economic case.


“Consultation cannot be meaningful if First Nations are invited only to discuss how a predetermined project will proceed,” it said.


“Nor can equity ownership, loan guarantees, revenue-sharing, employment, or other proposed benefits be treated as substitutes for consent.”


Carney’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the letter.


Alberta’s Ministry of Indigenous Relations said in an email Sunday that the pipeline will provide long-term benefits for Indigenous communities, and create jobs and energy security.


“The West Coast oil pipeline submission is currently under review by the Major Projects Office, which will consult with Indigenous communities as part of determining whether the project is in the national interest,” said press secretary Karah Folk.


“Our government remains committed to ongoing dialogue with First Nations and all partners as this work continues.”


The roughly 1,250-kilometre West Coast pipeline would carry upwards of one-million barrels of crude oil per day from Bruderheim, Alta., to a port near Delta, B.C., for shipment to international markets.


The Alberta government is listed as the pipeline project’s proponent. The pipeline would be owned by Trans Mountain, the Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission and Pembina Pipeline Corporation.


Ottawa took a step last week toward giving the proposed project a national interest designation under the Building Canada Act, which would allow government to fast-track the pipeline and skirt some environmental laws.


The government said it is accepting public feedback until mid-September on the designation.


An Alberta government website said it’s expecting to receive the designation on Oct. 1.


“Following Indigenous consultation and once all approvals and permits are in place, construction could start as early as September 1, 2027,” it said.


Ottawa and Alberta have agreed the pipeline would be conditional on a carbon storage project called Pathways, and vice versa. Pathways, which is owned by various companies, would prevent emissions from increased oil production from entering the atmosphere. It involves a pipeline network that would carry carbon emissions from several sites in northern Alberta to an underground storage hub near Cold Lake, Alta.


A think tank called the Canadian Climate Institute said in July, however, that emissions from the increased production that a new West Coast pipeline would enable far eclipse what Pathways would prevent from entering the atmosphere.


The West Coast pipeline is among several projects that have been approved or proposed under Carney’s Major Projects Office, which is headquartered in Calgary.


Ottawa has said the projects are meant to be of national interest and strengthen Canada’s autonomy, provide economic benefits, advance Indigenous interests and meet Canada’s climate change goals in a rapidly shifting global …

title: COP31 öncesi iklim tiyatrosu: Ev sahiplerinden fosil yakıtlara milyarlarca dolarlık fon
content:
Fotoğraf: Özer Akdemir/Evrensel

Çanakkale — Dünya genelinde iklim krizine karşı somut adımlar atılmasına yönelik çağrılar yükselirken, yaklaşan COP31 iklim müzakerelerine başkanlık etmeye hazırlanan Avustralya ve zirvenin diğer ev sahibi Türkiye'nin fosil yakıtları milyarlarca dolarla fonlamaya devam etmesi, karbon azaltımı taahhütlerinin samimiyetini derin bir şüpheye düşürüyor. WWF Avustralya'nın hazırladığı yeni rapor, müzakerelerin başkanı Avustralya’nın fosil yakıtlara, yenilenebilir enerji kaynaklarına kıyasla tam dört kat daha fazla devlet desteği sağladığını gözler önüne seriyor. Diğer ev sahibi Türkiye'nin ise yerli kömür santrallerine sunduğu astronomik alım garantileri ve fosil yakıt destekleri, küresel iklim zirvelerinin somut eylemler yerine bir şeyler yapılıyormuş gibi algı yaratma çabası yani bir tiyatro olduğu yönündeki sert eleştirileri bir kez daha haklı çıkarıyor.

WWF Avustralya tarafından yayımlanan rapor, Antalya'da düzenlenecek iklim zirvesinde müzakerelere başkanlık etme rolünü üstlenen Avustralya'nın iklim eylemindeki çelişkilerini çarpıcı verilerle ortaya koyuyor. Ülke bir yandan yenilenebilir enerji ihracatı vizyonu çizerken, diğer yandan fosil yakıt üretiminin genişletilmesine aktif olarak olanak tanımaya devam ediyor. Raporda bu durum, Avustralya’nın yenilenebilir enerji alanındaki gelecek potansiyelini gerçekleştirebilmesi için bir ticaret ve yatırım ortağı olarak ihtiyaç duyduğu kesinliği ve güvenilirliği zedeleyen çelişkili bir strateji olarak nitelendiriliyor.

Fotoğraf: Özer Akdemir/Evrensel

Fotoğraf: Özer Akdemir/Evrensel

Rapora göre, Avustralya'da fosil yakıt sistemleri, yenilenebilir enerjiye kıyasla dört kat daha fazla devlet desteği alıyor. Fosil yakıtlara yılda 20,1 milyar Avustralya doları bütçe ayrılırken, yenilenebilir enerjiye yalnızca 4,6 milyar Avustralya doları destek veriliyor. Fosil yakıtların toplumsal maliyetinin, bu sistemlerin devlet bütçesine sağladığı net mali katkı olan 23 milyar Avustralya dolarından neredeyse beş kat daha yüksek olduğu hesaplanıyor. Fosil yakıtların bütçeye sağladığı net katkı, yarattığı toplumsal maliyetin yalnızca yüzde 20'sine denk geliyor.

COP31’in diğer ev sahibi Türkiye’nin karnesi de en az Avustralya kadar derin çelişkiler barındırıyor. Türkiye, zirve öncesinde 2035 yılı için 120 GW güneş ve rüzgâr enerjisi kapasitesine ulaşma hedefi açıklamıştı. Ancak, bu hedeflerin hemen arkasından açıklanan devasa kömür teşvikleri, yenilenebilir enerji dönüşümü iddialarını kağıt üzerinde bırakıyor. Eylül 2025'te Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanı Alparslan Bayraktar tarafından açıklanan yeni teşvik paketi kapsamında, yerli kömür santrallerinde üretilen elektriğe 2030 yılına kadar 7,5 dolar/cent alım garantisi sağlanacağı duyuruldu. Dahası, yeni kurulacak kömür santralleri de 2045 yılına kadar alım garantisi kapsamına alındı.

Bağımsız bir iklim enerji düşünce kuruluşu olan Ember Türkiye'nin yaptığı analizler, bu teşvikin yarattığı büyük ekonomik ve çevresel çelişkileri gözler önüne seriyor. Belirlenen 75 USD/MWh'lik fiyat garantisi, yerli kömür santrallerinin son bir yıllık dönemdeki ortalama elektrik satış fiyatından yüzde 12, ortalama elektrik üretim maliyetlerinden ise yüzde 36 daha yüksek. Ember'in ilk raporunda kömür santrallerine 2030'a kadar en az 8,7 milyar dolar ödeneceği öngörülmüştü. Ancak alım garantisi detaylarının netleşmesi ve yüzde 60 kapasite faktörü sınırının görülmesiyle birlikte, bu faturanın 12 milyar doların üzerinde olacağı hesaplandı. Kömüre aktarılacak olan bu devasa kaynak, kısıtlı kapasite nedeniyle yeni santral yatırımlarına engel olan elektrik şebekesinin yenilenmesi için beş yıllığına ayrılan bütçeden yüzde 53 daha fazla!

Sürdürülebilir Ekonomi ve Finans Araştırmaları Derneği'nin Fosil Yakıt Teşvikleri Takibi çalışması, Türkiye’nin fosil yakıtları koruma eğilimini destekleyen başka çarpıcı veriler sunuyor. Türkiye, 2024 yılında kömürden elektrik üretiminde 122 TWh ile tarihi bir zirveye ulaşarak Polonya ve Almanya'yı geride bıraktı ve Avrupa'da kömürden en çok elektrik üreten ülke konumuna yerleşti. Türkiye Ulusal Enerji Planı, 2030 yılına kadar toplam 1,7 GW, 2035 yılına kadar ise 3,2 GW yeni kömürlü termik santral kapasitesinin kurulu güce dahil edilmesini öngörüyor. Türkiye'nin COP29'da açıkladığı 2053 Uzun Dönemli İklim Değişikliği Stratejisi belgesinde ise kömürden bahsedilmezken, fosil yakıtlardan çıkışa dair de herhangi bir takvim paylaşılmadı.

author: Unknown
title: Mining project threatens Pasur's main water basin
content:
Mining and extraction projects promoted by companies and private investors continue to expand across Kurdistan, posing growing threats to ecosystems, farmland and grazing areas. These projects not only endanger biodiversity but also put the livelihoods of local communities at risk, with potentially far-reaching consequences for the region's future.


The impact is compounded by an intensifying drought linked to the climate crisis, as planned mining exploration increasingly targets critical water basins. One such project is planned in Kulp (Pasur). The district is also expected to lose dozens of villages to flooding under the Silvan Dam Project.


The proposed mining project covers the area surrounding Akdoruk (Gavgas) village, as well as Islamköy (Kuyê), Dolu (Arketin), Narlıca (Awdegês) and Kaynak (Xuruç), threatening the drinking water sources of hundreds of villages. Although exploratory drilling has begun, local residents challenged the project in court after organizing protests against it. If the project proceeds, tens of thousands of people could face severe water shortages.


Project threatens to destroy a vital water basin


A project to explore for gold, copper and iron ore has been proposed by Kılıç Kardeşler Madencilik Inşaat Mühendislik ve Proje Hizmetleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi. After receiving a positive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) decision and the necessary operating license, the company sought to begin work in the area in 2024. The project, however, was met with resistance from local villagers.


Company personnel, accompanied by gendarmerie forces, entered the village to begin exploratory drilling, but villagers who protested were prevented from accessing the project site.


Mining approved despite water authority's warning


The planned project area is designated as both highland pasture and grazing land, while the drinking water needs of 60 neighborhoods and hamlets in the district are supplied from the same basin.


A report prepared by the Diyarbakır Water and Sewerage Administration (DISKI) warned that "No mining exploration should be carried out here. This is a water basin." Despite DİSKİ forwarding that warning to the General Directorate of Mining and Petroleum Affairs (MAPEG), the agency approved a Group IV mining license for the area. Local residents, DISKI and their lawyers continue to challenge the project through legal action and public opposition.


New court-ordered site inspection


Villagers later announced that they had taken the project to court, filing a lawsuit with the support of the Diyarbakır Bar Association seeking the annulment of both the positive EIA decision and the mining license.


 


The Diyarbakır 2nd Administrative Court ordered a new on-site inspection and an expert assessment. A delegation that included villagers and lawyers visited the area in recent days to take part in the court-ordered inspection. Residents said they hope the findings will support their case and pledged to continue both their legal challenge and their public campaign against the project.


Dozens of communities will face water shortages


Murad Ipek, co-mayor of Kulp, said the project would destroy not only drinking water sources but also the water used for livestock and irrigation, arguing that it would bring no benefit to the district. He spoke to ANF about the project's potential impact.


Ipek said: "Water shortages have long been a serious problem in our district. A mining project covering roughly 5,000 hectares is planned in the Islamköy and Gavgas area. If it goes ahead, around 100 settlements, including the district center, will face severe water shortages. The rivers flowing through the Gavgas region will also suffer extensive damage. There is no doubt that this project will result in ecological destruction."


The dam and the mine will accelerate migration


Ipek said the municipality has been working to improve access to water resources but that mining projects are making those efforts increasingly difficult. title: Videos from the World Social Forum
content:
By World BEYOND War, August 9, 2026


For background, read:


Nonviolent Citizen Resistance Moves the World Social Forum Forward in Benin


Here are some video recordings from the World Social Forum:


Intercontinental Dialogues on the Environmental Crisis:


The session brings together activists and scholars from different traditions who exchange perspectives on the ecological crisis, peace, democracy, and social justice, while exploring the wisdom resources that inspire their movements. It examines whether today’s environmental, political, and social crises reflect a deeper civilizational crisis, and discusses pathways toward ecological justice, peace, and a more sustainable future.


Standing with Sudan: Humanitarian action and global advocacy:


The session explores how civil society, humanitarian organizations, grassroots movements, and international networks are responding to the ongoing crisis in Sudan, and how they can work further through coordinated action and solidarity. The panel highlights initiatives supporting affected communities, particularly women, children, and displaced populations, and also examines how global advocacy can influence international actors, strengthen humanitarian responses and promote a nonviolent path toward des-escalation.


Grand débat (in French):


Video here on Facebook

.


During the debate, I said this as introductory remarks:


Grand Débat sur la paix, le désarmement et l’autodétermination des peuples


Mot introductif de Guy Feugap, Organisateur Africain de World BEYOND


C’est en principe Tord Björk qui devrait être à cette place, afin de s’exprimer en personne au nom de Internatinoal Peace Bureau, une organisation fondée dès 1891, sur cet important débat sur la paix. Mais il n’a pu être là, car il a été refoulé avec plusieurs autres personnes dès son arrivée à Cotonou.


Moi je suis Guy Feugap, Organisateur Africain de World BEYOND War, partenaire de IPB. Je tiens à vous adresser un message, simple, que je partage avec Tord : la jeunesse africaine remportera la lutte pour la liberté pour nous tous !


Dans le cadre de cette préparation au Forum social mondial au Bénin, IPB, World BEYOND War et l’Assemblée sociale mondiale des luttes et des résistances ont coopéré avec le Réseau pour la paix et la justice climatique. Ce réseau, né en Suède, s’étend désormais à travers le continent africain, au Congo et en Afrique de l’Est, parmi les jeunes, en associant la revendication de la paix à celle d’une transition climatique juste.


Au cours de ce processus, nous avons pu organiser plusieurs réunions en ligne avec de nombreux jeunes militants venus de Turquie, du Portugal, de Via Campesina, des syndicats, des mouvements de défense des migrants, des mouvements pour la paix et pour le climat, et bien d’autres encore. Nous avons été particulièrement touchés par le témoignage de Burry Turkana, originaire de Gambie, qui nous a fait part directement depuis la caravane en route du Sénégal vers le Bénin, ainsi que par celui de Jackson Kisangani, originaire de l’est du Congo, l’un des principaux organisateurs du mouvement international pour la paix et la justice climatique, depuis le cœur des zones de guerre où les jeunes se mobilisent pour protéger l’environnement et construire un avenir meilleur sans guerre.


Notre message est désormais clair : nous devons nous unir dans une action commune pour la paix sur Terre et la paix avec la Terre, et pourquoi pas à travers une journée d’action commune internationale en faveur de cette vision qui consiste à rassembler les préoccupations sociales et écologiques au sein d’un appel unifié à la paix. Un appel à la résistance contre le modèle de développement actuel oppressif, qui exploite les êtres humains et la nature et qui est contrôlé par des puissances occidentales de plus en plus racistes. Nous, les peuples de tous les continents, devons nous unir contre ce modèle qui opprime les populations tant dans le Sud que dans le Nord.


Partons de ce moment inspirant à Cotonou pour lancer un mouvement rural et urbain inspiré par la nouvelle dynamique créée par ce Forum social mondial, par les caravanes pour la terre et l’eau, et par la nécessité de décoloniser le monde entier. Un mouvement uni par un appel à la paix sur Terre et à la paix avec la Terre !


Globalisons la lutte et que vive la jeunesse africaine !

author: Novara Media
title: Ex Oil-Engineer Turned Climate Whistleblower: We Face Collapse.
content:
The summer of 2026 will go down in history books as the hottest, driest and most deadly set of heatwaves Britain has ever experienced. This weather isn’t normal – but it is predictable according to a global consensus of scientists. And yet this summer, according to the science, will be one of the coolest summers we ever have again. Things will only get hotter from here.


Beginning his career as an oil-rig engineer before retraining as a climate scientist, Kevin Anderson’s career has been an extraordinary journey. On Downstream this week, Aaron Bastani sat down with him to discuss what has become his life’s work: sounding the alarm on man-made climate change, and on the fossil fuel industry that gave him his start.


Just how much has the planet heated, and why? Is the Paris Agreement’s aim of keeping heating to beneath 1.5°C still achievable, or delusional cope? What are the political obstacles to tackling the issue? Having worked with Andy Burnham in Manchester, what does Kevin think he will do on climate, as PM? Is avoiding catastrophe still possible, and if so, how much time have we got to act, before it’s too late?

author: Mekong Review 2
title: Letter from the mudflats Hai-Dang Phan
content:
Toby creeping up to take a photo of the spoonie. Credit: Hai-Dang Phan


M

ud envelopes my feet, dark and cool, slick with sea. It’s low tide, and the sea has receded to reveal a massive mudflat stretching as far as the eye can see. We are at Tân Thành beach, roughly two hours by car from Saigon, on the coast of Vietnam’s Mekong Delta. It is early January—the dry season in the tropical south—when huge numbers of migratory shorebirds can be found on this expanse.


Following the lead of our guide, Ba and I cautiously navigate the ankle-deep water of a tidal channel. From atop the sea wall a storm-grey heron watches our slow progress. To the north and east, fishing huts perch high on bamboo posts. To the south, giant steel transmission towers dominate the horizon as they march offshore towards rows of wind turbines. On the muddy backshore, fishing boats lie stranded with nowhere to go, outsized eyes painted on their fading prows. They are the same kind of boats that my family used when we fled the country over forty years ago.


We are sloshing across the mudflats this morning because somewhere out there might be a spoon-billed sandpiper, one of the world’s rarest shorebirds and a critically endangered species. A few regular, if elusive, birds are recorded every winter here at

Tân Thành

. Our guide is

Bùi Thành Trung

—or, as he prefers it, Toby. He’s one the best birders in Vietnam, a shorebird specialist with a knack for finding “spoonies”, as he affectionately calls them.


“Stay inside the channel!” Toby shouts, spotting scope balanced over a shoulder. We have about two hours before the tide makes it too dangerous to be wandering the mudflats. We aren’t the only ones making the most of low tide. Further out, dozens of local women are digging for clams.


The watery path leads to the first set of makeshift bamboo “monkey bridges” we’ll need to cross. My seventy-four-year-old father stops in his tracks, considers the 30-metre obstacle course, his old knees, his bad balance, and tells us “kids” to go ahead without him. But Toby has just the pep talk. “You’re still cứng” he says, clenching his fist and smiling—s

till hard

,

still tough

. That’s all it takes; Ba comes along.


There is something simultaneously exhilarating and comforting about being at Tân Thành. There’s no point bothering with footwear because they’ll only get stuck in the mud. Earlier, the act of taking off our shoes before setting foot on the mudflat called to mind the familiar Asian custom before entering a home. We are, after all, guests here in what Toby calls “Spoonyland”.


F

or the past few days, Ba and I have been on a meandering road trip through the Mekong Delta, from Saigon to the river town of

Châu Đốc

 near Cambodia. He wanted to show me some of the places where he was stationed and fought during the war, some fifty years ago, as an officer of a patrol boat unit in the South Vietnamese Navy.


Today, we return to our primary mission: to experience Vietnam through its birds. Whenever we returned to Vietnam in the past, we usually spent all our time visiting family. For once, I wanted to see the country itself. On this matter, Ba and I found common ground. While he’s no avid birdwatcher like me, Ba likes a good challenge and wants to see as much of Vietnam as he still can.


Given the country’s long, distinctive coastline, a trip focused on shorebirds seemed essential, and searching for the spoon-billed sandpiper offered us a chance to do something extraordinary: witness a bird brought back from the brink of extinction. The guide I initially contacted was unavailable, but put me in touch with his friend, Toby. I knew about Toby from eBird, an online platform that birdwatchers the world over use to record and share sightings. Toby was the top “lister” in Vietnam, with 750 species observed—a distinction that filled me with unexpected pride when I first saw his Vietnamese name on top of a leaderboard stacked with Anglo-sounding names.


Toby studied business administration and held a decent desk job for an industrial sales company. Then, one day, a brief encounter with a sunbird ignited his passion for birds. More than ten years later, Toby has explored nearly every province in Vietnam on a quest to photograph every bird species in the country.


R

eaching the sandbar peninsula, we catch our first glimpse of the shorebirds. I can’t make most of them out; they are only shapes flying back and forth. The birds are everywhere, in …

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Experts challenge gov’t claims on Pax Silica
content:
The AI-assisted illustration of the proposed 1,600-hectare industrial hub to be located in New Clark City in Capas, Tarlac. Photo courtesy of the People’s Television Network

Pax Silica follows a pattern in which developing countries bear the environmental and social costs of technologies that largely benefit wealthier economies.

CABUYAO CITY, Laguna — Engineers and information technology professionals critical of the proposed Pax Silica data center and artificial intelligence (AI) hub said that the Marcos Jr. administration is making promises that fail to address the project’s social and environmental impact.

In a statement released on Aug. 4, Pro-people Engineers and Leaders (PROPEL) and the Computer Professionals’ Union (CPU) disputed recent remarks by Information and Communications Technology Secretary Henry Aguda defending the controversial project planned for New Clark City.

The groups said that government agencies have repeatedly introduced “technofixes” in response to concerns over water use, energy demand, and land conversion. They stressed that these measures only reveal the project’s weak planning and foreign-oriented character.

“It’s clear that in the face of the consistent opposition to the Pax Silica project, the different departments of the administration are throwing one technofix after another that will supposedly solve all the problems related to the project,” the groups said in a statement. “At best, it reveals how poorly conceived the project is from the beginning; at worst, it exposes the lengths at which the Marcos Jr. administration is willing to go just to cater to the economic agenda of another country.”

PROPEL challenged government assurances that advanced cooling technologies could minimize water use in the proposed AI facilities.

The group observed that some hyperscale data centers abroad have promoted closed-loop cooling systems that recycle water but stressed that such systems require large amounts of electricity. Desalination, another option reportedly being considered, would also consume substantial energy and require additional infrastructure along the Zambales coast or Manila Bay.

Engineers warned that cooling requirements in the Philippines could be significantly higher than in temperate countries because of tropical heat, with temperatures reaching 40°C in some areas.

“With all the lack of transparency behind the project, and all the sudden promises that they can address the water problem, we can only expect what communities in the US are already experiencing around data centers, unusable tap water, water shortages, and other disruptions,” the statement said.

The warning echoes growing international criticism of large AI facilities which have been linked to heavy water consumption and local resource conflicts in several parts of the United States.

The groups also questioned the projected electricity demand, citing BCDA estimates of three to five gigawatts.

According to PROPEL, meeting such demand through solar power could require thousands of additional hectares of land. The statement also raised concerns over the possible use of off-grid fossil fuel plants and generators, practices already documented in some overseas data center complexes.

The engineers said that government discussions of nuclear energy as a possible long-term power source introduce further technical, financial, and social issues that have not been publicly debated.

“The massive projected demand for electricity will only lead to even more land being ceded to the project,” the group said.

CPU said that government comparisons with existing local data centers are misleading because Pax Silica is designed primarily for AI development and training, requiring far greater computing power.

CPU chairperson Ian Aragoza said that newer Philippine hyperscale facilities consume less than 100 megawatts each, while the DICT itself has projected at least 400 megawatts of data center consumption in New Clark City.

“This means we can’t simply rely on old studies and past experiences,” the statement said. “Pax Silica is trying to introduce something new altogether.”

The group said AI-focused facilities differ substantially from conventional cloud and enterprise data centers, making previous impact assessments insufficient.

The groups said that Pax Silica follows a pattern in which developing countries bear the environmental and social costs of technologies that largely benefit wealthier economies.

title: Miembros de la comunidad Antonio Panitrur quedan en libertad y denuncian persecución política por su lucha contra empresas forestales y latifundistas de la zona
content:
«Comunicado Público Mapuche


1.- La comunidad Mapuche Antonio Panitrur, de la zona del bajo Malleko, venimos a manifestar nuestro profundo rechazo a la detención arbitraria y violenta del werken Adan Huentecol Neculpan y el peñi Dagoberto Soto Neculpan, quienes mediante un fuerte y desmedido contingente llegaron hasta la comunidad, mientras trabajaban en la reparación de un puente al ingreso de la comunidad.


La persecución política contra el Werken Adan Huentecol Neculpan y el peñi Dagoberto Soto Neculpan es de larga data, ya que en los últimos 10 años, han sido permanentemente amedrentados y reprimidos, cómo consecuencia de su digna constancia del proceso de reivindicación territorial que nuestra comunidad Antonio Panitrur a mantenido contra las empresas forestales y los latifundistas de la zona. Cuyo proceso nos ha costado la difamación pública de nuestra legitima lucha y la criminalización sesgada y racista.


2.- En lo particular la situación del werken Andan Huentecol tuvo que sortear denuncias punitivas de empresarios forestales y acusaciones públicas de la actual diputada Gloria Naveillan, quien en su afán de lucrar políticamente, ha utilizado la legítima causa Mapuche como trampolín político. Este personaje nefasto ha patrocinado constantemente un clima de confrontación y odio contra el pueblo Mapuche.


3.- Cabe mencionar que ambos peñi el día de hoy han quedado en libertad y han regresado a su comunidad junto a sus familiares. Los supuestos delitos que afrontan son «maltrato a la autoridad y usurpación» acusaciones que desestimamos por tratarse de acusaciones falsas y alejadas completamente de cómo sucedieron los hechos. Los peñi, fueron golpeados brutalmente en reiteradas ocasiones y en primera instancia por más 6 personas de civil, y que no se identificaron como carabineros.


Esta situación generó que los peñi, a pesar de estar en desventaja, tuvieron que defenderse. Pero que tras ser superados en números, fueron golpeados y sometidos a puntas de patadas en todo el cuerpo. La golpiza se detuvo solo cuando un furgón escolar apareció en el lugar. Recién en ese momento los civiles se identificaron como carabineros.


Cuya situación de abuso y violencia desmedida el tribunal ordenó una segunda constatación de lesiones basándose en el protocolo de interculturalidad en el hospital de Collipulli.


4.- Finalmente señalar que estos hechos de violencia contra nuestra gente, no nos van a amedrentar y afirmar que estas arremetidas racistas no son más que una demostración de odio y persecución política, amparado en un procedimiento judicial de facto contra nuestra comunidad. Pero vamos a permanecer en el camino de nuestra lucha por la restitución de nuestro territorio usurpado por el Estado Chileno.


Manifestar que estamos plenamente agradecidos, del acompañamiento de distintas comunidades Mapuche de zona Malleco, que nos han respaldado hoy de forma presencial frente al tribunal de collipulli.


-Libertad a los prisioneros políticos Mapuche


-Fuerza a los distintos y dignos procesos de recuperación territorial Mapuche.


-Fuera las empresas forestales del territorio Mapuche.


-De frente contra la represión política, del racista gobierno de Chile.


Comunica: Comunidad Mapuche Antonio Panitrur.


Wallmapu: Antonio Panitrur, 08 de agosto de 2026″.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Filipino journalists’ participation in Israel-funded trip draws criticism
content:
Several Filipino journalists pose for a group photo after they arrive in Israel for a special media delegation. Photo from Israel in the Philippines' Facebook page

“Far from being benign, trips sponsored by Israel are designed to bury the truth and whitewash reportage of the ongoing genocide against the Palestinian people.”

CAGAYAN DE ORO — “Accepting sponsored trips from those accused of committing genocide is downright unethical.”

The National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) issued this statement following the recent trip of several Filipino journalists to Israel, a country accused of committing genocide against Palestinians based on the findings by the United Nations (UN) Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel.

The Israel-funded trip reportedly served as an opportunity for the journalists to experience Israel “beyond the headlines.” For NUJP, participating in Israel-funded trips gives an avenue for the said country to justify violations of International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and infringes the principles of justice and humanity in journalism.

“Far from being benign, trips sponsored by Israel are designed to bury the truth and whitewash reportage of the ongoing genocide against the Palestinian people,” the journalists’ group said in a statement, urging its colleagues to reject Israel-sponsored trips.

As of June 2026, 209 journalists and media workers have been killed since Israel intensified attacks in Palestine in October 2023, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ).

Meanwhile, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), citing the numbers provided by Gaza’s Ministry of Health and Israeli authorities, reported that more than 72,000 Palestinians were allegedly killed from October 7, 2023 to May 6, 2026.

NUJP cited a part of its Ethical Guide for Filipino Journalists published in 2021 pertaining to media junket, where it says that “journalists may not accept an invitation to a media junket or an all-expense paid trip where there is no work involved or the purpose is only to get on their good side with expectation of positive coverage in the future, or to establish a friendship with the host.”

In a statement, The Philippine Business and News’s Monsi Alfonso Serrano who was among the participants said that their participation does not equate to surrendering their editorial independence.

For its part, the Filipino Freelance Journalists’ Guild (FFJ) asked, “How independent can reporting be when it is sponsored by a government with a direct stake in the story? What stories get told, and whose voices get amplified, when access comes with an agenda attached?”

FFJ said that grants and fellowships are common practice in the media community which makes reporting, especially for freelance journalists, possible. However, it urged journalists and media workers to “draw the line” at opportunities coming from a country that is facing allegations of genocide.

Last year, several Filipino journalists were also invited by the Embassy of Israel in Manila to visit the country with the same objective.

For the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association, to engage in such trips funded by a country accused of committing genocide is “complicity, both moral and intellectual.” (DAA)

Disclosure: Bulatlat editor-in-chief Ronalyn Olea is the secretary-general of the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines.

author: M.P
title: Osorno: Lof Winkul Kusra busca ejercer su derecho a debida defensa
content:
Con fecha 3 de agosto, y ante la audiencia realizada en el Juzgado de Chawrakawin, Osorno, el Lof Winkul Kusra de San Juan de la Costa, emitió una declaración pública, que replicamos a continuación. Además, convocan para audiencia para el día miércoles 19 de agosto, en el mismo tribunal.

Les informamos a ustedes el resultado de la audiencia sostenida en el juzgado de garantía de Osorno, donde a través del abogado de la defensoría penal indígena, solicitamos al juez la formalización de cargos por parte de la fiscalía, para que como Lof podamos ejercer nuestro derecho a defensa y prepararnos adecuadamente para el proceso judicial que se lleva adelante en contra nuestra, ya que se nos acusa de varios delitos graves, como homicidio frustrado, tenencia ilegal de armas, organización delictiva, robo de maderas, entre otras. Causa que se lleva adelante desde que hicimos ingreso al fundo Santa Herminia en diciembre de 2022.

Recordemos que, fuimos allanandos violentamente el 18 de diciembre de 2024, por una orden de la fiscalía, destruyendo pu sruka y enceres, esposados y amenazando con armas a las personas pertenecientes a nuestro lof, en su mayoría ancianos y niños, requisándonos teléfonos y computadores, que no se nos han sido devueltos en su totalidad desde entonces.

Finalmente esto fue desestimado por el juez, por lo que se rechazó la formalización, en cuanto que, no hay plazo para término de la investigación y que no se han vulnerado ningún derecho a quienes hacemos la solicitud.

Por otro lado, el juez dictaminó una nueva audiencia para que sean devueltas las pertenencias requizadas faltantes, para el día 19 de agosto a las 11.00 am en el mismo tribunal. Por lo que hacemos un llamado a acompañarnos nuevamente y agradecemos a quienes estuvieron presentes hoy de distintos territorios, entregando su küme newen.

title: উচ্ছেদের মুখে দাঁড়িয়ে প্রতিরোধের প্রাচীর তুলছেন ঢাকুরিয়ার বস্তির বাসিন্দারা
content:
দক্ষিণ কলকাতার ঢাকুরিয়া ব্রিজের নীচের বস্তির বাসিন্দাদের। গত ১২ দিন ধরে তারা উচ্ছেদ নোটিসের বিরূদ্ধে আইনি ও সামাজিক প্রতিরোধ গড়ে তুলেছেন। মাথার ওপর ছাদ হারানোর আশঙ্কা নিয়ে তাঁরা এক অনিশ্চিত ভবিষ্যতের সামনে এসে দাঁড়িয়েছেন।


 


সুদর্শনা চক্রবর্তীর

প্রতিবেদন


 


“বিজেপি-কে ভোট দিয়েছিলাম তো আমরা সবাই। কিন্তু তারাই বুলডোজার চালাবে আমাদের ঘরে বুঝতে পারিনি।”


 


“আমাদের দেশের বাড়ি তো অনেক দূর, সেই পাথরপ্রতিমা। ওখান থেকে কাজে আসব কী করে! তাই তো এখানে ঘর করে থাকি।”


 


“আমরাই তো খেটে খাই। বেশির ভাগ বাড়ির ছেলেরা তো তেমন কাজ করে না। না খাটলে খাব কি? এখন তো টেনশনে রাতের ঘুম চলে গেছে।”


 


“বাবুর বাড়িতে বলছে, তোমরা গরীব মানুষ, কী করবে! তোমরা চলে গেলে আমাদের অসুবিধা হবে। তোমরা আসো বলে আমাদের ঘর পরিষ্কার হয়, রান্না হয় তোমাদের জন্যই তো চলে আমাদের। সরকারকে বলো তোমাদের এখানে একটা জায়গা দিতে, যাতে আমাদের বাড়িতে কাজে আসতে পারো।”


  


প্রায় ৩০০ জন মানুষ গৃহহীন হওয়ার আশঙ্কায় রাত কাটাচ্ছেন। ৪৩টি পরিবার। কারোওর জন্ম বেড়ে ওঠা এখানেই, কারোর পাশের জেলাতেই বাড়ি থাকলেও কাজের জন্য এখানেই রয়ে গেছেন বছরের পর বছর। দূর থেকে কোলকাতা এসে কাজ করা সম্ভব নয় এই শ্রমজীবী মানুষদের। আর তাঁদের মধ্যে অধিকাংশ শ্রমজীবীই মহিলা। দুশ্চিন্তা তাঁদেরই সবচেয়ে বেশি। তাই প্রতিবাদে, প্রতিরোধে পথে নেমেছেন, অবস্থাবন করছেন তাঁরাই।


 


রত্না পড়ুয়া বলছিলেন,


“এত টেনশন, চাপের মধ্যে আছি যে কিছুই মনে থাকছে না। আমরা মেয়েরা বাবুদের বাড়ি কাজ করে এসে এখানে বসছি। আমরা আশা রাখছি ১০ তারিখ একটা সুখবর পাব। প্রশাসন তো আমাদের সঙ্গে থাকছে না। এত দিদিরা, সংগঠন আমাদের পাশে এসে দাঁড়াচ্ছেন, ভালো কিছু হবে না, বলুন?”


এই চিত্র দক্ষিণ কলকাতার ঢাকুরিয়া ব্রিজের নীচের ৩২ নম্বর পঞ্চানন তলা বস্তির বাসিন্দাদের। গত ১২ দিন ধরে তারা রাজ্য সরকারের কাছ থেকে প্রাপ্ত উচ্ছেদ নোটিসের বিরূদ্ধে প্রতিরোধে আইনি ও সামাজিক প্রতিরোধ গড়ে তুলেছেন। বহু অনুরোধ ও চেষ্টা সত্ত্বেও দেখা হয়নি নগর উন্নয়ন দপ্তরের ভারপ্রাপ্ত মন্ত্রী অগ্নিমিত্রা পাল, এলাকার বিধায়ক স্বপন দাশগুপ্ত কারোর সঙ্গেই। কলকাতা কর্পোরেশন-এর মেয়র পদত্যাগ করায় এই মুহূর্তে সরকারিভাবে সেখান থেকেও কোনোও সহায়তা মেলেনি। এই পরিস্থিতিতে জোটবদ্ধ আন্দোলন ও বিভিন্ন শ্রমজীবী সংগঠনের মঞ্চ যোগদানের ফলেই উচ্ছেদ রোখার চেষ্টা করছেন এই বস্তির বাসিন্দারা। এর পাশাপাশি হাইকোর্টে মামলাও দায়ের করেছেন। যার রায় বেরোনো ১০ অগাস্ট।


 


 


৩৫ বছর এই বস্তিতে রয়েছেন হীরা কয়াল। আচমকা এই নোটিস পেয়ে বিপর্যস্ত হয়ে পড়েছেন,


“আমরা তো ভয় পাচ্ছি, আমরা কোথায় চলে গিয়ে কী করব! আমাদের কোনোও জায়গা নেই, ঠাঁই নেই। কোনোও সামর্থ্য নেই যে কোথাও গিয়ে ভাড়া বাড়িতে থাকব। সেখানে ৫০০০ টাকা ভাড়া, ১০০০০ টাকা ডিপজিট। কোথা থেকে দেব? আমাদের স্বামীরা সেভাবে খাটতে পারে না। আমরা খাটতে পারলে, লোকের বাড়ি কাজ করতে পারলে খায়। আমরা ১০০০০ টাকা মাইনেই পাই হয়তো কোনো রকমে। আমাদের তুলে দিয়ে কোথায় গিয়ে থাকব? ১০ তারিখ কী রায় দেবে তাই নিয়ে খুব টেনশন হচ্ছে মাথার ভেতর। যবে থেকে নোটিস এসেছে আমাদের ঘুম নেই, খাওয়া নেই, বাড়িতে সবাই ভয়ে শুকিয়ে যাচ্ছে। নতুন সরকারের কাছে এমন আশা করিনি। সবাই ভেবেছিলাম দেখা যাক এই সরকার এসে আমাদের কী হেল্প করে। কিন্তু আসামাত্রই যে এভাবে ঝাঁটা মারবে বুঝতে পারিনি।”


এই বস্তির বাসিন্দাদের সকলেই বলছেন, কেউই বুঝতে পারেননি, আচমকা এভাবে তুলে দেওয়ার খবর আসতে পারে। পাশের দক্ষিণ ২৪ পরগণা জেলার প্রত্যন্ত গ্রামে, সুন্দরবনে বসত থাকলেও, সেখান থেকে প্রতিদিন কাজে আসা তাঁদের পক্ষে সম্ভবই নয়।


 


এই বস্তিতে যাঁরা থাকেন তাঁদের মধ্যে বেশিরভাগ মহিলাই সংলগ্ন এলাকায় গৃহ পরিচারিকার কাজ করেন এবং সেই সূত্রে পশ্চিমবঙ্গ গৃহ পরিচারিকা সমিতির সদস্য। তাঁরা যোগাযোগ করায় এই সমিতি উচ্ছেদ বিরোধী আন্দোলনে সক্রিয় ভূমিকা নিয়েছে। এই উচ্ছেদের বিরোধীতায় আন্দোলনের সঙ্গে রয়েছেন সমিতির নেত্রী স্বপ্না ত্রিপাঠি।


 


যেভাবে এই উচ্ছেদ প্রক্রিয়া শুরু হয়, আন্দোলন শুরু হয়ে এগোচ্ছে তা অনেকটা এইরকম –


 


গত ২৭ জুন প্রথম ৩২ নম্বর পঞ্চানন তলা বস্তিতে উচ্ছেদের নোটিস পাঠানো হয়। তার আগে ঢাকুরিয়া ব্রিজের তলার দুই দিকে ৯০ ও ৯২ নম্বর ওয়ার্ডে কর্পোরেশন থেকে এনকোয়ারি, ছবি তোলা, তালিকা তৈরি করা হয়। নোটিস পাওয়র পর সদস্যরা সমিতির সঙ্গে যোগাযোগ করেন। আলোচনার পর সর্বসম্মতিক্রমে সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া হয় যে আন্দোলনের পথেই হাঁটা হবে। ইতিমিধ্যে ২৭ জুনের নোটিস বস্তিতে সার্ভ করা হয় ২৯ জুন। বলা হয় ৩ জুলাইয়ের মধ্যে তাঁদের উঠে যেতে হবে।


 


এরপরেই তাঁরা দেখা করেন বোরো ৮-এর এক্সিকিউটিভ ইঞ্চিনিয়ার-এর সঙ্গে। তিনি সরাসরি জানান কলকাতা কমিশনার-এর কাছ থেকে নির্দেশ আসায় কিছুই করার নেই। কমিশনারের সঙ্গে তাঁরা দেখা করতে পারেননি। এলাকার চেয়ারম্যান ও কাউন্সিলার-এর সঙ্গেও তাঁদের দেখা হয়নি যেহেতু মেয়র-এর পদত্যাগের পর এই পদ্গুলি নিষ্ক্রিয় হয়ে পড়েছে। পদাধিকারী কারোওর সঙ্গে দেখা না হওয়ায় এরপরেই তাঁরা সিদ্ধান্ত নেন কোর্টে যাওয়ার ও ১ তারিখ কোর্টে যান।


 


তাঁদের উদ্দেশ্য ছিল যাতে ৩ তারিখের উচ্ছেদ আটকানো যায়। যদিও তাঁরা ১ তারিখ ডেট পাননি, ২ তারিখ লিস্টেড হলেও সেদিন তাঁদের শুনানি হয়নি। এরপরেই তাঁদের তরফে আইনজীবী পুলিস কমিশনার, কলকাতা কর্পোরেশন-এর কমিশনার, বোরো ৮-এর এক্সিকিউটিভ …

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Balik-Tanaw | Manatili sa katuruan ni Hesus
content:
1 Kings 19:9a, 11-13a Psalm 85:9, 10, 11-12, 13-14 Romans 9:1-5 Matthew 14:22-33

Noong State of the Nation Address (SONA), nagkaroon ako ng pagkakataong makinig kasama ang isang pamilyang naging kaibigan ko sa Payatas. Nasa gitna ng kanilang munting tahanan ang telebisyon—isang espasyong nagsisilbing sala, silid-tulugan, at lugar ng kanilang maliit na kabuhayan. Habang nagsasalita ang Pangulo, hindi lamang ang kanyang mga salita ang aking pinakikinggan; higit kong pinagmamasdan ang katahimikan at mga reaksyon ng pamilyang iyon. Gusto kong maramdaman kung paano tumatagos sa kanilang buhay ang mga ipinapangakong pagbabago.

Habang tumatagal ang SONA, tila maraming multo ang lumilitaw. Mga multo ng katiwalian, korapsyon, kahirapan, kawalang-katarungan, at pagkakahati-hati. Marahil nakakatakot ang mga multong ito sapagkat marami sa mga ipinagmamalaking hakbang ay hindi pa rin tunay na nararamdaman ng mga mahihirap. Ang ating bansa ay tila nasa gitna ng mga multong ito. Ngunit bilang mga Kristiyano, ang paanyaya ay hindi lamang ang manatiling nananalig kay Kristo kundi ang maging mukha ni Kristo sa gitna ng mga ito—ang patuloy na makita ang Diyos sa gitna ng nagbabanggaang kapangyarihan at manatiling umaasa kahit sa gitna ng matinding pagkadismaya.

Pagkatapos ng SONA, napatahimik kaming lahat. Walang nagsalita. Ang katahimikang iyon ang nagpaalala sa akin ng unang pagbasa. Hindi natagpuan ni Propeta Elias ang Diyos sa malakas na hangin, sa lindol, o sa apoy. Natagpuan niya ang Diyos sa banayad na tinig ng katahimikan.

Marahil ganoon din ngayon. Hindi natin laging matatagpuan ang Diyos sa malalakas na talumpati, sa ingay ng politika, o sa sigawan ng mga makapangyarihan. Naroroon Siya sa katahimikan ng mga dukhang naghahanap ng sagot sa kanilang mga tanong. Naroroon Siya sa buntong-hininga ng mga magulang na nag-iisip kung saan kukuha ng pagkain kinabukasan. Naroroon Siya sa mga pusong marunong huminto, magnilay, at makaramdam ng sakit ng lipunan habang patuloy na naghahangad ng tunay na pagbabago.

Ito rin ang dahilan kung bakit dinudumog si Hesus sa Ebanghelyo. Nauunawaan Niya ang hikbi ng mga dukha at ang kanilang pananabik sa isang makatarungang bukas. Hindi lamang Niya sila binigyan ng pahinga at kapayapaan; ginising din Niya ang kanilang kamalayan. Tinuruan Niya silang mangarap at makibahagi sa pagtatayo ng isang lipunang mas makatarungan at mas makatao.

Matapos ang katahimikan ng SONA, isa-isang lumabas ang aming mga saloobin. Marami ang nadismaya. Mahirap ngang hindi madismaya, lalo na’t ang ating bansa ay nahaharap sa iba’t ibang krisis—ang mga epekto ng digmaan sa Gitnang Silangan, mga usaping pampulitika tulad ng impeachment, patuloy na korapsyon, at lumalalim na pagkakahati-hati ng lipunan. Sa gitna ng lahat ng ito, ang higit na naaapektuhan ay ang mga mahihirap.

Sa ikalawang pagbasa, ipinakita ni San Pablo ang kanyang matinding dalamhati para sa kanyang mga kababayan. Nadismaya siya, ngunit hindi siya nagpadaig sa pagkadismaya. Nanatili siyang nakaugat kay Kristo. Iyan ang paalala sa atin: ang pagkadismaya ay hindi dapat maging dahilan upang tayo’y manahimik o mawalan ng pag-asa. Sa halip, dapat itong maging hamon upang lalo nating samahan ang mga pamayanan, gisingin ang kanilang kamalayan, at tulungan silang huwag malinlang ng mga huwad na pangako. Sa panahong laganap ang kahirapan at kawalang-katarungan, napakadaling piliin ang pananahimik at kawalang-kibo.

Kung ayaw nating habang-buhay na mabuhay sa takot sa mga multo ng ating lipunan, kailangan nating manatili kay Hesus. Siya ang nagtagumpay laban sa kasamaan, sa kawalang-katarungan, at maging sa kamatayan. Siya ang ating lakas upang huwag magpalamon sa takot at pagkadismaya, kundi maging mga saksi ng pag-asa, katarungan, at kapayapaan sa gitna ng mundong puno pa rin ng mga multo.

Balik-Tanaw is a group blog of Promotion of Church People’s Response. The Lectionary Gospel reflection is an invitation for meditation, contemplation, and action. As we nurture our faith by committing ourselves to journey with the people, we also wish to nourish the perspective coming from the point of view of hope and struggle of the people. It is our constant longing that even as crisis intensifies, the faithful will continue to strengthen their commitment to love God and our neighbor by being one with the people in their dreams and aspirations. author: Mat
title: Tierra, vivienda y bienes comunes: los derechos mínimos para una vida digna que el Congreso y el Gobierno quieren saquear
content:
Pese a la lluvia, y los intentos del Gobierno por desinflar la protesta, miles y miles de personas colmaron las calles para decirle no a una ley de entrega. La presión de la jornada popular, que se realizó con carácter federal en todo el país,

title: SES Malatya Şubesi: Sağlık emekçileri tükenme noktasında
content:
Fotoğraf: Alberto Giuliani/Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

SES Malatya Şubesi, İnönü Üniversitesi Turgut Özal Tıp Merkezindeki sağlık emekçilerinin ağır çalışma koşullarına dair Eğitim Sen Malatya il binasında basın toplantısı düzenledi. Topantıda açıklamayı SES Malatya Şube Eş Başkanı Cansu Kaplan okudu.

Sağlık emekçilerinin deprem, kovid-19 pandemisi ve yıllardır ağırlaşan çalışma koşullarının yükü altında tükenme noktasına geldiğini ifade eden Kaplan, "Personel eksikliği, artan iş yükü, yoğun nöbetler, düşük ek ödemeler ve ekonomik kayıplar sağlık emekçilerinin hem çalışma hem de yaşam koşullarını ağırlaştırmaktadır" dedi.

Yeni personel alımının bu sorunların tek başına çözümü olmadığını dile getiren Kaplan, "Sağlık emekçisinin emeğini değersizleştiren, çalışanı yoksulluğa mahkum eden ve tükenmişliği artıran çalışma koşulları değiştirilmelidir" diye konuştu.

Kaplan, "Performans, teşvik ve ek ödeme gibi parçalı ve emekliliğe yansımayan ücret politikası yerine yoksulluk sınırının üzerinde, emekliliğe yansıyan, güvenceli ve tek kalemde ödenen bir ücret istiyoruz" dedi.

Sağlık kurumlarının baskının, korkunun ve mobbingin değil saygının, diyaloğun, dayanışmanın ve demokratik katılımın bulunduğu alanlar olması gerektiğini söyleyen Kaplan, "Çalışanların ve sendikaların sözünün dinlendiği, sorunların birlikte konuşulduğu ve çözümün ortak akılla üretildiği bir çalışma düzeni istiyoruz" çağrısında bulundu.

SES Malatya Şubesi olarak sağlık emekçilerinin sorunlarını ve çözüm önerilerini konuşmak adına sendikal görüşme talebinde bulunduklarını ancak yanıt alamadıklarını dile getiren Kaplan, taleplerini ise şu şekilde sıraladı:

Yoksulluk sınırının üzerinde, emekliliğe yansıyan, tek kalemde ve güvenceli maaş istiyoruz.

Yeterli ve güvenceli personel istiyoruz.

İş yükünün ve nöbetlerin azaltılmasını istiyoruz.

Çalışma saatlerinin insan onuruna uygun düzenlenmesini istiyoruz.

Performansa dayalı parçalı ücretlendirmeye son verilmesini istiyoruz.

Deprem ve pandemi dönemlerinden bu yana çalışan sağlık emekçilerinin tükenmişliğinin dikkate alınmasını istiyoruz.

Mobbing ve baskının olmadığı, demokratik, güvenli ve barışçıl bir çalışma ortamı istiyoruz.

Sendikaların ve çalışan temsilcilerinin karar süreçlerine katılımının sağlanmasını istiyoruz.

Sndikal görüşmenin gerçekleştirilmesini istiyoruz.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Katheryn Houghton
title: Medicaid Work Requirements Leave Unhoused People Out in the Cold
content:
“You can’t really worry about getting paperwork done when you don’t know where you’re eating today,” said one advocate.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation .

MISSOULA, Mont. — Tywon Pugh has seizures that make it hard to find and keep a job.

“They called me a ‘liability to the job site,’” Pugh said, recalling the words of his manager when a seizure cost him his last job at a fast-food restaurant in this western Montana city.

When the 46-year-old lost work in the past, his wife of 10 years covered their rent and he tended to their home until he found another job. But his wife died last year. Soon after, Pugh became homeless. His problem with alcohol became worse, which made managing his seizures more difficult.

“When she died, my whole base was depleted,” Pugh said.

Medicaid pays for the prescriptions that keep Pugh’s seizures at bay. The government-subsidized health coverage would also pay for an addiction treatment program that Pugh said he has tried to get into, but he was told there’s a waitlist.

Pugh’s goal has been to get healthy enough to work again. But he’s worried about being able to keep the Medicaid coverage he needs to get to that point.

In the spring, the federal government finalized regulations requiring millions of people who receive Medicaid benefits to prove they’re working, volunteering, or going to school to keep their coverage. States have until January to begin those checks. Montana, Arkansas, and Nebraska have already started implementing them.

The Trump administration’s federal work requirements exempt certain groups of people: those with disabilities, those older than 64, pregnant people and Native Americans, among others. To receive an exemption, anyone without a clear-cut qualification — such as through their age or disability status — will have to prove they’re too sick to work.

But the administration decided that being homeless isn’t a medical condition and can’t count as an automatic out from having to meet the new requirements. Many conservative policymakers support work requirements, and some states have attempted to implement such rules for years. At least four states — Montana, Arizona, Kentucky, and Utah — previously proposed policies that included homelessness as an exemption.

But federal officials have said that’s not allowed. In an email to KFF Health News , the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services declined to provide a comment on the record. But the agency confirmed that states must stick to the federal government’s list of exemptions. Homelessness in the U.S. increased by 27% from 2013 to 2025, according to data from the Department of Housing and Urban Development. Last year, about 746,000 people were homeless .

Many, like Pugh, qualified for Medicaid, though the number of enrollees who are homeless is difficult to measure. In 2023, 55% of patients who received medical or behavioral health services through one of the nation’s roughly 300 Health Care for the Homeless programs were enrolled in Medicaid.

Jennifer Tolbert, deputy director of KFF’s Program on Medicaid and the Uninsured, said the federal regulations are a lot stricter than many states had expected, even those on board with work requirements. (KFF is a health information nonprofit that includes KFF Health News .)

“It took everyone by surprise,” Tolbert said.

Mehmet Oz, who leads CMS, touted the regulations as a “path to prosperity” during a press conference in June.

“We need to get people to try to work,” Oz said. In June, 25 mostly Democratic-led states sued the Trump administration over the regulations, arguing the medical frailty standard would be too hard for enrollees to meet — and for states to assess. The work requirements are projected to increase the number of uninsured people nationwide by more than 5 million by 2034, according to the Congressional Budget Office.

Most states will begin to implement the Medicaid work requirements in January.

Montana plans to begin booting Medicaid enrollees from coverage this October if they can’t prove they’re in compliance with the work requirement.

“My Medicaid is still active, but when are they gonna cut that off from me?” Pugh said. “I can’t get employed. How am I supposed to survive?”

The differences between the states’ and federal government’s exemption lists don’t end with people who are homeless. In Montana, lawmakers also …

title: Free but out of reach? The long wait for public mental health services
content:
Jem Curtny Narboneta, a BS psychology student, participates in the poster-making contest during Psychology Week celebration. Photo courtesy of Jem Curtny Narboneta.

“The biological aspect includes medicines and genetics,” Del Valle said. “But psychosocial factors—the social determinants of health—also affect us. If we improve education, if people have jobs, and communities can support them, these all contribute to mental health.”

Trigger warning: Mentions of suicide

By Kasheena Camacho Bulatlat.com

MANILA —  For Filipinos experiencing mental health crises, long waiting periods for free mental health consultations continue to hinder their access to care, forcing some of them to seek costly private treatment.

For March Lavela, 24, deciding to seek professional help came after months of grief, mounting family responsibilities, and worsening panic attacks. “The turning point for me was when the pressure built up so much that my body couldn’t handle it anymore,” Lavela said.

He said the panic attacks began during online thesis classes, where repeated confrontations with a professor became overwhelming. The anxiety persisted even outside the classroom, with merely hearing the professor’s name triggering panic.

“I knew it was time to ask for help when I started thinking about death and killing myself,” he said. “…[R]ealizing my mind was going to that dark place made me see that I couldn’t fight this on my own anymore.”

Unable to afford private psychiatric consultations, Lavela sought free mental health services. He booked consultations with both the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) and the National Center for Mental Health (NCMH). The available schedules, however, were months away.

“I decided to just walk in at NCMH because I knew I couldn’t wait for a far-off online appointment date,” he said. “I felt like if I waited that long, I might already be gone.”

At the NCMH, he disclosed to hospital personnel that he had been experiencing suicidal thoughts. “They assisted me through the whole process once I walked into the hospital,” he said.

Lavela’s experience mirrors a broader challenge confronting the country’s mental healthcare system.

Jem Curtny B. Narboneta, 21, also agonized over the waiting period to access care.

Narboneta, a psychology student, said she initially spent around P11,000 ($181) on several online psychological consultation platforms in search of answers.

She also contacted around 15 to 20 emergency hotlines she found online but said none responded.

Her mother later accompanied her to NCMH for free consultation. Instead of receiving immediate care, they were advised to secure an online appointment. Narboneta said the earliest available schedule was nearly a year away.

“Obviously I couldn’t wait that long because I’d be long gone if I were to wait a year,” she said.

Unable to wait, she then sought consultation with a private psychiatric facility despite the additional cost.

“It greatly affected my well-being because I needed mental health consultation that time,” she said. “To find out I had to wait a year made me think of all the people who finally mustered the courage to seek help only to discover mental health services weren’t as accessible as they thought.”

Lavela and Narboneta are among the thousands of Filipinos seeking professional mental health services in the past years.

In an online interview with Bulatlat , Dr. Teresa Rosalie D. del Valle, a medical specialist IV at the NCMH, said that consultations have increased significantly in recent years.

“The pandemic heightened public awareness of mental health,” Del Valle said.

The increase in demand, however, has outpaced the country’s available mental health workforce, according to both Del Valle and international data.

According to the World Health Organization’s Mental Health Atlas 2024 , the Philippines has only 3.9 mental health workers for every 100,000 population, including 0.2 psychiatrists, 0.3 psychologists, 0.7 mental health nurses, 1.1 social workers, and 1.6 other mental health workers per 100,000 population.

The report also recorded one specialized mental hospital, 22 psychiatric units in general hospitals, and 1,362 community-based outpatient mental health facilities nationwide.

Del Valle said the current number of psychiatrists remains insufficient to keep up with the growing number of patients seeking care.

author: DisabilityARK
title: England V Disability
content:
Disabled people in the United Kingdom (UK) have endured relentless


attacks on their rights and opportunities on multiple fronts. Many


hard-won freedoms have been steadily rolled back in recent years.


This document summarises some of these policies that have either


been proposed or successfully enacted. Disabled people are often


used as the testing ground for future policies, so being aware of what


is happening to them has broader implications for the rights of other


groups. During the Holocaust, many of the procedures developed on


disabled people were later applied to wider populations. More recent


examples include bank account surveillance systems, which are laying


the groundwork for more extensive population-wide surveillance.


Following the 2008 financial crash, attacks on disabled people’s rights


intensified. In 2016, the United Nations (UN) found that the UK was


engaged in “grave and systematic” violations of disabled people’s


rights, and linked these actions to a significant number of excess


deaths. In 2024, the UN follow-up report to the inquiry declared that


the UK made “no significant progress” on implementing the inquiry’s


recommendations regarding independent living, social security, and


an adequate standard of living. Now, in 2026, things have only gotten


worse. This zine cannot adequately cover every front of attack or the


rapid changes currently taking place, but it aims to provide a broad


snapshot of the situation in England in the Summer of 2026.
