title: Bakırhan: The foundational law is the first step toward including the Kurds into the law
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan spoke on the draft law titled “Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” currently being debated in the General Assembly of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM).


‘Historic transition’


Bakırhan began his speech by commemorating the political prisoners in Turkey, the peoples of Turkey, and Sırrı Süreyya Önder, a member of the DEM Party İmralı Delegation who passed away while receiving medical treatment last year. He said that the century-old Kurdish question was moving from the shadow of conflict onto the ground of law.


“We are witnessing this historic transition here today. The draft law before us is a compass pointing the country toward a new direction. The institution that will guide us along this path is the Grand National Assembly of Turkey,” he said.


‘A historical knot is finally beginning to be untied’


Recalling that the Kurdish question was governed through a martial law mentality during the early years of the Republic, Bakırhan further stated the following:


“From the Law on the Maintenance of Order (Takrir-i Sükûn) to the Independence Tribunals, from secret administrative plans to states of emergency, this issue has always been treated as an exception. The history of this issue within the state has been one in which dual state practices became widespread, politics was sidelined, and the state of exception expanded. The entire country has paid the price for this in one way or another. Today, we have the opportunity to close the chapter filled with pain and denial. We are living in a period in which we must change the very grammar of our political discourse. For the first time, this issue is being discussed in ordinary legislative language, with written justifications, open to negotiation and criticism. The significance of today is that a historical knot is finally beginning to be untied through politics and is being entered into the parliamentary record. Parliament bears the responsibility of resolving this issue through politics and dialogue.


‘Parliament must

open the way to a new chapter in history’


This is also Parliament’s responsibility toward our shared history and our common future. The shared destiny that began between the Shaddadid Kurds and the Seljuks in Kars in 1064 opened the gates of Anatolia with the Battle of Manzikert in 1071. In the following centuries, this partnership was renewed and endured for hundreds of years. The global, regional, and national developments of the 20th century disrupted this dynamic. Today, we have the opportunity to renew it on the basis of democratic and egalitarian principles. Parliament must therefore shoulder this responsibility and open the way to a new chapter in history. We know that the days that make history require strong political will, and that will exists in this Parliament today.


The memory of this Parliament reminds us of the shared history of Turks and Kurds and the powerful potential of their partnership. There has been a shared life between Anatolia and Mesopotamia stretching back centuries. There have been common meeting points, a shared cultural sphere, and shared stories. Our thousand-year brotherhood and the founding of the Republic are proof of this. In Amasya, these lands were regarded as the common homeland of Turks and Kurds. In Erzurum, the will for unity was expressed in this spirit. The First Parliament brought together representatives of different regions and identities under one roof. The 1921 Constitution embodied a pluralist spirit that created space for local self-government. However, this vision narrowed amid a cycle of denial and rebellion. Our ancient historical relationship suffered great damage, a situation that most benefited those who regarded these lands as a threat.


‘The first step toward including the Kurds into the law’


I would like to open a parenthesis here. When this process began, certain foreign powers said, ‘This step will overturn the balance of the Middle East.’ In reality, what will be overturned are the century-old calculations of global powers. We know this very well. This process will frustrate efforts to pit brother against brother. It will strengthen our unity and reinforce our common future. Half a century of conflict has brought immense suffering to every part of this country. Today, we have an opportunity to leave behind the cycle of conflict and violence. author: CMI Argentina
title: Qué cambia para quienes alquilan con la nueva ley: “si no hay contrato ni recibos, hay desalojo en 72 horas”
content:
En su Capítulo II, el proyecto de “Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada” modifica de manera sustancial el procedimiento judicial para desalojar viviendas y locales. Un informe elaborado por Inquilinos Agrupados, que analiza artículo por artículo, señala las consecuencias que tendría la reforma. Advierte que la iniciativa acelera los procesos y reduce las posibilidades de defensa de quienes alquilan, especialmente en un mercado donde una parte importante de los contratos se desarrolla de manera informal, sin contratos escritos o comprobantes formales de pago. “Este proyecto de ley no ordena el mercado de alquileres: desmantela las pocas garantías procesales que le quedaban a quien alquila”, remarca la organización. Entre los principales cambios, señala la incorporación del juicio sumarísimo para todos los desalojos, mecanismos de entrega inmediata del inmueble y restricciones a las pruebas que pueden presentar los inquilinos.


El proyecto de “Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada” contiene un capítulo específico (el Capítulo II) que modifica el procedimiento judicial para los desalojos de viviendas urbanas y rurales y locales en todo el país. Un informe elaborado por Inquilinos Agrupados analiza los 12 artículos que integran este capítulo y advierte que la reforma acelera los procesos y reduce las garantías procesales para quienes alquilan.


“Este proyecto de ley no ordena el mercado de alquileres: desmantela las pocas garantías procesales que le quedaban a quien alquila”, sostiene el documento. Y agrega: “todos los desalojos pasan a tramitarse por la vía más rápida que existe en la Justicia, dejando a los inquilinos sin tiempo real para defenderse”.


Desalojo en el barrio de Monserrat el 25 de agosto de 2025. Foto: GCBA.


Uno de los principales cambios analizados es que todos los juicios de desalojo pasarían a tramitarse mediante el denominado “juicio sumarísimo”, el procedimiento más rápido previsto en el Código Procesal Civil y Comercial. El informe señala que esto reduce los plazos para contestar demandas, presentar pruebas y apelar. “Si no hay contrato ni recibos —la realidad de buena parte del mercado informal— cualquier inquilino puede terminar tratado como intruso y desalojado en 72 horas”, advierte la organización.


La guía también pone el foco en los casos de quienes no tienen contratos escritos o comprobantes formales de pago. El proyecto establece que, en los juicios por falta de pago o vencimiento del contrato, sólo podrán utilizarse pruebas documentales y periciales. Según Inquilinos Agrupados, esto deja particularmente expuestos a quienes pagan el alquiler en efectivo y sin recibos, ya que no podrían recurrir a testigos para demostrar esos pagos.


Foto: Marcos Sierra.


Otro de los puntos cuestionados es la posibilidad de que el juez ordene la entrega inmediata del inmueble antes de que exista una sentencia definitiva cuando el reclamo del propietario resulte verosímil. El informe lo define como “desalojo exprés, sin sentencia firme, basado solo en la apariencia de derecho y la palabra jurada del propietario”.


La iniciativa también contempla mecanismos que permiten requerir el auxilio de la fuerza pública durante las notificaciones y habilita el allanamiento del domicilio en determinadas circunstancias. Para el lanzamiento, además, el proyecto autoriza el uso de la fuerza pública, el allanamiento y la apertura de cerraduras, incluso cuando la propiedad se encuentre desocupada.


Desalojo en Villa Mitre el miércoles 22 de abril de 2026 . Foto: GCBA.


El capítulo incorpora además un mecanismo específico para viviendas donde habiten menores de edad, personas con discapacidad o adultos mayores en situación de desamparo. En esos casos, el juez debe dar intervención a organismos de protección y otorgar un plazo que no puede superar los diez días para procurar una alternativa habitacional transitoria, pero el informe remarca que esto “no impide el desalojo”.


Como conclusión, Inquilinos Agrupados sostiene: “el resultado es un esquema diseñado para acelerar los desalojos y blindar al propietario, mientras el Estado sigue sin garantizar ningún piso mínimo de derechos para quien alquila”.


Foto: Marcos Sierra.


El avance de este tipo de reformas sobre los procedimientos de desalojo se da en un contexto de fuerte deterioro de las condiciones de acceso a la vivienda y de creciente vulnerabilidad de quienes alquilan. En ese escenario, acelerar los mecanismos para recuperar un inmueble y …

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Israel Ramps up Attacks on Reporters in the West Bank
content:
Israeli forces are targeting journalists in the West Bank with growing frequency, contributing to a record number of 108 violations committed against reporters in Palestine as a whole this July. 


Documented violations range from detention, physical assault and obstruction of coverage to raids on journalists’ homes and seizure of equipment. 


According to the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate (PSJ), 90% of incidents recorded last month occurred in the West Bank, including occupied Jerusalem.


The most common violations were attempts to obstruct journalistic coverage, at a moment when

settler attacks in the West Bank have reached an all-time high

. There were 58 instances of journalists being stopped from reporting on illegal activity – more than double last September’s tally of 27 incidents. 


Al Jazeera reports that more than 270 journalists have been killed since October 2023. 


In March, Israeli soldiers killed two Palestinian journalists. Amal Shamali, a Qatar Radio correspondent in Gaza, was struck in an attack targeting displaced people’s tents in Nuseirat refugee camp. Palestine TV’s Marwan Harzallah died in Israel’s Megiddo Prison, where he was being held without charge.


Palestine has become the most dangerous place in the world for journalists, according to Reporters Without Borders. The rights group filed a complaint with the International Criminal Court in 2023, accusing Israel of committing war crimes against journalists in Palestine and Israel itself.

author: Unknown
title: IDPs returning to Serêkaniyê: We cannot express our happiness in words
content:
The first group of migrants from Serêkaniyê, consisting of around 400 families, left the Washokani Camp in Heseke region earlier today. Returning to their homeland after seven years, the migrants hope to live in peace.


Several members of the first group from Serêkaniyê spoke to ANHA before setting off.


Mihemed Hisên El Elî said: “We cannot express our happiness in words. I have a little daughter, and she couldn’t sleep because of the excitement. Returning home has always been our dream. We endured many hardships in displacement. Today we are going back, we will rebuild our homes, and we will live as we did before.”


Fatma Emîn Şerîf said: “I miss my home and my city very much. We faced hardship and suffering during displacement, and our children grew up far from their homeland. We are very happy and grateful to be returning. If I had wings, I would fly with joy. Our house may have been destroyed, but that is no obstacle to our return.”


In the meantime, the group is reported to have reached Serêkaniyê after years of displacement.


The returns, organized as part of the agreement reached between the interim Damascus administration and the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on January 29, are expected to continue.


The Serêkaniyê Migrants Committee announced that registration for families wishing to return will continue in Dêrik, Dirbêsiyê, Til Temir, Amûdê, Qamişlo and Hesekê.

author: Helmut Weiss
title: Kolumbianische Ernährungsgewerkschaft Sinaltrainal ungebrochen im Kampf gegen Coca Cola
content:
Dossier


Eine Regierung, die selbst kleine Zusagen zum Schutz von mit dem Tode bedrohten Gewerkschaftern nicht einhält, stattdessen eine Justiz, die Anzeigen gegen Gewerkschaftsfunktionäre von Seiten paramilitärischer Banden verfolgt, und ein Unternehmen, das unberührt von allem seinen besonderen Stil der Ausbeutung fortsetzt – so ist die Situation der Gewerkschaft Sinaltrainal, die neben der eigenen Kraft nur auf die der Solidarität, in Kolumbien wie weltweit, zählen kann – das wird in dem

Interview von Eric Cortes mit William Mendoza

, Vorsitzender von Sinaltranail, anlässlich des Hungerstreiks der Coca Cola Mitarbeiter am 13. April 2015, Plaza de Bolívar in Bogotá deutlich. Siehe das

Interview

,

Hintergründe

 sowie die weitere Entwicklung zu Coca Cola in Kolumbien:


Aufruf zur internationalen gewerkschaftlichen Solidarität mit den Beschäftigten von Coca-Cola in Kolumbien und der Gewerkschaft SINALTRAINAL


„

Die unterzeichnenden Gewerkschaftsorganisationen des Internationalen Gewerkschaftsnetzwerks für Solidarität und Kampf bekunden ihre tiefste Solidarität mit den Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmern von Coca-Cola in Kolumbien und mit ihrer Gewerkschaft SINALTRAINAL angesichts der schwerwiegenden Vorwürfe bezüglich der Verletzung von Arbeits-, Gewerkschafts- und Menschenrechten.


Coca-Cola beschäftigt derzeit rund 1.000 direkt angestellte Mitarbeiter, während mehr als 9.000 Arbeitnehmer im Rahmen von Outsourcing-Modellen tätig sind – eine Situation, die zu einer erheblichen Prekarisierung der Beschäftigungsverhältnisse führt und die wirksame Ausübung kollektiver Rechte beeinträchtigt.


Wir bringen unsere tiefe Besorgnis über die seit langem bekannten Vorwürfe zum Ausdruck, wonach in Kolumbien zwölf mit dem Unternehmen verbundene Gewerkschaftsführer ermordet wurden – Vorfälle, die einen der schwerwiegendsten Ausdrucksformen gewerkschaftsfeindlicher Gewalt darstellen und weder in Vergessenheit geraten noch ungestraft bleiben dürfen.


Zudem prangert die Gewerkschaft die Nichteinhaltung von Tarifverträgen durch das Unternehmen an, darunter auch die Missachtung von Rechten im Zusammenhang mit gewerkschaftlichen Freistellungen. Hinzu kommt die Zersplitterung der Gewerkschaftsbewegung, die die Fähigkeit zur kollektiven Verteidigung geschwächt und die Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer in eine besonders schwierige Lage gebracht hat. Folglich:


Wir bekunden unsere uneingeschränkte Solidarität mit den Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmern von Coca-Cola in Kolumbien und mit SINALTRAINAL bei der Verteidigung ihrer Arbeits-, Gewerkschafts- und Menschenrechte.


Wir fordern die uneingeschränkte Einhaltung der Tarifverträge und die uneingeschränkte Achtung der Gewerkschaftsfreiheit, einschließlich der Garantien für die Ausübung gewerkschaftlicher Tätigkeiten und der Erteilung der entsprechenden Genehmigungen.


Wir lehnen jede Form der Auslagerung ab, die dazu dient, die Beschäftigungsverhältnisse zu verschlechtern oder die gewerkschaftliche Organisation zu schwächen.

author: Randi Beers
title: Inuit drummers lead Montreal’s 2026 Pride parade
content:
Spectators lined René-Lévesque Boulevard on Sunday, taking in the bright colours of Montreal’s Pride Parade.


Bobby Manning-Leduc, a member of Southern Quebec Inuit Association and workshop host, says he enjoys seeing other Inuit take part in Pride events. (Photo by Cedric Gallant, special to Nunatsiaq News)


Near the front of the parade was a group of Inuit drumming performers, backed by the Southern Quebec Inuit Association. 


The Inuit association was busy that morning, running a brunch table at the Place du Canada park alongside non-profit organization Native Montreal. On the menu were breakfast

burritos, pancakes and eggs, and muskox and potatoes. 


Near the brunch table was Bobby Manning-Leduc,

a member of Southern Quebec Inuit Association who has lived most of his life in Montreal, but has family ancestry from Kinngait.


“When I was younger, I never really saw Inuit at Pride,” he said.


“It is good to see that younger generations do participate in Pride.”


He said it can be helpful for northerners to see people in larger urban centres who are not afraid to celebrate Pride.


“I had a cousin up north who is gay, and he hid it for a long time,” Manning-Leduc said. “But he knew since he was 14, he just hid it.” 


Seeing the Southern Quebec Inuit Association join forces with other Indigenous non-profits during Pride creates a welcoming atmosphere, and can help make life less lonely for Inuit who live in the city, he said.


Back at the parade, the Inuit traditional drummers led the way for more drummers and singers, some of them hoop dancing while standing on a pedestal. The caravan was hosted by Indigenous non-profit organization Projet Autochtones.


As the Inuit drum-dancers broke out into a dancing pattern, the crowd cheered.


Pride Montreal, which ran from July 31 to Aug. 9, bills itself as the largest celebration of its kind in the French-speaking world. It attracts an estimated 750,000 people to various events, including music performances, film screenings, workshops and panels.


This summer marked 20 years of Pride Montreal.

title: Can Atalay'dan 'çerçeve yasa' açıklaması: 'Şiddetsiz siyaset' adımları önemlidir
content:
Gezi Davası kapsamında 4 yıldan uzun süredir cezaevinde tutulan Can Atalay, TBMM Genel Kurulunda görüşülen 'çerçeve yasa' konusunda açıklama yaptı.

'Türkiye Cumhuriyeti hükümetini ortadan kaldırmaya teşebbüse yardım" suçlamasıyla 18 yıl hapis cezası verilen ve Hatay milletvekilliği düşürülen Can Atalay'ın açıklaması sosyal medya hesabından paylaşıldı.

TBMM Adalet Komisyonunda kabul edilen 12 maddelik yasa teklifi için 'şiddetsiz siyaset ortamı oluşturmanın' adımlarının önemli olduğunu vurgulayan Atalay, 4 Mart 2025 tarihli açıklamasını tekrar paylaştı.

Can Atalay'ın "Şiddetin gölgesini, memleketin ve Kürt yurttaşlarımızın demokratik talepleri üzerinden kaldırmak için hatırlatma ve tavrımdır" başlığıyla yayımladığı açıklamasının şu şekilde:

"Şubat 2025’te 'silahların bırakılması' çağrısından hemen sonra ülkemizde; Anayasa'nın, yasaların, başta TBMM olmak üzere kurumların, kuralların askıda olduğunu dikkat merkezimizden kaçırmadan ama Kürt sorununda 'silahlara veda çağrısı'nın başlatacağı yeni bir siyaset ortamını heba etmeden sürecin ülkemiz ve bölgemiz için önemli sonuçları olacağını açıkladım.

Bugün de ülkemizde demokratik siyaset ortamının bir yıl öncesine göre daha olumsuz olduğunun altını çizerek 'şiddetsiz siyaset' adımları önemlidir.

4 Mart 2025 tarihli açıklamamı tekrar paylaşıyorum.

'Şiddetsiz bir siyaset ortamı oluşturmak için' her yurttaşın, her kurumun önemsemesi gereken çok güçlü bir çağrı yapıldı.

Bir an için Anayasa’nın askıda olduğunu unutalım.

Bir an için hukukun en dipte, keyfiliğin dorukta olduğunu unutalım.

Bir an için her türlü demokratik talep gibi Kürt yurttaşlarımızın demokratik taleplerinin demokratik bir ortam olmadan serpilip gelişemeyeceğini, atılan adımların güvenceye kavuşamayacağını, kalıcı olamayacağını da unutalım.

Şimdi, Kürt Sorununun silahların gölgesi olmadan, şiddetsiz bir ortamda konuşulabilmesi için, 'önce barış' diyen, 'şiddetsiz bir siyaset ortamı' için yapılan çağrıya dikkat kesilelim. Yakılmaya çalışılan barış ateşinin, her yönden esen sert siyaset fırtınalarıyla sönmemesi için çevresini kuşatalım. Toplumsallaşması için sahip çıkalım.

Kürt Sorunu üzerinden şiddetin gölgesinin kaldırılması çabaları yeni toplumsal ve siyasal mutabakatlar için bir fırsat olabilir. Bu çabanın karşılığı verilmelidir. Barışçı bir ortamda bütün görüşlerin özgürce kendini ifade edebilmesi, derinlemesine konuşulup tartışılması 'fiili durumlar'a, siyasetin hoşgörüsüne bırakılamaz. Önceki yılların 'fiili durumlar'ının sonuçlarını yaşamaktayız. Şiddetin siyasetten dışlanması adımları siyasetten gelen demokratik adımlarla karşılık bulmalıdır.

Sorunun çözümü geniş bir toplumsal mutabakat gerektiriyor. Toplumsal ve siyasal desteği genişletmenin ilk adımı Meclisi çözüm odağı olarak işlevli kılıp süreci şeffaflaştırmaktır. Acilen, önceki yıllarda yasal güvencelere bağlanmadan atılmış adımların ceremesini yaşayanları özgürleştirmek, Kürt yurttaşlarımızın seçme iradesini yok eden kayyumluk vesayetine son vermektir.

Her ileri adım önemlidir. Dikkate alınmayı hak eder.

Ve şimdi başta “unutalım” dediklerimizin hepsini yeniden hatırlayalım.

Cumhuriyetimizi demokratikleştirmek için; hukukun, yasaların, kurallı, kurumlu bir işleyişin kazanılması için, Kürt yurttaşlarımızın demokratik talepleri için, eşit ve özgür bir Türkiye için yürüyüşümüze devam edelim."

*“ŞİDDETİN GÖLGESİNİ, MEMLEKETİN ve KÜRT YURTTAŞLARIMIZIN DEMOKRATİK TALEPLERİ ÜZERİNDEN KALDIRMAK” İÇİN HATIRLATMA ve TAVRIMDIR!* Şubat 2025’te “silahların bırakılması” çağrısından hemen sonra *ülkemizde; Anayasanın, yasaların, başta TBMM olmak üzere kurumların, kuralların… pic.twitter.com/873SzR8ZLM

author: Unknown
title: Tuncer Bakırhan 'çerçeve yasa' görüşmelerinde konuştu: "Metni ne gözü kapalı kutsuyoruz ne de eksik diye reddediyoruz"
content:
Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti) Eş Genel Başkanı Tuncer Bakırhan, 'çerçeve yasa' kapsamında TBMM Genel Kurulunda konuştu.

Bakırhan konuşmasında “Görüştüğümüz bu kanun teklifi, ülke olarak yeni bir istikamete yol almanın pusulasıdır. Türkiye'nin kendi içindeki ateşi çağrısıyla bu başlangıca imkân sağlayan Sayın Öcalan’ın bu kurucu rolünün altını önemle çizmek istiyorum. Kendisinin Türkiye çözümünden yana çabalarının önyargılarla değil, hakkaniyetle görülmesi gerekiyor. Özellikle Cumhurbaşkanı Sayın Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Meclis Başkanı Sayın Numan Kurtulmuş, MHP Genel Başkanı Sayın Devlet Bahçeli’nin süreçteki kurucu rolünün hakkını veriyoruz” dedi.

Yasanın ayrıcalık üreten bir yasa olmadığını belirten Bakırhan, “Çatışma çözümünün ilk adımıdır. Bu bir al-ver meselesi değil. Bu yasa ve süreç taviz değildir; yenme ve yenilme hiç değildir. Bu sürecin tek bir kazananı var. O da tüm Türkiye’dir, 86 milyon yurttaşımızdır. Barış bir müsabaka değildir. Halklar arasında tutulmuş bir skor tabelası olarak görülmemelidir. Bu süreç kimliğimizin eritilmesi değil, varlığımızın hukukla buluşmasıdır. 'Yine mi kandırılacağız' kaygısını biliyoruz; bu kaygı vehim değil, sizi çok iyi anlıyoruz. Her şeyden önce Kürtler artık örgütlü bir halktır. Ne kanar ne de kandırılır. Velev ki terazimiz şaşsa da düzeltecek bir kantar var. O da sizsiniz” şeklinde konuştu.

Bakırhan yasaya dair eksiklerin fakında olduklarına dair de vurgu yaptı:

“Bu metni ne gözü kapalı kutsuyoruz ne eksik diye reddediyoruz. Değerini teslim ediyor, eksiğini açıkça söylüyoruz. Bu yasada şüphesiz eksiklikler ve eleştirilecek yönler de var. Bu yasada yok diye ana dili, eşit yurttaşlık ve yerel demokrasi başta olmak üzere demokratik haklar unutulmuş talepler değildir. Bunlar sürecin olmazsa olmazıdır. Barışa giden yolun taşlarıdır. Fakat ilk aşamanın ölçütleriyle nihai çözümün ölçütlerini birbirine karıştırmamalıyız. İlk adımın işlevi, çatışma zemininden hukuk zeminine geçişi mümkün kılmak ve demokratik siyasi mücadeleye kapı aralamaktır.”

Süreci "Kürt kimliğinin eritilmesi değil, varlığının hukukla buluşması" olarak nitelendiren Bakırhan, "'Yine mi kandırılacağız' kaygısını biliyoruz. Bu kaygı vehim değil. Çok iyi anlıyoruz. Her şeyden önce Kürtler örgütlü bir halktır. Ne kanar ne de kandırılır. Velev ki terazimiz şaşsa da düzeltecek bir kantar var. O da sizsiniz. Emin olun siyaset alanında Kürt halkının demokratik hakları için daha güçlü mücadeleye devam edeceğiz. Ama şimdi hepimizi yakan bir ateş var. Önce o ateşi söndürmeliyiz. Kürtçe’de ‘agir bi agir venamire’ denir. Yani ateş ateşle söndürülmez. Elli yıllık çatışmanın bize öğrettiği en yanlı hakikat budur inanın" şekinde konuştu.

Düzenlemenin birlikteliği güçlendireceğini vurgulayan Bakırhan, "Yarım asırlık çatışmalı süreç ülkemizin her bir yanına büyük acılar yaşattı. Yüz yıl önce Kürtler hukuk dışına itilmişti. Bu kök yasa, Kürtleri hukuka dahil etmenin ve tarihi eşiği aşmanın ilk adımıdır. Bu süreç Türkiye'nin bölünmesine değil bütünleşmesine, ayrışmaya değil ortak yaşamın güçlendirilmesine büyük bir fırsat sunacaktır. Ortak tarihimize ve geleceğimize karşı sorumluluğumuzu Meclis çatısı altında kararlılıkla yerine getiriyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı.

author: Unknown
title: Mersin Barosu: "Turizm cennetimizi çöp rantına kurban etmeyin"
content:
Gözde Tüzer Korkmaz [email protected]

Mersin Barosu Başkanlığı ile Mersin Barosu Kent ve Çevre Komisyonu yaptığı yazılı açıklamada, Türkiye turizminin ithal çöp rantçılarının hırsı uğruna heba edildiğini, Akdeniz kıyılarında artan mikropilastik kirliliğin insan ve çevre sağlığını telafisi imkânsız devasa bir felakete sürüklediğini belirterek, “Plastik atık ithalatına derhal son verilsin. Turizm cennetimizi çöp rantına kurban etmeyin” ifadelerini kullandı.

Akdeniz’deki mikroplastik alarmı konusunda yazılı açıklama yapan Mersin Barosu Başkanlığı ile Mersin Barosu Kent ve Çevre Komisyonu açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verdi:

“Son dönemde Mersin, Adana ve Antalya kıyılarında yoğun mikroplastik kirliliğini gösteren görüntülerin kamuoyuna yansıması, Akdeniz’in ve kıyılarımızın karşı karşıya bulunduğu çevresel tehdidin ciddiyetini bir kez daha ortaya koymuştur. Türkiye, Avrupa'nın plastik atıklarını ithal eden ülkeler arasında uzun yıllardır ilk sırada yer almaktadır. Bilim insanlarına göre bu kirliliğin önemli nedenlerinden birinin, Avrupa'dan ithal edilen plastik atıklar olduğu, geri dönüşüm tesislerinde işlenen plastiklerin bir bölümünün süreç sonunda mikroplastik olarak denizlere karıştığının tahmin edildiği belirtilmiştir.”

“Türkiye’nin 17 milyar dolarlık turizm; ithal çöp rantçılarının hırsı uğruna heba ediliyor. Turizm cenneti sahillerimizi parayla ölçülemeyecek, telafisi imkânsız devasa bir doğa felaketine sürüklenmektedir. 2025 yılı bilimsel verilerine göre plastik atık ithalatı bir önceki yıla göre yüzde 19 artarak 503 bin tona ulaşmıştır. Yine bilimsel açıklamalara göre, dünyadaki plastiklerin yalnızca yüzde 9’unun geri dönüştürüldüğü, büyük bölümünün geri dönüştürülemediği, çöplüklere gönderildiği, plastiklerin fosil yakıtlardan üretildiği ve geri dönüşüm ya da yakma süreçlerinde ortaya çıkan toksik maddelerin insan sağlığı açısından ciddi risk oluşturduğu, iklim krizini derinleştirdiği kaydedilmiştir. “

“Avrupa ülkelerinden Türkiye’ye plastik atık ithalatının yüksek seviyelere ulaşması bu kapsamda kamu otoritelerince bilimsel veriler ışığında titizlikle değerlendirilmesi gereken önemli bir konudur. Plastik atıkların ülkeye girişinden nihai bertarafına kadar tüm süreçlerin etkin biçimde denetlenmesi ve çevre mevzuatına aykırı faaliyetlere karşı gerekli yaptırımların uygulanması zorunludur.”

“Anayasa’nın 56. maddesi, herkesin sağlıklı ve dengeli bir çevrede yaşama hakkına sahip olduğunu açıkça güvence altına almaktadır. Aynı madde uyarınca çevreyi geliştirmek, çevre sağlığını korumak ve çevre kirlenmesini önlemek yalnızca bireylerin değil, devletin de temel görevleri arasındadır. Bu nedenle çevrenin korunması, ekonomik çıkarların gerisinde bırakılabilecek bir mesele değil; anayasal güvence altındaki temel bir haktır.”

“Denizlerimizin, kıyılarımızın ve doğal yaşam alanlarımızın ekonomik kazançlar uğruna geri dönülmez biçimde zarar görmesine izin verilmemelidir. Turizm, tarım, balıkçılık ve kıyı ekosistemleri üzerinde yaratacağı uzun vadeli sonuçlar dikkate alınmadan yürütülecek bir atık politikası, yalnızca bugünün değil gelecek kuşakların da yaşam hakkını tehdit edecektir.”

“Bu nedenle; plastik atık ithalatı ve geri dönüşüm süreçlerine ilişkin etkin denetim mekanizmalarının işletilmesini, çevresel risklerin bağımsız ve bilimsel biçimde araştırılmasını, mikroplastik kirliliğinin kaynağının ortaya çıkarılmasını ve sorumlular hakkında gerekli hukuki ve idari işlemlerin gecikmeksizin yapılmasını talep ediyoruz.”

"Mersin Barosu Başkanlığı ve Mersin Barosu Kent ve Çevre Komisyonu olarak; hukukun üstünlüğünü, insan haklarını ve sağlıklı bir çevrede yaşama hakkını savunmanın sorumluluğuyla, Akdeniz’in ve kıyılarımızın korunması konusunda kamuoyunu duyarlı olmaya, yetkili kurumları ise görev ve sorumluluklarını etkin biçimde yerine getirmeye çağırıyoruz. Denizlerimizi, kıyılarımızı ve geleceğimizi plastik atıklara teslim etmemek için hukuksal mücadelemizi sürdüreceğiz.

Akdeniz bizim ortak yaşam alanımızdır. Plastik atık ithalatına derhal son verilsin. Turizm cennetimizi çöp rantına kurban etmeyin.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Edinburgh International Festival Director & Famed Violinist Nicola Benedetti on the Power of Art
content:
Democracy Now!

 is broadcasting from Scotland at the Edinburgh International Festival, which features music, opera, theater and dance and is one of Europe’s biggest arts festivals. We are joined by the acclaimed Scottish violinist Nicola Benedetti, one of the most celebrated classical violinists in the world. She became the first woman and first Scottish artist to become director of the Edinburgh International Festival in 2022.


“I think what is quite unusual about the Edinburgh International Festival is the humanitarian mission that is woven into all of its origin rhetoric,” says Benedetti. She explains that this year’s festival focuses on the 250th anniversary of the American Revolution. “We’re not celebrating only dark or dazzling. We’re trying to present these things alongside each other.”

author: Mosha Folger
title: Judge says Iqaluit lawyer was unfairly denied entry to legal aid panel
content:
A Toronto judge found that a Nunavut legal service “breached its duty of fairness” when it denied an Iqaluit lawyer re-admission to its panel of criminal lawyers.


In his Aug. 6 decision, Justice Paul Rouleau said the Legal Services Board of Nunavut should reconsider reinstating Alison Crowe to its legal aid panel, the board’s private practice lawyers who provide services to legal aid clients.


“The appropriate disposition is simply to remit the matter to the [board] for reconsideration,” he wrote.


In January, Crowe applied for a judge to order the board to add her to the panel, of which she was a member from around 2012 to October 2024, when she resigned and

became

 a justice of the peace.


In June 2025 applied to rejoin the Legal Aid panel but was denied admittance. In court documents, Crowe said legal aid files had accounted for at least four-fifths of her annual income.


In his letter to inform Crowe of the board’s decision, co-chairperson Tim Zehr said that “a number of concerns were raised, including your interpersonal skills, your ability to work with Inuk staff and some questionable interactions with staff lawyers and judges.”


In January, she

asked a judge

 to order the legal services board to reinstate her.


For that judicial review, the board had to file evidence for the basis of its decision.


For her part, Crowe had to “explain why [the board’s concerns] are either unfounded or do not provide a basis for rejecting her reinstatement application.”


Rouleau stopped short of reinstating her, partially because there was “no allegation of bad faith by the [legal services board].”


“I trust that, now informed of the applicant’s response to its concerns, the [board] will exercise its discretion fairly and appropriately,” he wrote.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to Stephen Bird, who represented the board in January, but he did not respond before press time.


Crowe, when asked for comment, said in an email that “as the matter is still pending, I am limited in what I can say. The decision and pleadings are all public documents and speak for themselves.”

author: David Swanson
title: Pax Silica: The Philippines’ Role in Propping up U.S. Militarism and War
content:
Pax Silica will not only exploit the Philippines’ natural resources and workforce, but it will also drag the country further into a role that serves ongoing U.S. military aggression and war. The Filipino people must reject Pax Silica and call on the Philippine government to end all agreements between the U.S. and the Philippines.


By Jhay de Jesus, World BEYOND War Asia Organizer, August 10, 2026


What is Pax Silica?


Pax Silica

 is a U.S.-led coalition launched in December 2025 as the U.S. Department of State’s flagship effort on artificial intelligence (AI) and supply chain security. This

economic partnership

 between the U.S. and its allies will facilitate supply chains for mineral mining, semiconductor manufacturing, the creation of energy-intensive AI data centers, and surveillance technology infrastructure.


Currently, there are

24 member states

 to Pax Silica. Israel is among the founding members alongside the U.S., Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and the United Kingdom. Taiwan is a non-signatory but has endorsed the declaration’s principles via the Joint Statement on the Pax Silica Declaration and U.S.-Taiwan Economic Security Cooperation.


The Philippines entered the coalition in April 2026. As part of its entry into the coalition, the Philippine government is leasing around 4,000 acres (1,600 hectares) of land in New Clark City, Tarlac, Central Luzon. As part of the broader Luzon Economic Corridor, this

lease

 is intended to last up to 99 years. This Economic Security Zone will serve as a site for high-tech industries and supporting businesses, functioning as a supply chain hub for artificial intelligence (AI) technology.


The formal binding agreement is set to be signed in November 2026.


Issues Surrounding Pax Silica (How Will It Affect the Filipino People?)


Various sectors are raising critical concerns about this project. One major issue is the strain on electricity and water supplies. Because data centers run 24/7, they require vast amounts of power and water. An estimated 3,000 megawatts are needed to power the facilities, along with 60 to 130 million liters of water daily for their cooling systems—all while the country continues to face ongoing electricity and water crises.


Additionally, concerns regarding ancestral domains and agricultural land have surfaced. Local farmers are already experiencing problems of land grabbing and conversion from agricultural to commercial use. They also receive little to no support from the government. Indigenous communities in particular face land-grabbing of their ancestral domains by government and corporations. And now, these land categories are the site for Pax Silica infrastructure. Evictions of settlers already started as some families of farmers are offered small amounts to sell their lands to the government for this project.


Sovereignty also remains a central concern for the public. Historically, agreements between the Philippine and U.S. governments have been unequal. Starting with the Mutual Defense Treaty, these pacts have spawned further military cooperation, such as the Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA). These agreements opened more locations for permanent U.S. military presence in the country, which has been a source of human rights violations such as gender-based violence, further militarization of communities, and evictions.


While the Philippine government promises that Pax Silica will bring more jobs and economic growth, no consultations were conducted with affected communities and sectors. Furthermore, the government has provided no assurance that the formal binding agreement will be fair or capable of delivering on these promises.


July 27, 2026. Translation: Resist and Fight Pax Silica!


Young Bataeños for Environmental Advocacy Network (Young BEAN

)


On Peace and Security


Pax Silica will serve U.S. military interests by hosting infrastructure used to develop surveillance systems, military technology, and the global arms industry.


Amid ongoing conflicts involving the U.S. and Israel in regions like Palestine and Iran, infrastructure under Pax Silica will support the U.S. and Israel’s objective of maintaining constant surveillance on designated rival nations and enhancing their military advantage. These facilities also leave local communities vulnerable to attacks if rival countries launch a counter-offensive. Furthermore, the coalition serves the U.S …

title: Framework Law debated in the Turkish Parliament: A milestone for a peaceful resolution
content:
The draft law titled “Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” prepared within the framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, is being debated at the plenary session of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey today.


The twelve-article draft was submitted to the parliamentary presidency on Wednesday with the signatures of 367 members of parliament. Two days later, deliberations on the bill began in the Justice Committee.


After around 18 hours of deliberations, the committee approved the draft by majority vote and forwarded it to the plenary.


The parliamentary debate began today at 11:00 a.m. local time. As in the Justice Committee, the draft law is expected to be approved by a majority of lawmakers in the plenary.


The deliberations on the draft law began with lawmakers’ speeches.


In their speeches, DEM Party MPs emphasized that the proposal represents an important opportunity for the democratic and peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question, the establishment of lasting peace, and coexistence.


'One of the most important days in the history of the Turkish Parliament'


Hakkari MP Onur Düşünmez said that Parliament was experiencing one of the most important days in its history and expressed hope that the overwhelming majority of lawmakers would take a stand in favor of peace. Düşünmez also expressed the hope that the proposal would become the first step toward achieving a Democratic Republic.


'A milestone for a democratic and peaceful resolution'


Şırnak MP Zeki İrmez described the proposal as a “milestone” for the democratic and peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question. İrmez said they would continue their struggle to consolidate peace and build a democratic society.


'An opportunity for a transition from conflict to democratic politics'


Şırnak MP Beritan Güneş Altın said the law provides an opportunity for a transition from conflict to democratic politics, adding: “However, if everyone is not placed under legal protection during the process of its formation, it will turn into conflict and suffering. Unfortunately, we experienced this during the first century of the Republic of Turkey. Now is the time to unite the ideals of the Republic with democracy.”


Beritan Güneş Altın stated that, in the past, the lack of legal safeguards in Turkey had led to the reproduction of conflict and suffering. She called for the Republic to be united with democracy and for political issues to be resolved through democratic dialogue.


'Constructive suggestions and criticism will also eliminate potential ambiguities'


Mersin MP Ali Bozan also drew attention to the high attendance at the plenary session where the proposal is being debated, stating that constructive suggestions and criticism should be taken into account during the legislative process. Bozan said, “Taking these constructive suggestions and criticism into consideration will also eliminate potential ambiguities during the implementation of the framework law.”


'Peace is a society healing enough to live together'


Mardin MP Kamuran Tanhan said the new regulation would pave the way for freedom, peace, and coexistence, while Diyarbakır (Amed) MP Serhat Eren stated that it should mark “the beginning of a new legal order that does not carry the conflicts of the past into the future.”


“Peace is not merely a society’s survival. Peace is a society healing enough to live together. Let this law become the beginning of a new legal order that does not carry the conflicts of the past into the future,” Eren said.

title: Two Kurdish researchers remain detained in Orumiyeh prison
content:
Kajal Mobaraki and her husband, Jamal Ahmadzadeh, two Kurdish researchers at Orumiyeh University of Medical Sciences, remain detained in Orumiyeh Central Prison more than six weeks after their arrest by security forces.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that security forces arrested Mobaraki, from Dehgolan, Kurdistan Province, and Ahmadzadeh, from Mahabad, West Azerbaijan Province, in their vehicle in Orumiyeh in late June.


The forces did not present a warrant and transferred the couple to a security detention facility in the city.


They were interrogated there for several weeks while being denied access to a lawyer and family visits, before being transferred to Orumiyeh Central Prison.


The charges brought against the two citizens remain unknown.

author: Steven Methven
title: The Jason Arday Saga Is a Story of Great British Gullibility
content:
April may be the cruellest month, but August is the daftest. For around a fortnight now, we’ve all had to participate in the story of Jason Arday, a former professor in Cambridge University’s education department (

he quit last week

). Has anyone ever heard of that faculty before? Well, you have now.


I’ll give you the long story short. Arday, appointed in 2023 and

Cambridge’s youngest ever black professor

, had, it turns out, a well-publicised biography with

significant inconsistencies

. His academic work is also in dispute, with

allegations of plagiarism

 in his PhD thesis and potentially other forms of academic misconduct in some of his published work making headlines.


For his part, Arday resigned from his post at Cambridge last week, describing his “profound sadness” at the decision. He added that the intense public scrutiny had “taken a profound toll on me and on those I love”. However, he vowed to “return stronger, wiser and with the same determination” and said his resignation should not “be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me”.


There’s been a lot of hand-wringing around these claims, endless calls for investigations, and the general sense that, yes, it’s the end times. But lads, don’t we live in Britain? Isn’t the (alleged) grift a national industry?


You say con. I say: that’s Britness, baby.


I don’t want to defend Jason Arday. To be honest, I find the story mostly hilarious.  I hadn’t heard of him before the last few weeks. But could people

really have believed

 that he was

mute til 11, illiterate til 18

, but also, a runner of

multiple marathons

 and a former

sufferer of locked-in syndrome

 to boot? God bless

his old primary schoolmate

, who, claiming online to remember a young Arday, labelled him a

‘chatty patty’

. And they say this country needs more weapons.


Cambridge University dons were beguiled by Arday – you only have to watch the BBC broadcast around his appointment to

see and hear it from his head of department

. Never mind that Britain has been beguiled by Cambridge – and Oxford – for centuries. Many, it seems, still believe the fairytale that these two institutions are the nation’s Harry Potter sorting hat, infallibly sifting the best from the rest. We eat it up. That’s partly why this mild puncturing of national mythology – Arday was, after all, just one among over 6,000 Cambridge academic staff – has generated such overheated reactions.


Yes, Cambridge fell for it. And from that fact we’re asked to draw sweeping diagnostic conclusions about everything that’s wrong with the country. The right has its answer – the “victimisation” of white people to the benefit of people of other ethnicities has gone too far, not just in academia but everywhere. This shouldn’t even need a reply, when last year there were

just 75 black academics

 across all levels in a university that draws talent from across the world. That’s just 1.25% of its teaching and research staff.


Their lives are very likely now going

to be made hell

, as scores of MacBook Miss Marples, suddenly gifted with the ability to judge advanced research in fields from nanotechnology to ancient Greek, start scouring their work. And the rest of us will have to endure even more

weepy existential questions

 from people who suddenly find that this one university really, really matters to them.


If you care about British universities, maybe worry about the

imminent contraction

 of a sector that

employs around 700,000 people

. I’m not seeing a lot of headlines about that.


Still, how could Cambridge –

Cambridge!

 – be fooled? The answer isn’t complicated. It exists in Britain, a nation of patsies that repeatedly falls for cons.


We’re constantly beguiled. We were

deceived by the Lib Dems

 in the coalition government,

then by austerity

,

then by Brexit

. We were fooled by

ops against Jeremy Corbyn

,

oven-ready deals

 from Boris Johnson and

PPE contracts

 during Covid (Michelle Mone is

still in the House of Lords

, by the way). Keir Starmer played

an absolute blinder

 in the deception-leagues. And Reform UK, distorted by now

seemingly endless


financial scandals

, still somehow survives.


I’d love to say that, in our tradition of national self-owns, Jason Arday represents black excellence. But no. It’s a B-minus at best. The only innovation is that, finally, the establishment got duped. You know what? Make it a B.


It’s becoming increasingly difficult …

title: Nichteinhaltung des Mindestlohns in Deutschland
content:
Dossier


„… Seit dem 1. Januar 2015 gilt in Deutschland ein einheitlicher gesetzlicher Mindestlohn. Zwar belegen Forschungsergebnisse einen positiven Effekt auf Löhne am unteren Ende der Lohnverteilung, der mit der Einführung des Mindestlohns einhergeht. Dieser Befund bedeutet jedoch nicht, dass es keine Unterschreitung des Mindestlohns gibt. Wie viele Personen unterhalb der Mindestlohngrenze bezahlt werden, ist bisher nicht abschließend geklärt worden. Die Einschätzungen zu dieser Frage reichen von etwa 483.000 Personen im Jahr 2018 bis zu 2,4 Millionen Personen. In dieser Stellungnahme werden die Schwierigkeiten beschrieben, das Ausmaß der Nichteinhaltung mit den vorliegenden Datensätzen abzuschätzen…“

 12-seitige

IAB-Stellungnahme 7/2020 verfasst von Duncan Roth in 10/2020

 


, siehe dazu:


DGB-Studie belegt Gesamtschaden durch Mindestlohnverstöße seit 2015 bis Ende 2024 von mind. 64 Milliarden Euro – Kontrollbehörden chronisch unterbesetzt


„

64 Milliarden Euro Schaden sind durch Mindestlohnbetrug seit 2015 entstanden, zeigt eine aktuelle Studie des Deutschen Gewerkschaftsbundes. Zur Vorstellung der DGB-Auswertung erklärt Stefan Körzell, stellvertretender DGB-Vorsitzender: „Wer den Sozialstaat stärken will, muss Lohnraub konsequent bekämpfen, statt die Rechnung denjenigen aufzubürden, die jeden Tag arbeiten und trotzdem oft kaum über die Runden kommen. Mindestlohnbetrug ist kein Kavaliersdelikt – er muss rigoros verfolgt und hart bestraft werden.


Während die Politik über Sozialabbau und weitreichende Kürzungen diskutiert, lassen kriminelle Arbeitgeber Milliarden in ihren eigenen Taschen verschwinden, die eigentlich den Beschäftigten, den Sozialversicherungen und dem Staat zustehen. Mit diesem Geld ließen sich Renten und Krankenversicherung stärken, Kitas und Schulen finanzieren und dringend notwendige Investitionen ermöglichen. Gleichzeitig würde dies die Binnennachfrage stärken und die Konjunktur stützen, denn wer zum Mindestlohn arbeitet, gibt dieses Geld meist direkt für den Konsum aus

.““

DGB-Pressemitteilung vom 10. August 2026


 („Mindestlohnbetrug kostet die Gesellschaft 64 Milliarden Euro“) zu:


Mindestlohnbetrug kostet die Gesellschaft 64 Milliarden Euro! Exklusive DGB Auswertung zu den finanziellen Auswirkungen von Mindestlohnverstößen


„Rund 6 Millionen Beschäftigte in Deutschland arbeiten zum Mindestlohn – vor allem im Gastgewerbe, im Handel und in der Landwirtschaft. Der gesetzliche Mindestlohn beträgt derzeit 13,90 Euro pro Stunde und steigt im kommenden Jahr auf 14,60 Euro. Doch der Mindestlohn kann nur dann seine soziale Schutzfunktion entfalten, wenn er bei den Beschäftigten auch tatsächlich ankommt. Genau daran mangelt es seit Jahren – und das mit enormen Folgen für Beschäftigte und die Allgemeinheit. Seit Einführung der gesetzlichen Lohnuntergrenze im Jahr 2015 haben durchschnittlich rund 2 Millionen

Beschäftigte jährlich nicht den ihnen zustehenden Lohn erhalten, wie die Berechnungen auf Grundlage des Sozioökonomischen Panels (SOEP) zeigen. Besonders betroffen sind Teilzeit- und geringfügig Beschäftigte, Frauen sowie Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer in Ostdeutschland. (…)


Dem Fiskus fehlen 7 Milliarden Euro an Einkommensteuer.Die unmittelbar Betroffenen – die Beschäftigten selbst – haben netto rund 35 Milliarden Euro weniger erhalten, als ihnen bei ordnungsgemäßer Lohnzahlung zugestanden hätte. Nicht inbegriffen in den Berechnungen sind unrechtmäßige Abweichungen von Zahlungen vertraglich und tariflich vereinbarter Löhne durch die Arbeitgeber, die oberhalb des Mindestlohns liegen. Es ist folglich davon auszugehen, dass die gesamtwirtschaftliche Schadenssumme aller unrechtmäßigen Lohnauszahlungen somit deutlich höher

liegt.


Diese Zahlen gewinnen besonderes Gewicht vor dem Hintergrund der aktuellen politischen Debatte über Einschnitte bei den Sozialversicherungen und den Abbau sozialer Leistungen. Ein Teil der Finanzierungslücken geht auf kriminelles Handeln von Arbeitgebern zurück, die ihren gesetzlichen Pflichten nicht nachkommen.

title: Menzione: The fact that Abdullah Öcalan’s status has still not been defined is a major problem
content:
The draft framework law entitled “Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration,” prepared as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, was discussed by the Parliamentary Justice Commission after being submitted to the Speaker of Parliament and was approved in a vote.


Italian lawyer Ezio Menzione, who has been closely following the process, spoke to ANF about the draft framework law. Describing the framework law as an important beginning, Menzione criticized, in particular, the fact that Öcalan’s status has still not been clarified, that responsibility for verifying the laying down of arms has been assigned solely to the government-controlled National Security Council, and that there is insufficient democratic and parliamentary oversight of the implementation of the law.


 


A good beginning


Lawyer Menzione said he viewed positively the fact that the draft framework law was supported by all parties, saying that it had moved the process onto a political and legal footing.


“I don't think the framework law that has emerged is bad. I appreciated the fact that all parties, even the opposition, voted for it and supported it,” Menzione said, noting that the law had moved the discussion beyond the level of words and onto a political and legal platform.


Menzione said that the next stage should involve a concrete discussion of what needs to be done. “This is no longer a time for discussing things in general terms. From now on, each point must be addressed from a political and legal perspective, because this is the only way to advance the peace process and ensure that it reaches its goals,” he said.


Menzione said Parliament should approve the law and that the regulation should become law. “Some additional regulations are needed for the law to be implemented. But this is a good beginning and I must admit that I did not expect a draft law that was this realistic, concrete and implementable in the form in which it has been prepared,” he said.


The uncertainty over Öcalan's status is the most critical point


Lawyer Menzione emphasized that one of the most important shortcomings and critical points in the draft framework law was the uncertainty surrounding Öcalan’s status. “It is unacceptable to exclude Öcalan from the opportunities provided by the law, that is, by the draft law. This is very unfortunate, very negative. This is the most critical point, because Öcalan is the principal actor in the entire process. If Öcalan is excluded from the process, it becomes uncertain how any progress can be achieved,” he said.


Menzione argued that Article 3 of the framework law was intended to target Öcalan, and said that the exception extending to June 2005 would essentially exclude Öcalan and a few other people from the scope of the regulation.


Emphasizing the importance of including Öcalan in the process and clarifying his status, Menzione said: “It is difficult even to imagine how the process can continue without Öcalan. Initially, a measure such as house arrest could be introduced for Öcalan. It is important to place Öcalan in a position from which he can work on the process, as he has done over the past two years. Two years, or slightly more than two years, have passed since the process began. I hope Öcalan’s status will be clarified. Because he cannot lead the Kurdish people from İmralı in the way required by the process. Öcalan should be regarded not only as the leader of the PKK, but as the leader of all Kurds and the Kurdish people.”


Lawyer Menzione also criticized the decision to leave responsibility for the laying down of arms and its verification solely to the National Security Council. “I would have preferred this responsibility to be given to a special parliamentary committee rather than a body subordinate to the government. Because that would ensure that real political representation was involved in such a verification process. Otherwise, leaving such verification to a non-independent body such as the Security Council would not be impartial,” he said.


Menzione also noted that the draft did not make clear the timing between the verification of the laying down of arms and the implementation of the legal regulations. “Before moving on to the details of releasing all prisoners and all opponents, will they wait for the laying down of arms and for the laying down of arms to be verified? That is a question, a fundamental question,” he said.

title: First convoy sets off for Serêkaniyê
content:
The first convoy for the return to Serêkaniyê, which was occupied by the Turkish state in 2019, departed this morning from the gathering point opposite the Waşûkanî Camp in the Tiwêna district of Hesekê.


Initially, 647 families from the city of Serêkaniyê and its surrounding countryside were expected to return. However, due to logistical problems, around 400 families were able to join the convoy.


The returns, carried out as part of the agreement reached between the interim Damascus administration and the SDF on January 29, are expected to continue.


The Serêkaniyê Migrants Committee announced that registration for families wishing to return will continue in Dêrik, Dirbêsiyê, Til Temir, Amûdê, Qamişlo and Hesekê.

title: [Itália] Massenzatico: Acordes Libertários – Festival da Canção Anárquica 2026
content:
ACORDES LIBERTÁRIOS


FESTIVAL DA CANÇÃO ANÁRQUICA 2026


MASSENZATICO (RE) – 2, 3 E 4 DE OUTUBRO DE 2026


Pelo menos numa coisa todos concordam: as canções anarquistas são as mais bonitas!


Do século XIX até hoje, do “sombrio fim do século que se extingue” ao triunfo da inteligência artificial e da crise das esperanças coletivas, passando por todas as resistências e pelo punk, o canto acompanhou as lutas dos anarquistas. “Nossa pátria é o mundo inteiro”, “O amor mantém unidos os afetos naturais”, “Mesmo que vocês se julguem absolvidos, continuam envolvidos”, “Facas para cortar o pão da amizade”… os poetas populares forneceram slogans e ideias ao movimento dos trabalhadores.


A reivindicação de um mundo de justiça social, sem guerras e sem opressões individuais, sempre encontrou o apoio físico dos anarquistas e o acompanhamento de seus cantos. Porque os anarquistas gostam da vida, e qual melhor maneira de vivê-la do que se reunir, cada um com sua própria voz, entre cantos coletivos e contracantos individuais?


É por isso que nos dias 2 (sexta), 3 (sábado) e 4 (domingo) de outubro de 2026 serão realizados três dias dedicados ao canto anarquista.


Acontecerão em Massenzatico, na província de Reggio Emilia: um lugar onde, há muitos anos, os anarquistas se reúnem para uma grande festa convivial centrada na comida – “As Cozinhas do Povo”. Esta também será uma festa para ouvir canções antigas e novas, encantar-se ao som de violões, acompanhar as narrativas de cantadores históricos e modernos, viver a partilha inclusiva dos coros populares.


Distribuídas ao longo dos três dias, alternando momentos de escuta com outros de pura festa, a dimensão física e a poética, essas diferentes formas de expressão musical terão momentos dedicados.


• Os dias serão marcados por debates, aprofundamentos e oficinas.


• Nas tardes, espetáculos e conferências reunirão os cantos com a história e com as histórias dos cantores individuais: cantautores famosíssimos como De André, companheiros históricos como Pietro Gori, figuras do nosso mundo como Paola Nicolazzi.


• O fim das tardes será dedicado a breves apresentações individuais.


• Após o jantar, haverá shows envolventes e momentos de partilha musical entre diversos coros, que entrelaçarão suas vozes com as de todos os participantes.


Uma grande festa da música, sob o signo do pensamento libertário.


O canto anarquista: um fenômeno em certos aspectos indefinível, mas que – assim como a revolução – encontra seu momento no cruzamento entre a alegria da participação e a libertação dos tabus e das correntes.


Marquem essa importante iniciativa na agenda: 2, 3 e 4 de outubro de 2026. Primeiro Festival da Canção Anarquista.


CIRCOLO ARCI CUCINE DEL POPOLO – CIRCOLO ARCI CAPANNINA / PARADISA

20 e 21 de agosto de 2026

 Estes encontros, voltados à classe trabalhadora e a todos os que sofrem com as violações cotidianas, serão conduzidos mediante agendamento prévio, que deverá ser solicitado exclusivamente pelo endereço eletrônico 

uaf@riseup.net

.


É fundamental compreender que esse serviço não se reduz a uma mera assistência burocrática ou a uma tentativa de “ajustar” os companheiros às leis vigentes. Pelo contrário, a UAF encara o Direito como mais um campo de batalha — um espaço onde o Estado exerce sua violência simbólica e material para perpetuar a exploração e a desigualdade. Portanto, nossa atuação jurídica busca desvelar as contradições do ordenamento legal, oferecendo suporte prático para que os oprimidos possam resistir às investidas do sistema, sem jamais perder de vista que a verdadeira emancipação só virá com a superação radical dessa ordem.


A União Anarquista Federalista se constitui, assim, como um importante ponto de luta organizada contra o 

Estado

, a 

democracia burguesa

capitalismo

. Não nos iludimos com as falsas promessas de igualdade perante a lei, pois sabemos que o judiciário, os parlamentos e as demais instituições políticas servem, acima de tudo, aos interesses das elites econômicas e à manutenção dos privilégios de classe. No entanto, enquanto a revolução social não se concretiza, entendemos que é nosso dever fortalecer a solidariedade prática, utilizando todas as ferramentas disponíveis — incluindo o conhecimento técnico-jurídico — para desgastar as engrenagens do sistema, proteger nossos militantes e garantir que os trabalhadores e as trabalhadoras não sejam esmagados impunemente pela máquina estatal.


Convidamos, portanto, todxs xs companheirxs que se sintam encurralados pelo poder público ou explorados pelas relações capitalistas a nos procurarem, assim como já vêm fazendo, fortalecendo os laços de confiança e reciprocidade. uaf@riseup.net

title: [Espanha] A história de Jacinto Toryho, o anarquista com várias vidas
content:
José Miguel Fernández Barreira publica um livro sobre a trajetória pessoal e política de um dos referenciais do anarquismo e do jornalismo libertário nos anos 30, nascido em Villanueva del Campo | Foi ele quem popularizou o hino “A las barricadas”


Por 

Manuel Herrera

 | 01/07/2026


Jacinto Torío Rodríguez nasceu em primeiro de fevereiro de 1909 em Villanueva del Campo, no canto nordeste da província de Zamora. Cerca de 25 anos depois, ele se tornara um dos referenciais do movimento anarquista na Espanha e do jornalismo libertário. Como ele chegou até lá? A vida deste homem, que adaptou seu sobrenome para Toryho durante a juventude, é o objeto do novo livro de José Miguel Fernández Barreira (Ermua, 1973). Trata-se de reconstruir os passos de um tipo que foi protagonista de várias vidas.


A primeira, na Tierra de Campos do início do século XX. “Pelos poucos escritos que temos sobre sua infância, provenientes de alguns artigos de imprensa, tudo indica que ele pertencia a uma família de rendeiros do campo. Na verdade, quando ele era pequeno, a Justiça foi penhorar a colheita de seu pai e foi ali que ele sentiu a raiva pela primeira vez, embora intuamos que a situação da família foi melhorando com o tempo”, destaca Fernández Barreira. De fato, Toryho pôde estudar. Primeiro, no colégio dos Padres Agostinianos de Valencia de Don Juan; depois, no seminário de Valderas.


Sim, no seminário. Apesar de sua trajetória posterior, foi por ali que começou a assumir as rédeas de sua vida adulta um homem que acabou fugindo do centro religioso após alegar que lhe haviam acontecido “coisas terríveis”. Seja como for, a qualidade de seus textos escritos, já naquela época publicados na imprensa local como o El Heraldo de Zamora, permitiu-lhe conseguir acesso – provavelmente por meio de uma bolsa de estudos – à escola de jornalismo do El Debate, em Madri.


Naquela época, no amanhecer dos anos trinta do século passado, Toryho escrevia muito influenciado pelo “azar do camponês”, segundo relata Fernández Barreira, que destaca o “conteúdo social” dos artigos do zamorano. Na verdade, o já jornalista logo se vinculou ao agrarismo, um movimento que defendia a libertação das pessoas do campo. Foi nesse contexto que a chegada da II República o pegou, um regime que ele defendeu em seu nascimento.


No entanto, pouco tempo depois, Toryho ficou decepcionado com a deriva do agrarismo. Ficara para trás o sonho do zamorano de ver os camponeses sentados no Parlamento. Foi então que o tom “antipolítico” do anarquismo começou a atrair um homem que mudou de sobrenome e que começou a se integrar no movimento libertário em sua esfera pessoal e no ofício. A partir de 1932, começou a colaborar com o Solidaridad Obrera, um jornal do qual foi correspondente em Madri.


Dessa posição, Toryho cobriu para a imprensa da época acontecimentos como os Sucessos de Casas Viejas. “Ele entendia o jornalismo como uma arma de mobilização social”, explica Fernández Barreira, que aponta que o zamorano chegou a ser também cronista parlamentar ou repórter experiente. Como prova disso, aparece uma série com uma dezena de reportagens escritas do manicômio de Ciempozuelos, onde ele se infiltrou para saber como os doentes eram tratados de acordo com a origem de suas famílias.


Com tudo isso, Toryho foi adquirindo um nome dentro do mundinho anarquista. Em Madri, criou as Juventudes Libertárias e de lá foi para Barcelona para continuar trabalhando no jornal a partir de sua sede central. Também nessa época de sua vida, ele é um dos responsáveis pela popularização, dentro do movimento anarquista espanhol, do hino “A las barricadas”. “A tonalidade era de uma canção polonesa, e a letra em castelhano foi adaptada por Valeriano Orobón, segundo várias fontes, a pedido do zamorano.


Na verdade, em sua função posterior como porta-voz dos Escritórios de Promoção e Propaganda durante a Guerra Civil, ele se encarregou de promover a gravação do que mais tarde se tornaria o grande hino da CNT. Antes disso, Toryho também desempenhou um papel relevante na Revolução de 1934, o que o levou de volta a Madri. Naquela altura, ele já compartilhava sua vida com a também jornalista e tradutora Rosa Zimmerman.


Apesar dessa mudança, Toryho não tardou a retornar à Catalunha em 1935. Foi para continuar sua trajetória paralela no jornalismo e na luta social sob a ótica da disciplina orgânica dentro do anarquismo. Essa posição converteu o zamorano em uma figura com detratores dentro da própria …

title: Cin: Framework Law is only a first step
content:
The submission of the framework law to Parliament by the AKP government as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process marked the first step in a new phase. As the public debates the content of the law, one of the issues generating the most curiosity is what kind of regulation will be introduced concerning the return of Kurds who have been living in exile for years.


Kurdish politician Emrullah Cin, who is himself living in exile, served as mayor of Weranşar in the 1994, 2009 and 2014 local elections and was imprisoned for a period following the operations carried out under the name of the KCK. He spoke to our agency about how the law came about and the new period.


The state has taken a legal step


Pointing out that Turkey has taken a step toward addressing the Kurdish issue on a legal basis for the first time, Cin said: “This is happening for the first time after 40 years. Many things had been said before, but in practice there had been no legal effort. If we start with the Özal period and go up to 2015, this is a step being taken now. It is currently on Parliament’s agenda. Today, it is a positive development.”


The Framework Law is a positive step


Pointing out that people in exile are discussing these issues among themselves, Cin continued: “People are discussing and talking about it. There is a significant Kurdish population abroad, especially in Germany, where I live. A large part of the Kurdish community is trying to stand up for its rights, its culture, its national values, and the political process as well... At the very least, they are evaluating it. They see some steps as positive and others as inadequate. There may be a return in this regard, but we need to see the outcome. What does it offer, whom does it cover and whom does it not cover? Another issue is whether Parliament transfers its authority — since the law has not yet been passed, it is difficult to say anything at this stage — to a commission. If Parliament itself follows up on this matter, that would be one thing, because it is Parliament that makes the law. But if it transfers its own authority to another appointed delegation, group or commission, I don't know. That is something that needs to be discussed.


How long will the postponement last? Regardless of the period specified, the postponement could be taken off the agenda or result in a positive outcome with the approval of that commission. But there is also a high possibility that this could have negative consequences. Despite everything, despite all the negative aspects, I view this new step positively.”


Emrullah Cin noted that Kurds have paid a heavy price for more than 40 years and continue to do so, and said: “The Kurdish issue has required a long-term struggle. Kurds have already paid a heavy price for more than 40 years and continue to do so. Neither the problem nor the struggle will end. In my personal view, both in Europe and in the country, this achievement should be embraced with greater motivation and much higher morale.


Whether the first step is an achievement or not needs to be assessed separately, but in terms of its name, I think it is an achievement. I think the next steps can be taken much more easily because a legal basis has been established and a legal path has been found. This is only the first step. Millions of steps can be taken, and I believe positive results will be achieved.”

title: Pressure on women prisoners increases in Iranian jails
content:
According to human rights organisations, pressure by the Iranian regime on women prisoners has increased recently. It was reported that guards in Tehran’s prisons have attacked and subjected prisoners to violence, while some prisoners have been unreachable.


According to a report published on the website Iran Prisoners’ Voice (Dengê Girtiyên Îranê), conditions in Tehran’s prisons have deteriorated recently. It was reported that following attacks in the prisons, contact could not be established with some female and male prisoners. Among those from whom no news could be obtained were Hesen Emîdî and Mucteba.


Yelda Mûîrî sentenced to 16 years in prison


According to a report published by the HRANA news agency, Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced news and documentary photographer Yelda Muîrî to 15 years in prison in absentia.


Muîrî announced in a statement published on a digital platform that she had been sentenced to 15 years in prison. The statement did not provide details about the grounds for the ruling.


New case file opened against Persya Kemalî


A new case file has also reportedly been opened against university student Persya Kemalî, who is being held in Yazd Central Prison.


According to information reported by the website Prisoners’ Voice, Kemalî had previously been sentenced to prison in April 2024 on charges of establishing contact with people opposed to the Iranian authorities.


It was reported that the new case against Kemalî was opened because of an audio message she had published concerning the increase in executions in prisons.


It was also reported that Kemalî has thyroid cancer and has been denied her right to receive medical treatment in prison.

title: CDK-S and YJK-S: Shortcomings in the framework law must be addressed
content:
The Democratic Kurdish Council of Switzerland (CDK-S) and the Swiss Kurdish Women’s Union (YJK-S) issued a joint written statement regarding the “Bill on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration,” which was adopted by the Parliamentary Justice Commission. Describing the legislation as a positive step, the organisations criticised its security-oriented language and the ambiguity surrounding the position of the Kurdish people’s leader.


CDK-S and YJK-S described the adoption of the framework law as an important threshold in terms of resolving the Kurdish issue on a political basis, stating that the legislation provides an opportunity to place the gains of the Kurdish people’s decades-long struggle on a legal footing.


The statement said that, for the first time since the establishment of the Republic, Kurdish demands for rights were being discussed in legal texts, adding: “The Kurds’ demands for rights, albeit cautiously, are now open to discussion outside the cycle of conflict and violence.”


The law has been prepared in a security-oriented language


Pointing out that the law has both positive aspects and causes for concern, the statement noted that the bill had been prepared in security-oriented language and that an attempt was being made to define the Kurdish issue through a security-based approach.


The statement said: “We want it to be known that we categorically reject the continued definition of the honourable struggle waged by the sons and daughters of the Kurdish people as ‘terrorism’ in the bill.”


The organisations also criticised making sentence postponements and other provisions conditional on specific requirements, saying that this approach could allow the mechanism of repression against Kurds to continue.


Öcalan's position must be defined


CDK-S and YJK-S went on to criticise the fact that Öcalan’s position had been left undefined in the legal regulation. The statement said that the Kurdish side’s calls for the law to cover everyone had not been taken into account, and that distinctions such as 2005 and earlier prevented cadres of the Kurdish movement and Öcalan from benefiting from the legislation.


The statement added that Kurds from Kurdistan living in Switzerland regarded the law as a “positive step” despite its shortcomings, and added: “We reiterate our demand that, above all, Öcalan’s position be defined and that he be included in the process on a legal basis as the ‘Coordinator for Peace and Politicisation.’”


The statement also called for the categorising language used during the parliamentary discussions of the law to be changed and for language to be adopted that separates the Kurdish Freedom Movement from the designation of “terrorism.”


Call for regulations to enable the return of Kurds in the diaspora


CDK-S and YJK-S stated that the law should also cover Kurds from Kurdistan living in Europe, particularly Switzerland, and in other countries. The statement said: “Our most important demand is that the law be put into practice in a way that covers all Kurds from Kurdistan who are forced to live in the diaspora, particularly those living in Switzerland, and facilitates their return to the country.”


Öcalan is the chief negotiator


In the final section of the statement, CDK-S and YJK-S said that Öcalan is recognised by the Kurdish people as the chief negotiator and stated that the role Öcalan will assume in implementing the law and continuing the process will also affect the position of Kurds living in Europe.


CDK-S and YJK-S said: “We want it to be known from now that we fully support the process being conducted by our leader and the Kurdish Freedom Movement, and that we will fully support any call they make for a return to the country.”

title: Tahmaz: Despite its shortcomings and flaws, the Framework Law is an important threshold
content:
The long-awaited legislation in the negotiation process aimed at resolving the Kurdish issue, which began with Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan’s February 27 call for peace and a democratic society, has now been introduced. The Framework Law, entitled by the government the “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration” and consisting of 12 articles, has drawn criticism because it contains no steps toward democratization and is limited to a narrow perspective focused on issues such as postponing sentences and laying down arms.


The Framework Law, which was adopted by the Parliamentary Justice Commission after intense debate, is expected to be placed on the agenda of the General Assembly and passed by Parliament today. Speaking to ANF about the Framework Law, Peace Foundation President Hakan Tahmaz said that the law did not meet expectations but represented an important threshold despite its shortcomings and flaws.


We have a law that the parties have agreed on for the first time


Hakan Tahmaz, president of the Peace Foundation, emphasized that the Framework Law, introduced a year and a half after the launch of the Peace and Democratic Society process aimed at resolving the Kurdish issue, does not meet expectations but nevertheless represents an important threshold despite all its shortcomings. Tahmaz said that the Peace Foundation had made its views on the scope of the Framework Law public in July 2026 under the title “Our historic responsibility,” adding: “As the Peace Foundation, we issued a statement on what the scope of the law should be. We see that the law discussed in the parliamentary commission does not address a large part of the issues raised in our statement. But despite all the shortcomings and flaws in the law, we are at an important threshold. At least we now have a law that the negotiating parties have agreed on for the first time. I think we need to work to ensure that this law becomes a reality and is taken forward.”


Assessing the fact that the introductory section explaining the reasoning behind the bill focuses on the organization laying down its arms rather than examining the causes and consequences of the Kurdish issue and presenting perspectives for its resolution, Tahmaz said this was not a surprise from their perspective.


He added they had defined the process as one of disarming the PKK and subsequently bringing the Kurdish issue onto a political and democratic footing, as Abdullah Öcalan had also stated. He continued: “We define this process as the disarmament of the PKK and subsequently, as Abdullah Öcalan has said, bringing the Kurdish issue onto a political and democratic footing. Therefore, the fact that there would be no perspective aimed at resolving the Kurdish issue was already something accepted at the negotiating table.


Now that the parties have agreed on something, we cannot say, ‘No, this won't work.’ At present, the parties are essentially focused not on resolving the Kurdish issue but on the PKK laying down its arms, and that is how we are approaching it. Of course, when we look at it from that perspective, as I said earlier, we see shortcomings and flaws. That is why we do not expect Turkey's democratization to emerge immediately from this process. The parties have first agreed on the PKK laying down its arms, and if this agreement becomes a reality, we will have the opportunity to continue the struggle for democracy in Turkey on a more solid footing,” 


We were expecting a law about laying down arms without conditions


Tahmaz said they had expected the Framework Law to provide for the laying down of arms without distinctions or conditions, but had found that this was not the case. He said: “We knew that this law would not produce democratization, but we were expecting a law on laying down arms without distinctions or conditions. By ‘without distinctions,’ we mean that we do not think it is right for the law to say, ‘these people, these people and these people are excluded from the scope of this law,’ or to impose political conditions in this regard. We also believe that democratization in Turkey is impossible as long as the Anti-Terror Law remains in force. But ultimately, the parties have agreed on this. Abdullah Öcalan has approved it.


As the Peace Foundation, we thought and proposed that the right to hope should also be included in the Framework Law. But today they are saying, ‘No, this is where we will begin.’ We do not object to that. We are …
