author: Unknown
title: Tiryaki: Together we'll implement a model of governing, producing and sharing through municipalities
content:
DEM Party Êlih (Batman) MP and Deputy Co-Chair responsible for Local Government Mehmet Rüştü Tiryaki stressed that countries with strong local governments also have high standards of democracy.


“The more democracy there is at the local level, the more democracy there is in that country. The stronger local governments are, the stronger that country’s democracy is,” Tiryaki said.


 


Tiryaki noted that local government in Turkey has a 150-year history, but said this process had not followed a course in which local democracy became stronger day by day. He stressed that in recent years, the powers of administrative tutelage over local governments had increased. “Local democracy and local governments have never been this weak in the history of this country,” he added.


We have 27 years of experience


Recalling that the DEM Party tradition has 27 years of experience in local government, dating back to 1999, Tiryaki said they had introduced practices during this period that would be written in golden letters in the country’s history. He said practices such as multilingual municipal administration, co-presidency and equal representation had set an example not only for Turkey but for the world.


Tiryaki said they had also made significant progress in the cultural sphere, opening kindergartens providing education in the mother tongue and transforming every municipality into a centre for culture and the arts. He added that they had governed municipalities together with the people. “We made municipalities institutions that belong to our people themselves. We created municipalities whose doors they could open, where they could meet managers at every level and where they could see that these institutions belonged to them,” he said.


Participatory budgeting in six municipalities


Tiryaki said they had recently introduced participatory budgeting, starting in Gımgım (Varto) and Amed’s Rezan (Bağlar) district, and that this year the practice had been expanded to six municipalities. He said it would be implemented in all municipalities in the coming years. He also noted that they organised public meetings in neighbourhoods and determined budget items together with residents.


Tiryaki said they viewed municipalities as communes and communes as municipalities. “We are discussing the principles of governance, production and sharing together with our people. We are talking about governing together with our people, producing together with our people and sharing what we produce. We will work to truly turn our municipalities into centres of the commune,” he said.


He added that, within this framework, they were conducting a broad discussion ranging from cooperatives to the restructuring of governance mechanisms.


The expanding role of local government


Tiryaki said modern municipalities were no longer limited to services such as waste collection, sewage, water, parks and gardens, but had assumed responsibilities across a broad range of areas, from services for people with disabilities and the elderly to culture, the arts, language and literature.


He said there was a strong social demand and a serious struggle both in Kurdistan and in Turkey to strengthen local governments. However, he pointed out that laws adopted in recent years had restricted the powers of local governments, while many decision-making mechanisms had been transferred to the central government.


Solving problems


Mehmet Rüştü Tiryaki said that local governments had assumed an almost central position in Abdullah Öcalan’s proposals concerning the Kurdish issue and the democratisation of Turkey, and continued: “If we can truly resolve the issue of local government in Kurdistan; if we can increase the powers of local governments, remove the reservations attached to international conventions, limit the powers of administrative tutelage, and turn them into governments that draw up their own budgets and make their own decisions, then we will also have resolved the fundamental century-old problem of this country, the issue for which efforts are being made to find a solution within the framework of the discussions on a ‘Peace and Democratic Society.’”


Tiryaki stressed that democratising local governments, abolishing the powers of administrative tutelage and organising municipalities as communes were important areas that could help resolve the country’s two fundamental problems, particularly the Kurdish issue and the problem of democracy.

title: Peter Kropotkin - Den nya internationalen
content:
Författare

: Peter Kropotkin

Titel

: Den nya internationalen

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #53 1916


 Man intreserar sig för ögonblicket mycket för vilken karaktär Internationalen kommer att erhålla, när den efter kriget blir rekonstituerad. Och bland oss anarkister frågar man sig, vad man kan göra för att hjälpa till att skapa en ny International, som kan bli till verklig hjälp för arbetarna i deras befrielsesträvanden och som samtidigt kan förhindra framkallandet av nya krig!


 Denna fråga förtjänar hela vår uppmärksamhet.


 Det är bekant, att det gjorts ansträngningar från tyska socialdemokrater, understödda av deras franska, italienska, holländska etc. trosfränser, för rekonstitueringen av deras international - de socialdemokratiska partiens international, som existerade före kriget.


 Nåväl, det är uppenbart, att denna international, allenast varande en sammanslutning av parlamentariska socialisternas partier, som godkänna den tyska socialdemokratiens program, icke kan motsvara arbetarnas behov, vilka sträva att skapa en internationell organisation av

arbetare,

 en organisation som kan ge internationellt stöd åt arbetarnas direkta kamp mot den kapitalistiska exploateringen på dennas egen mark, i gruvorna, fabrikerna, dockorna, etc., samtidigt som den förbereder internationell enighet inom de omfattande sammanslutningarna av en och samma branch av produktionen, för skapandet av framtida sociala förbund utanför staterna.


 Behovet av sammanslutningar av detta slag, har gjort sig så starkt kännbart de sista tjugo åren före kriget, att de franska, engelska, belgiska arbetarna inom olika branscher, sådana som loss- och lastningsarbetarna, metallarbetarna, etc. ha gjort ständiga ansträngningar för att organisera sig internationellt genom direkt samarbete inom yrket.


 Det gäller därför att skapa en

arbetareinternational

 utan att befatta sig med den

sociala demokratiens uteslutande parlamentariska international.


 Det är dessutom nödvändigt, att denna arbetareinternational icke begränsar sin verksamhet blott till rent professionella frågor om löner och arbetstid, men att den utan omsvep tar fast på frågan om den

sociala omvandlingen.

 Det är på grund av, att man icke fastslagit detta mål som siktpunkt för alla de partiella striderna, som de fackliga och trade-unionistiska organisationerna, som funktionerat under de sista fyratio åren, i glömska av sin verkliga uppgift och

raison d'étre,

 överlämnat sitt huvudsakliga mål åt de parlamentariska "taktikerna", som utskjuter dess förverkligande till en avlägsen framtid.


 Den naturliga kärnan av en arbetareinternational i Europa kommer antagligen att bildas av de franska och italienska fackliga konfederationerna, de engelska trade-unionerna och de olika belgiska, holländska, spanska, skandinaviska, ryska arbetareorganisationerna, till vilka en gång antagligen de tyska och österrikiska organiserade arbetarna komma att ansluta sig. Man måste således fråga sig om dessa olika organisationer erbjuda de nödvändiga elementena för konstituerandet av en sådan international varom vi nyss talas?


 Blott för några år tillbaka hade man måst svara på denna fråga med ett

nej.

 Men under sista tiden har allvarliga förändringar börjat göra sig märkbara i dessa organisationers anda och krigets obarmhärtiga lärdomar har redan bidragit till att vidga arbetarnas syn med avseende på nödvändigheten av en omvandling av samhället på kommunistisk bas.


 Man har sålunda sett hur det inom de engelska yrkesförbunden, vid sidan av de gamla unionerna, trånga och egoistiska, har uppstått nya unioner, sådana som loss- och lastningsarbetarnas, som gjort ett värdefullt arbete för organiserandet av ett internationellt förbund av alla arbetare inom denna bransch. Och inom järnvägsmännens union har man under den stora strejken 1912 sett hur åtskillnaden mellan lokomotivförarnas aristokrati och järnvägarnas demokratiska massa försvunnit.


 Samtidigt kan man iakttaga hur de engelska unionerna icke längre rygga tillbaka för de socialistiska eller ens de kommunistiska idéorna.

Socialiseringen av jorden

 som redan sedan ett trettiotal år tillbaka figurerat på deras program, har fått en ny, praktisk mening sedan kriget har visat faran för ett land, att icke odla sin jord men förlita sig på importen.

Socialiseringen av kolgruvorna,

author: CMI Argentina
title: Protesta en el Congreso: la resistencia popular enfrentó más de tres horas de represión que dejó 1500 heridos y 29 detenidos
content:
El jueves 6 de agosto, una masiva movilización contra la ley de extranjerización de tierras no solo desafió el mal tiempo y la estrategia comunicacional del Gobierno, sino que enfrentó el operativo represivo más extenso de la gestión de Javier Milei. Durante más de tres horas, un despliegue conjunto de fuerzas federales y de la Policía de la Ciudad avanzó en múltiples frentes. En esta nota repasamos los puntos donde se concentró la represión: el inicio en Bartolomé Mitre y Callao con gases lacrimógenos; el avance sobre la protesta en plaza Congreso; el caótico operativo por Avenida de Mayo y sus intersecciones hasta llegar a la 9 de Julio y luego, a la Plaza de Mayo, con efectivos embistiendo desde los costados para acorralar a los manifestantes. El saldo oficial arroja 29 detenidos – ya liberados – y organismos como la CPM registraron al menos 1500 heridos, con casos de traumatismos de cráneo y lesiones oculares por balas de goma.

Una convocatoria masiva pese a todo


La masividad de la protesta es un hecho inapelable.

La concurrencia colmó la plaza del Congreso pese a las tormentas que asomaron desde temprano

 (ver nuestra cobertura de la marcha)

. A esto se suma que el Gobierno había bajado el día anterior la parte de la ley que más resonancia tuvo en los medios de comunicación, los cuales, una vez conocida esta noticia, levantaron el dato como un triunfo para los sectores populares sin resaltar que aún quedaban artículos sustanciales, como el articulado de quema de tierras y desalojos, temas que son muy caros para las comunidades que sostienen recursos naturales, los territorios de pueblos originarios, campesinos y de quienes pagan un alquiler. Pese a todos esos factores, la plaza del jueves se colmó, incluso con la siempre latente amenaza de represión y la fuerte tormenta mediante.


El operativo represivo


El operativo de seguridad fue el habitual para este tipo de movilizaciones en el Congreso: participaron las cuatro fuerzas federales (PSA, PFA, Gendarmería y Prefectura), con la Policía de la Ciudad desplegada por fuera del perímetro de la plaza. Hacia las 17 horas, en la esquina de Bartolomé Mitre y Callao, Gendarmería inició la represión con gases lacrimógenos contra los manifestantes que se encontraban junto a las vallas. La respuesta de los presentes, que no cedieron terreno, derivó en una rápida escalada del operativo: se sumaron balas de goma y el agua a presión de los camiones hidrantes.

author: Unknown
title: Sendikal sıkışmışlığa karşı işçi iradesi
content:
Eskişehir – Odunpazarı Belediyesinde çalışan işçilerin bir süredir gündeminde sendika değişikliği var. Bir yanda yıllardır var olan ancak işçilerin hak arayışında silik bir figür olarak kalan yetkili sendika, diğer yanda yeni kurulan “bağımsız” bir yapı ve alanı boş bırakmamaya çalışan alternatif iddialar… İşçiler için asıl ihtiyaç kimin en doğrusu olduğunu seçmek değil kendi iradelerinin temsiliyetini garanti altına almak.

Yetkili sendika Belediye-İş yöneticileri ve işçiler, belediye yönetiminin işçilere yeni sendika Çağdaş-Sen’e geçmeleri yönünde baskı yapıldığını dillendiriyor. Bu iddianın sahadaki karşılığı ve doğruluk payı göz ardı edilemez. Nitekim yerel yönetimlerin sendikalaşma süreçlerinde bir sendikadan yana taraf olması ya da yönlendirici bir biçimde tutum alması sık rastlanan ve sendikal özgürlüğün altını oyan başlıca unsurlardan.

Ancak meseleye sadece “yönetim baskısı” penceresinden bakmak, tablodaki kimi gerçekleri de ıskalamak anlamına gelir. Çünkü Belediye-İş Sendikasının bugüne kadar sergilediği pratik işçilerin gözünde bu yapının meşruiyetini çoktan tartışmalı hale getirmişti. İşçilerin haberi ve onayı olmaksızın imzalanan Toplu İş Sözleşmeleri (TİS), işten çıkarmalar karşısında sessizliğe bürünmeleri ve işçilerin kadro mücadelesinde gösterilen atalet, hafızalardaki tazeliğini koruyor.

Yıllar boyunca şantiyelerde, park ve bahçelerde görünmeyen, işçinin feryadına ve taleplerine kulak tıkayan bu bürokratik mekanizma şimdi koltuğunu kaybetmenin verdiği endişe sebebiyle sahaya inmiş ve işçileri Belediye İş’te kalmaya ikna etme turlarında. Çağdaş-Sen tehdidi uzun zamandır uyku modunda olan sendika şube başkanını ve yöneticilerini uyandırdı. Lakin bu ani uyanış işçiler nezdinde bir hak arama mücadelesinden ziyade koltuğu bırakmama çabası olarak okunuyor.

Tartışmaların fitilini ateşleyen bağımsız olarak kurulan Çağdaş-Sen ise kurulur kurulmaz işaret edilmişçesine Odunpazarı Belediyesinde örgütlenme yarışına girdi. Hızla şantiyelere inerek, işçilerle temas kurmaya çalışan bu yapı, bir yandan mevcut sendika ile bağını koparmak isteyen işçiler için bir çıkış yolu gibi görünürken diğer yandan arkasındaki “hızlı ve organize” hareket kabiliyetine dair soru işaretleri barındırıyor. İşçiler, yukarıdan tasarlanan ya da birilerinin eliyle yönlendirilen bir yapının işçinin çıkarlarını savunup savunmayacağı konusunda son derece kuşkulu. Çağdaş-Sen ile ilgili konuşan bir işçi örneğin şöyle diyor; “Dillerinde bir laf var Çağdaş Sen’de birlik olalım. Tamam, birlik olalım da ne vaat ediyorsun. Belediye İş’ten farklı olarak ne yapacaksın. Ortada ben bir fark göremiyorum. Kuru kuruya birlik olma çağrısı yapıyorlar. Hangi ilken var, neden sana katılalım buralarda bir açıklamaları yok”

Bu karmaşa yetmiyor olacak ki sahneye çıkmaya çalışan bir diğer aktör de DİSK’e bağlı Genel-İş Sendikası oldu. Odunpazarı işçilerine “Gelin bizde örgütlenin” çağrısı yapan Genel-İş yöneticileri, yaptıkları açıklamada kulağa hoş gelen, sendiakal mücadele ilkelerine dayalı bir söylem benimsiyor. Ancak işçilerin hafızası ve tecrübeleri etiketlerin ötesine geçmeyi zorunlu kılıyor. Ülke genelinde ve yerelde Genel-İş yönetiminin gerek pratiği gerekse işçilerin yaşadıkları sorunları ele alışı olsun, TİS masalarında atılan imzalar olsun Belediye İş’in pratiğinden çok da farklı sayılmaz. Bürokratikleşmiş sendikal anlayış, tabanın iradesini yok sayan merkezi kararlar Genel-İş’in de sıklıkla eleştirildiği alanlar. Dolayısıyla tabela değiştirmek dışında bir karşılığı olmayan bu çağrılarının işçilerin sorunlarını sihirli bir değnek misali dokunup çözemeyeceği aşikâr.

Tüm bu aktörler sahada rekabet ederken Odunpazarı Belediyesi işçileri içerisinde derin bir tedirginlik ve güvensizlik yayılıyor. Hangi sendikanın arkasında duracaklar, hangi sendika kendilerini gerçekten temsil edecek, net bir fikir birliğinden söz etmek mümkün değil. Bir yanda yıllardır belediyede örgütlü olan bürokratik merkez, diğer yanda yeni kurulan ve arkasındaki dinamikler tam olarak çözülememiş bağımsız bir sendika, öte yanda ise iddialı ama pratik sınavı sabıkalı bir başka sendika. Bu sıkışmışlık hali, işçiler arasında kafa karışıklığı yaratırken, asıl kaybedenin yine işçiler olacağı kaygınsı da körüklüyor. Belediye işçileri tepeden inmeyi alışkanlık haline getirmiş bu sendikal zincirlerin arasında adeta öğütülüyor.

Odunpazarı Belediyesi işçileri mevcut tartışmaları ve sendikal rekabeti bir kriz olarak değil, aksine mücadeleci bir sendikal çizgiyi inşa etmek için bir fırsat …

You may not have heard about this latest tax from Trump. That could be because he’s not going through Congress to get it. Also, this scam could get buried in the middle of his many other grifting schemes. Trump is starting a new special subscription service to his social media platform, Truth Social, where big investors will pay $100,000 a month for advance access to Trump posts that can move markets.

This means that the next time Trump posts that he will blow Iran off the map and sends oil prices soaring, the people who paid Trump’s fee will have the opportunity to buy oil futures before the jump. The same story applies on the way down, as when he posts that a deal with Iran’s leaders is imminent.

And the inside information goes well beyond oil prices. He may announce a big military contract with Lockheed or one of his sons’ companies, sending stock prices soaring. Or he could announce a big DEI investigation of Disney or some other Hollywood entertainment company, causing their stock to plummet.

There are an infinite number of ways that Trump Truth Social announcements can move markets. This subscription service allows rich investors around the country to get in on the action.

If it’s not clear how Trump’s scheme amounts to a tax on your 401(k), think more carefully. If Trump’s clients get the jump on a big rise in oil prices, that means that they get the money, not you. This is true even if, like the vast majority of small investors, you are not actively managing your funds.

The person who is managing whatever fund(s) you hold will pay the higher price for oil or stock or anything else the funds might buy because Trump’s accomplices got their first. The same applies on the way down. The fund will get less money because the Trump gang already sold the stock before your fund manager had the chance to do so.

At this point, we can’t know how much money is involved because we don’t know how many big investors are prepared to sign up for what is blatantly an insider trading scheme. But we can do some speculation.

First, we need to calculate how much money an investor would expect to make from a service where they are paying $1.2 million a year. Since this scheme would likely lead to civil and possibly criminal charges if the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) or Justice Department ever gets taken over by honest people, it seems a very big payoff would be required.

Any person paying Trump for insider information would need to expect substantial legal bills, and also the possibility of being forced to leave the country or face prison time. (Ask Martha Stewart .) Let’s say the payoff has to be at least 20 to 1, which would mean they would need to earn $24 million a year for their Trump Truth Social subscription to make sense.

Then we need to speculate on how many people are prepared to sign up for Trump’s racket. We know Wall Street is a cesspool, but this level of open corruption is probably too sleazy even for most of the big traders. Still, there could be a 1,000 Trump-loving sewer dwellers who don’t mind being open about their thefts.

In that case, the Trump insiders would be siphoning off $24 billion a year from other investors in the market. That is not huge in the context of a $7.5 trillion budget, but it is larger than many things we have big fights over.

For example, the AIDS program for Africa, which saved tens of millions of lives, and Elon Musk eagerly fed into the wood chopper, cost $6 billion a year. That’s roughly a fourth of Trump’s 401(k) tax. The cost of extending the subsidies in the ACA exchanges, which Trump and the Republicans ended, would have been a bit higher at $27 billion a year.

So, 401(k) holders and other small investors are paying a considerable chunk of money through this “tax” to Trump and his enrolled insiders. As I said, this tax is not going to Congress for approval, but we can assume that all the Republicans in Congress approve of it. If not, Trump would be impeached for such a blatantly illegal scheme, but we know the Republican motto: “If Trump Does It, It’s Good.”

author: Stephen Prager
title: Trump May Be Renewing His Push for Control of Greenland
content:
A Texas oil company with ties to Trump is preparing to drill for oil without permission from Greenland’s government.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

After appearing to back off earlier this year, President Donald Trump this week renewed his threats to seize Greenland . A Saturday report that a Texas oil company with ties to Trump had begun preparing to drill in the Arctic territory without permission has raised fresh concerns that his push for control of the island may already be moving beyond rhetoric.

As The Guardian reported , Greenland’s government issued a “strong warning” last week after learning that a Texas oil company called Greenland Energy had begun making unauthorized preparations for oil extraction in Jameson Land, a remote area of eastern Greenland, including bringing drilling materials ashore.

The company, founded last year, has claimed that Jameson Land may contain $1 trillion worth of crude oil and announced plans to drill two wells there — a project that requires approval from Greenland’s government.

Has Trump’s invasion of Greenland already begun? An American oil company connected to Donald Trump is preparing to sink wells in remote Greenland despite not having received permission from the local authorities. https://t.co/12w064lknY

The company also has ties to several Trump allies and associates. According to The Guardian :

Greenland Energy has retained Phil McGraw, better known as Dr. Phil, a prominent right-wing former chatshow host who served on Trump’s religious freedom commission, to make a documentary series that will “capture the mission of these modern-day wildcatters.”

It has also appointed as a director a US Navy veteran who is working on Golden Dome, the missile defense plan for which Trump says controlling Greenland is “vital.”

Larry Swets, Greenland Energy’s chair and a big shareholder, appears to enjoy access to Trump’s circle. He has said the oil project is “not related to American annexation.”

A Greenland Energy representative falsely claimed in June that the company had permission to place equipment on Jameson Land, before later saying there had been confusion.

But the following month, residents saw a barge arrive with drilling equipment. A Danish outlet confirmed that the delivery was intended for Greenland Energy.

Following the delivery, Greenland’s government said on July 30 that the company “did not have the necessary approvals from the mineral resources authority” and would receive a warning that “all future logistical matters must be advised and approved by the mineral resources authority—before they are carried out.”

Two days later, Trump posted an ominious digitally altered image to Truth Social depicting himself as a giant looming over a Greenlandic town, captioned “Hello, Greenland!”

A day earlier, Trump had appeared on the right-wing network Real America’s Voice, where host Steve Gruber reminded him that he had predicted Greenland would be under US control by the time he leaves office in 2029.

“You’ll be right,” Trump replied. “Greenland is important. Not from their standpoint, from our standpoint. You should make that bet.”

Before this week’s comments, Trump had spoken far less publicly about Greenland since January, when he threatened to use military force to take over the island if Denmark did not cede it. To pressure NATO allies, Trump threatened steep tariffs on several European countries, but backed off after Europe pledged retaliatory tariffs, causing panic in the financial markets .

President Trump just posted, "Hello, Greenland!" 👋 So… when is it happening? 😉 pic.twitter.com/gs4jRH7ZIS

“Let nobody think Trump has given up on taking Greenland,” said John O’Brennan, professor of European politics at Maynooth University in Ireland. He added that Greenland Energy’s unauthorized activity “is the latest act of lawlessness his acolytes are engaged in.”

Kenneth Roth, the former executive director of Human Rights Watch, responded to the story by asking , “Has Trump’s invasion of Greenland already begun?”

Historian Ruth Ben-Ghiat suggested it was possible. “Invasions,” she said, “often start with ‘technical’ projects that justify the presence of operatives and ‘technical experts’ who are also doing recon and advance prep.”

title: Bilgesu Erenus Nakkaştepe'de toprağa verildi
content:
5 Ağustos 2026 Çarşamba günü, 83 yaşında aramızdan ayrılan Erenus için ilk uğurlama töreni Harbiye Muhsin Ertuğrul Sahnesi'nde düzenlendi. Törene ailesi, yakınları, sanatçılar, tiyatro emekçileri ve çok sayıda seveni katıldı.


Bilgesu Erenus hayatını kaybetti


5 Ağustos 2026


Tören, Bilgesu Erenus'un yaşamı ve çalışmalarını anlatan kısa bir video gösterimiyle başladı.


İstanbul Şehir Tiyatroları Genel Sanat Yönetmeni Ayşegül İşsever, konuşmasında Erenus'un "yalnızca üretken bir sanatçı değil, toplumsal sorunlar karşısında sorumluluk üstlenen cesur bir aydın" olduğunu vurguladı. Erenus'un eserlerinin yeni kuşaklarla buluşmaya devam ettiğini belirten İşsever, özellikle 5 yıldır kapalı gişe sahnelenen Yaftalı Tabut oyununun sanatçının kalıcı mirasının önemli örneklerinden biri olduğunu söyledi.


Oğlu Ali Erenus ise annesini yaşamı boyunca ezilenlerin, emekçilerin ve hak arayanların yanında duran bir aydın olarak anlattı. Bilgesu Erenus'un hiçbir zaman kişisel çıkar uğruna ilkelerinden ödün vermediğini belirten Ali Erenus, sanatçının yalnızca eserleriyle değil, yaşamı ve duruşuyla da çok sayıda insana ilham verdiğini dile getirdi.


Toplumun aydınlarına onlar yaşarken sahip çıkılması gerektiğini vurgulayan Erenus, annesine "Bana sesi, sözü ve insanların ruhuna giden yolu aydınlatan ışığı verdin" sözleriyle veda etti.


Toplumcu sanat dünyasında iz bıraktı 


1943'te Bilecik'te doğan Bilgesu Erenus, tiyatro, sinema ve müzik alanlarında uzun yıllar çalıştı ve eser verdi. Eserlerinde ağırlıklı olarak emek ve emekçiler, toplumsal eşitsizlikler, kadınların yaşamı ve demokrasi mücadelesini ele aldı. Özellikle Yaftalı Tabut, Misafir ve çeşitli senaryo çalışmalarıyla toplumcu sanat geleneğinin ilgi çeken şahsiyetleri  arasında yer aldı.


Şair Müştak Erenus’un eşi ve müzisyen Ali Erenus’un annesi olan

Bilgesu Erenus

, Kadıköy Kız Koleji'nden mezun olduktan sonra, bir süre hukuk fakültesinde ve konservatuvarda eğitim aldıktan sonra İstanbul Üniversitesi Gazetecilik Enstitüsü'nü bitirdi. 


1965-1973 arasında TRT'de çalışan Erenus, tiyatro, roman ve öyküleriyle tanındı.


Toplumsal meseleleri, emek, göç, kadın ve insan haklarını sahneye taşıyan Erenus'un oyunları, Türkiye dışında da çeşitli tiyatrolarda sahnelendi ve farklı dillere çevrildi.


Kaleme aldığı oyunlar Devlet Tiyatroları, Ankara Sanat Tiyatrosu ve Dostlar Tiyatrosu gibi önemli topluluklar tarafından sahnelendi. 

Yaftalı Tabut

, Misafir, El Kapısı, Ortak, Kelaynaklar, Güneyli Bayan ve Acılar Şenliği en bilinen yapıtları arasındaydı. Halide, Böyle Bir Dünya, Göz, Gece ve Kırmızı Karaağaç da Erenus'un ilgi gören kitapları arasındaydı. 

Erenus, toplumsal etkinliklerde yaptığı konuşmaların yanı sıra, gitarı eşliğinde seslendiği şarkılarla da toplumsal muhalefetin ön saflarında yer aldı.

title: Güneş panellerinin açıyla durmasının bir sebebi var
content:
Son yıllarda çatılarda, tarlalarda ve binaların cephelerinde sıkça karşılaştığımız güneş panelleri dikkatinizi çekmiş olabilir: Bu paneller hiçbir zaman yere tamamen paralel (düz) veya dik şekilde yerleştirilmez. Belirli bir eğimle monte edilen panellerin bu duruşu yalnızca mimari bir tercih değil; arkasında fizik, coğrafya ve mühendislik kurallarının yattığı kritik bir hesaplamaya dayanıyor.

Güneş enerjisi sistemlerinin temeli, güneşten gelen fotonların panellere dik açıya yakın bir şekilde temas etmesine dayanır. Güneş ışınları bir yüzeye ne kadar dik (90 derece) vurursa, birim alana düşen enerji miktarı ve buna bağlı olarak üretilen elektrik o kadar yüksek olur.

Dünya’nın eksen eğikliği ve küresel yapısı nedeniyle güneş ışınları yeryüzüne hiçbir zaman tamamen dik bir açıyla sabit kalmaz. Panelleri belirli bir açıyla eğmek, gün içinde ve mevsimler boyunca gelen ışınları mümkün olan en dik açıya yaklaştırır.

Bir bölgedeki ideal panel açısı doğrudan o bölgenin coğrafi enlemine bağlıdır. Örneğin, Ekvator'a yakın bölgelerde paneller neredeyse düz sayılabilecek kadar düşük açılarla yerleştirilirken, kutuplara doğru gidildikçe panellerin eğim açısı belirgin şekilde artar. Türkiye gibi orta kuşak ülkelerinde ise paneller genellikle 30 ila 35 derece arasında bir eğimle monte edilir.

Güneş kış aylarında gökyüzünde daha alçak bir yörünge izlerken, yaz aylarında yükselir. Sabit panellerde bu durum göz önüne alınarak yıllık ortalama en yüksek verimi sağlayacak açı optimize edilir.

Panellerin eğimli olmasının son derece pratik ve biyolojik/çevresel bir nedeni daha vardır: Temizlik.

Tamamen düz yerleştirilen panellerin üzerinde yağmur suyu birikir; toz, polen, kuş pislikleri ve yapraklar panel yüzeyinde çamur tabakası oluşturur. Belirli bir eğim (genellikle en az 10–15 derece) sayesinde yağmur suları paneller üzerinden kayarak akar ve biriken tozu yıkayıp götürür. Temiz bir panel, kirli bir panele göre yüzde 15 ila yüzde 25 daha fazla enerji üretir.

Kış aylarında panellerin üzerinde biriken kar, hücrelerin güneşle temasını keserek elektrik üretimini tamamen durdurabilir. Eğimli panellerde kar kütlesi yerçekiminin etkisiyle kayarak dökülür. Ayrıca, birden fazla panel dizisinin bulunduğu santral sahalarında ön sıradaki panellerin arka sıradakileri gölgelemesini engellemek için ideal açı hesaplamaları hayati önem taşır.

author: Anna Maria Barry-Jester
title: Trump’s Foreign Aid Priority? Investigating Crime Against White South Africans
content:
Other proposed grant recipients include a British organization fighting to keep gay conversion therapy legal.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Since he returned to office, President Donald Trump’s administration has upended foreign aid. It’s labeled well-established, long-running programs as “ not aligned with American interests ” and slashed their budgets.

Still, the billions of taxpayer dollars Congress has allocated for foreign aid programs must be spent; lawmakers have insisted the government continue to fund humanitarian aid, global health and pro-democracy causes around the world. With most of the old programs now gone, however, we wanted to know: What is the Trump administration doing with that money now?

Recently, we published our investigation that found one answer to that question in a little-known bureau of the State Department that has dramatically transformed under Trump. For decades, the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights and Labor, known as DRL, has supported  human rights in some of the most oppressive countries in the world. Now, our reporting found,  it’s planning to direct funds to controversial groups supporting right-wing causes in Europe and elsewhere.

Our full story lays out some of the groups the government has considered funding, which include a British free-speech organization that has fought against bans on “gay conversion therapy” and a British American think tank created this year to focus on “existential threats to Britain, to America, and to our shared Judeo-Christian civilisation.” (Administration officials dropped that grant after significant pushback from Congress.)

One proposed grant particularly caught our attention: Trump administration officials suggested funding research on crime against minority populations in South Africa.

It’s clear from sources we spoke with that the key targeted minority population in question is the white ethnic group known as Afrikaners. Afrikaners were responsible for creating the nation’s infamous and brutal racially segregated apartheid system. Previously, DRL staff had been told to begin the process of awarding funds to a group called Lex Libertas, which was founded by a controversial figure who has called for Afrikaner self-governance . The group is currently fundraising to place 3,000 white crosses on the National Mall in remembrance of attacks on South African farmers.

The proposed grant was later opened up to allow a broader set of invited groups to apply for $1 million of funding, though it is still intended for the same purpose, according to people with knowledge of the process. The State Department declined to say whether Lex Libertas will be among those invited to compete, citing ongoing deliberations, but said the Trump administration has serious concerns about the human rights situation in South Africa that need to be addressed. Lex Libertas did not respond to questions about the organization or the proposed grant.

Former diplomats who have worked extensively on human rights told us they were shocked that the victimization of white South Africans would be prioritized over the serious issues elsewhere in the region.

“It’s laughable to suggest that on the African continent, the prime issue of human rights concern is whites in South Africa,” one former agency official said when we asked him about the grant. South Africa is plagued by violence, but extensive research has found that white South African farmers are not victims of crime at higher rates than other groups.

Experts also described the proposed grant to fund research into violence against Afrikaners as keeping with the Trump administration’s overall stance toward South Africa.

For decades, the U.S. relationship with the country has been symbolized by our massive support for HIV care, Mattie Webb, a professor at the Virginia Military Institute who studies South Africa and U.S. foreign policy, told us.

Since Trump returned to office, there’s been a stark shift as the administration has strengthened ties with borderline white nationalist groups that are considered fringe in South Africa.

“The U.S. is very clearly shifting its priorities away from aid that would benefit far more people in South Africa to this narrow focus on the white minority,” Webb said.

author: Candice Norwood
title: With Blanche Confirmed as AG, Epstein Survivors Say DOJ Continues to Fail Them
content:
“We have tried countless times to engage the DOJ, and they’ve had absolutely no interest,” said one survivor.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Every minute of every day, Liz Stein has to relive the worst thing that’s ever happened to her. She does it during news interviews and when meeting lawmakers on Capitol Hill to demand justice for herself and other survivors of the late disgraced financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

And she’s had to do it throughout the attorney general confirmation process for Todd Blanche , a man who rose from being President Donald Trump’s criminal defense lawyer to the top official overseeing the U.S. Department of Justice. Blanche has served as deputy attorney general, the No. 2 at DOJ, since March 2025. He then became acting attorney general in April after Trump fired his predecessor , Pam Bondi, and officially nominated him to oversee the department in June.

Since that time, Stein and her fellow survivors have consistently urged senators to vote against Blanche’s confirmation, arguing that he has shown no urgency or concern with expanding the Epstein investigation. Despite some initial pushback from two Republican members of the Senate Judiciary Committee, Blanche cleared that first hurdle to advance to a full Senate vote, in part by meeting with survivors — something he’d previously declined to do.

Republican Sens. Susan Collins, who is in a tough re-election race in Maine, and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska then announced that they would join Democrats in voting against Blanche, raising the tension heading into the final vote. With last-minute support from GOP Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, the Senate confirmed Blanche, 50-49, early Saturday morning.

Stein told The 19th that just last year she felt momentum toward accountability growing, driven by public outrage from across the political spectrum and the Epstein survivors’ decision to step into the national spotlight as a unified group calling for transparency. However, Blanche’s confirmation crystalizes another feeling for Stein: “It feels like the DOJ is weaponizing this case for political reasons, and it feels like we’re the pawns being used in that game,” she told The 19th .

That momentum feels stagnant for now, Stein said, but she wants people to know that it won’t be a deterrent. “I think that every attempt the Department of Justice has made to make us go away has not worked,” she said. “We’re not going away.”

The Epstein cloud has hung over the Trump administration since the president began his second term, and included a series of perceived missteps by Bondi that drew criticism from both Democrats and Trump’s base.

In February 2025, Bondi claimed in interviews that her office would be releasing new documents tied to Epstein that would make people feel “sick,” and stated that she had a list of Epstein’s clients sitting on her desk. At a White House meeting the same month, she handed out binders to a group of right-wing social media influencers that contained no new information.

By July 2025, DOJ had released a memo stating it “did not uncover evidence that could predicate an investigation against uncharged third parties.” Trump supporters began to weigh in. Podcaster Joe Rogan, who boasts an average of about 11 million listeners and viewers per episode, accused the administration of “trying to gaslight” the public about how much information it had on the Epstein case.

For Stein, DOJ’s “nothing to see here” attitude has been a constant. In September 2025, the human trafficking specialist and a group of about a dozen other survivors gathered publicly for the first time, standing in front of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. They called for investigations into Epstein’s associates, no presidential pardons or concessions for Maxwell and a full release of the Epstein files — documents and images capturing his personal relationships, business dealings and crimes.

Survivors advocated for the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which became law in November 2025, and required the department to publish unclassified records and communications related to the investigation and prosecution of Epstein. Between December 2025 and March 2026, the department released hundreds of thousands of documents, photos and videos tied to Epstein.

title: Liegenddemo in Hamburg heute - Gedenken an die Verstorbenen.
content:
NDR: Long Covid und ME/CFS: Betroffene demonstrieren in Hamburg


Stand: 08.08.2026 15:16 Uhr


Atemnot, Herzrasen und Müdigkeit sind nur einige Symptome, unter denen Menschen mit einem postakutem Infektionssyndrom (Post Acute Infection Syndrome - PAIS) leiden. Eine Heilung ist bisher nicht in Sicht, obwohl seit Jahren daran geforscht wird. Am Samstag demonstrierten Betroffene in Hamburg für eine bessere medizinische Versorgung.


Laut Veranstalter nahmen etwa 150 Menschen an der sogenannten Liegenddemo vor dem Universitätsklinikum Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE) teil. Zu den Betroffenen von PAIS gehören unter anderem ME/CFS- und Long-Covid-Patienten. Deutschlandweit sollen an Long Covid rund 1,5 Millionen Menschen erkrankt sein. Wie viele es in Hamburg sind, ist unklar.

author: Rizomatica
title: Detienen violentamente a dos miembros del Lof Antonio Panitrur en Bajo Malleco
content:
«Mediante violento procedimiento y con fuerte contingente policial fue detenido el Peñi Adan Huentecol Neculpan y el Peñi Dagoberto Soto Neculpan, ambos miembros de la comunidad Mapuche Antonio Panitrur, de la zona del bajo Malleko.


La detención de los peñi se produce en momentos que ambos trabajaban en reparar los caminos interiores de la comunidad, hasta donde llegan un fuerte contingente de carabineros, los que sin mediar con ellos, lo comienzan a golpear y posteriormente los detienen, y los trasladan hasta la comisaría de Collipulli. dónde quedaron retenidos hasta mañana sábado cuando serán pasados a control de detención en el tribunal de Collipulli.


Cómo comunidad Antonio Panitrur, consideramos que estas prácticas abusivas, responden a la medidas de amedrentamiento policial y persecución política del racista gobierno de José Antonio kast.


La comunidad Antonio Panitrur, acompañó hasta altas horas de la noche a la familia en la comisaria, con la finalidad de conocer el estado de salud de los peñi. Quienes presentan  lesiones evidentes de la golpiza que propinaron a ambos.


La detención según lo informado por carabineros, se dió por tener orden de detención pendiente del año 2019 en caso del peñi Adan Huentecol Neculpan, mientras que el peñi Dagoberto Soto Neculpan fue detenido por maltrato a obra de carabineros.


Hacemos un llamado a distintas comunidades Mapuche de la zona, para que nos puedan acompañar mañana en su control de detención.


Comunica: Lof Antonio Panitrur Wallmapu


Bajo Malleko. 7 de agosto 2026″.

Radio Kurruf

title: “I don’t want to die without seeing peace”
content:
When the hamlet of Birezayna, near the village of Temiran (Demirli), was burned down in the 1990s, İhsan Bayram and the other residents were forced to watch. Turkish soldiers lined up the villagers and made them witness the destruction of their homes. More than three decades later, the now 85-year-old man has returned to live in his village. He has lost much; family members, his homeland, and countless years of his life. Yet one wish remains: to live long enough to see peace.


“Every day I think about peace and about the return of those who were forced to leave,” Bayram said. “I hope I live long enough to see those days.”


A life in the shadow of war and displacement


İhsan Bayram’s story reflects the experience of many families in Kurdistan. Fifteen members of his extended family joined the PKK and lost their lives. Four other relatives, including his son, are currently in prison. One of his nephews was the victim of a political murder that remains unsolved to this day.


Bayram himself also spent 15 months in prison. In 2008, he was arrested along with numerous relatives following an explosion. While he was later released, his son Neytullah Bayram and his nephew Murat Yıldeniz were convicted in the same case and sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment. Yet, according to Bayram, his most painful memories go back much further.


“They brought me home every day and came back for me the next morning”


Bayram recalls that before the 1990s, his family made a living from livestock farming. There was a shortage of water, he said, but not of security. That changed completely with the escalation of the conflict in Kurdistan.


“They labeled us as terrorists. Altogether, I spent about seventy days in detention and was tortured. Every day they brought me back home, and the next morning they came to take me away again. Over and over. They did everything forcing us to abandon our village.”


In addition to torture, the villagers were subjected to threats and extrajudicial killings, Bayram said. He himself narrowly escaped death on several occasions.


“They wanted to kill me. Instead, after torturing me, they left me lying in front of my house until they came back again.”


When the village went up in flames


Eventually, Birezayna was destroyed. Bayram still vividly remembers the day when the villagers were forced to watch the destruction of their homes.


“They lined us all up and burned our houses before our eyes. Anyone who spoke was threatened with death. Columns of smoke were rising from villages everywhere.”


In the spring of 1994, the residents were loaded onto tractors and forcibly displaced—first to nearby villages and later to the city.


Alone in a destroyed village


Not long afterward, Bayram returned. Very little of his village remained. For three years, he lived there alone—without electricity, with almost no infrastructure, and surrounded by the ruins of the burned homes.


He was later displaced once again and relocated to the village of Seyrek, but he did not stay there.


“I couldn’t live anywhere else. This was my homeland.”


When Bayram eventually returned to Birezayna permanently, other families gradually followed. Slowly, the village began to come back to life. Even today, however, it still lacks basic infrastructure and public services. Electricity has since been restored, but access to water and roads remains a major problem.


“We are not asking for an apology, we are asking for peace”


Despite everything he has endured, Bayram says he remains hopeful about the current Peace and Democratic Society Process.


“Of course, I still have concerns. But if the state also does its part, then we can truly speak of peace.”


He says that people in the villages have paid a heavy price.


“We lost our children. We lost our property. We were driven from our homeland. Yet today we are not saying, ‘Apologize to us.’ We are saying, ‘Take a step toward peace.’ No more people should die.”


“I hope I live long enough to see those days”


At the age of 85, Bayram is focused less on the past than on what the future might bring.


“For decades, I have lived with the hope of peace. So much blood has been shed, so much suffering has taken place. This process must end in peace.”


He is especially moved by the thought of those who remain far from their homeland or are still in prison.


“I dream of the day when the guerrillas return and the prisoners are released. Every day I ask myself: Will I live to see that …

author: Ohood Nassar
title: I Saw Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya Save Lives. Now Israel Is Holding Him Hostage.
content:
Israel forced Abu Safiya to choose between his own safety and caring for his patients. He chose his patients.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya is not only the director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza; he is one of the medical voices that brought the suffering of patients and the wounded to the rest of the world. He has dedicated his own life to saving the lives of others and caring for children and patients. He refused to leave Gaza even amid Israeli attacks, choosing instead to remain beside his patients and medical team.

But now Abu Safiya has been imprisoned by Israeli authorities since his arrest on December 27, 2024 . International organizations, including Amnesty International, have called for Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya’s immediate release, while Physicians for Human Rights Israel has repeatedly raised alarm over his detention conditions and warned that his life is in imminent danger.

I first met Abu Safiya at the beginning of February 2024 when I visited Kamal Adwan Hospital. I entered the pediatric intensive care unit, where several premature babies were receiving treatment. Their health conditions were critical, and they were suffering from malnutrition.

I saw Abu Safiya moving between the hospital departments. He appeared anxious and exhausted as he asked one of the nurses to search for formula specifically needed for premature infants.

I asked him whether this milk was available in the markets. He told me that throughout northern Gaza, it was unavailable, and if found, it was extremely difficult to obtain and could cost more than 280 Israeli shekels (around 80 U.S. dollars at the time), a price beyond the ability of families and the Ministry of Health to afford under the circumstances.

At that time, I told him that a friend abroad — with whom I had worked before the war in writing, translation, and website management — wanted to provide $1,000 in aid, and he asked me to find those who needed it most.

Although all of northern Gaza was facing severe shortages of food, medicine, and humanitarian assistance, I decided to direct this support to the children suffering inside Kamal Adwan Hospital.

When I handed the money to Abu Safiya, he asked a nurse, Ahmed Al-Kahlout, to help distribute it. Al-Kahlout refused to take the money, and instead said he would accompany me personally to distribute it among the families most in need. He insisted that the parents should see who was providing the assistance and express their gratitude, and added that he would guide me to the families who needed it most.

Al-Kahlout spoke about the suffering of children due to malnutrition. “Because of the famine and the lack of available milk, we have been burying nearly eight children every day for the past month. But the limited media coverage means the world does not know about it,” he told me.

After distributing the assistance, I met Abu Safiya again. He told me that he documented the hospital’s situation daily, including the lack of medical supplies, the suffering of patients and the wounded, and the repeated attacks on the hospital. He said he continued trying to deliver these messages to the world despite the risks and direct threats he and the medical staff faced.

As the hospital came under repeated attacks and a prolonged siege, Abu Safiya became one of the few people documenting the collapse of health care in northern Gaza. Through frequent messages and statements shared with journalists, he described the growing number of wounded, the lack of essential supplies, and the danger facing patients and medical teams. His appeals were not only medical warnings but urgent calls for international action.

Months later, I returned to Kamal Adwan Hospital in September 2024 to interview Abu Safiya again. I saw him as he always was: walking through the departments wearing his medical uniform, with his stethoscope around his neck. I never saw him sitting in his office; he was always among patients and medical staff.

I asked him about the conditions of patients, the availability of medicines, and the hospital’s ability to continue operating. He answered all my questions and emphasized the importance of telling the world about what patients and medical workers were experiencing.

The last time I saw Abu Safiya, he was in good health. He was wearing his medical uniform, walking through the hospital corridors, and continuing his work without …

author: Brett Wilkins
title: New Mexico Court Fines Meta $567 Million for Harming Kids
content:
The company’s total fines for exposing children to exploitation and harming their mental health now top $1 billion.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation .

A New Mexico court on Thursday ruled that Meta must pay an additional $567 million fine on top of the $375 million a jury fined the tech giant in March for harms caused to teens and children who use its Instagram and Facebook social media platforms.

First Judicial District Judge Bryan Biedscheid said in his 68-pager ruling that “significant numbers of people in New Mexico experience harm from Meta’s products due to risks of sexual exploitation, interference with education, and adverse mental health outcomes.”

“The harm to the impacted New Mexicans is not doubtful, eventual, or contingent, but an immediate, temporally connected, and highly probable result of Meta’s actions,” he continued.

“The youth mental health crisis has inflicted significant and widespread harm in New Mexico in terms of the number of youth suffering mental health harms, the profound suffering they and those in their families suffer, and the resulting interferences with the functioning of the schools, law enforcement, [and] healthcare systems in New Mexico,” the judge added.

The case centered on allegations that Meta knowingly designed and operated Facebook and Instagram in ways that exposed children to harmful content, encouraged excessive use, and failed to adequately protect minors from exploitation. New Mexico officials argued that internal company knowledge and outside warnings showed Meta was aware of risks associated with its platforms but did not act sufficiently to address them.

Most of the new fine — $420 million — will go toward funding youth treatment services, while the rest is designated for awareness and prevention, screening services, and other costs.

Biedscheid’s order also compels Meta to make changes to its platforms in New Mexico, including removing “like” counts and only showing them to minors with parental consent, and prohibiting overnight push notifications for users under age 18.

“Regardless of whether it is labeled as an ‘addiction’ or ‘problematic use,’ the evidence at trial proved that design elements, such as autoplay, infinite scroll, ‘like counts,’ and push notifications create a product that, particularly for adolescent users, is highly rewarding psychologically and neurochemically,” he wrote. “As a result, for many, it is irresistibly compelling to start scrolling and very difficult to stop or abstain from its use.”

“In addition,” the judge added, “algorithmic content recommendations can create harmful feedback loops and ‘rabbit hole’ users. Within a similar vein, ‘like counts’… can provide a potentially harmful focus for adolescent users.”

Meta spokesperson Andy Stone said the company would appeal the ruling, claiming: “We work hard to keep people safe on our platforms and have been transparent about the challenges of identifying and removing bad actors and harmful content. We remain confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts.”

New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez hailed the ruling, saying that “Meta built products it knew would fuel addiction, deepen a youth mental health crisis, and expose children to sexual exploitation, then lied to parents and policymakers about the danger. Today, it pays for that choice.”

At Fairplay — a children’s advocacy group — executive director Josh Golin hailed the “landmark ruling” as “the clearest indication yet that the tide is turning when it comes to protecting kids from social media.”

“For the first time, Meta is being compelled by a court to change its dangerous and harmful design,” he continued. “And with so many states lined up to sue Meta and other social media companies, we should expect to see a lot more injunctive relief to make online platforms used by young people safer.”

“This ruling also clearly indicates why families need the Kids Online Safety Act,” Golin added, referring to a controversial bill advanced this week by the Senate Commerce Committee. “The judge said it was up to Congress to address the addictive features on Instagram and other social media platforms. KOSA’s duty of care against compulsive use is the key to ensuring that Meta and other social media companies stop designing for addiction …

title: Bundestag Vice President calls for amnesty for Kurdish activists in Germany
content:
As the peace process between Turkey and the Kurdish PKK is gradually moving forward, German Parliament (Bundestag) Vice President Bodo Ramelow of the Left Party, believes that Germany can also contribute to the process. He calls on the German federal government to introduce an amnesty for Kurdish activists in Germany.


Speaking to

Rheinische Post

, Ramelow said: “The framework law on the peace process, which has now been submitted to the parliament in Ankara, opens new paths toward peace and is a response to the voluntary dissolution of the Kurdish PKK last year.”


He added: “The German federal government should support this process through diplomatic means and must now, just as Turkey intends to do, implement broad and swift amnesty measures for Kurdish activists in Germany.”


Under an amnesty, the state waives the prosecution or punishment of certain offenses. In Ramelow’s view, such a step would represent “a concrete contribution to peace in the region and to safeguarding Kurdish rights and interests.”


The call comes in response to a

framework law

 submitted to parliament by Turkey’s ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP). One of the bill’s stated objectives is to facilitate the reintegration of PKK members into civilian life in Turkey. It also seeks to establish a legal framework for the possible release of convicted PKK members.


“I welcome the fact that the Turkish government now appears ready to take concrete steps toward peace with the Kurdish people in Turkey,” Ramelow said. “It once again underscores the determination of the Kurdish population in Turkey to achieve democratic change and bring the country’s violent past to a definitive end.”

content:

ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖅ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᔨ ᐅᓇ ᐃᓄᒋᐊᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑎᑦᑎᔾᔪᑎ ᐅᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᑎᒍᔭᐅᓯᒪᔪᑦ ᐊᑯᓂᐅᓂᕐᓴᖅ ᑎᒍᔭᐅᓯᒪᕙᖕᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᐅᓯᒪᔫᑉ ᐅᖓᑖᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᖕᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓕᓚᐅᖅᑎᓐᓇᒋᑦ ᑖᒃᑯᐊᓗ ᒪᓐᑐᕆᐊᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓗᑎᒃ ᓅᑕᐅᙱᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐊᐃᒪᔅᒧᑦ, ᑕᐃᑲᓂᓗ ᐊᒥᓱᑦ ᑎᒍᔭᐅᓯᒪᕙᒃᖢᑎᒃ.


ᓗᐊᐃᔭ ᐊᓕᒃᓵᓐᑐ ᐳᕌᓱ-ᕕᐅᕆ, ᑭᒡᒐᖅᑐᐃᔪᖅ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᔨᒥ ᒪᐃᑯᓪ ᑯᕆᐅᒥᓐ, ᑭᐅᓗᒍᑎᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐅᐸᒍᑎᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᖅ ᐊᒃᓱᕉᑎᐅᓇᔭᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᑎᑦᑎᖃᑕᐅᔪᑦ ᐃᓚᐅᔪᓐᓇᙱᓐᓂᕐᓴᐅᓗᑎᒃ.


ᑯᕆᐅ, ᑲᖏᕐᓱᒥᐅᑕᖅ, 2018-ᒥ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᓕᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐃᓄᒋᐊᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᔭᐅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᑎᒍᔭᐅᓯᒫᓪᓚᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐅᓪᓗᕐᓂ ᖁᓕᓂ ᐅᕙᓂ ᓴᓂᑦ ᔨᕉᒻ ᑎᒍᔭᐅᓯᒪᕝᕕᒃᒥ ᒪᓐᑐᕆᐊᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᑰᓚᐅᖅᑎᓐᓇᒍ.


ᐅᓇ ᐃᓄᒋᐊᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑎᑦᑎᔾᔪᑎᐅᔪᖅ ᑭᐅᓗᒍᑎᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ “ᑭᖑᕙᕆᐊᖅᑕᐅᑎᑦᑎᕙᖕᓂᖅ ᐅᓪᓗᐃᑦ ᐱᖓᓱᑦ ᐅᖓᑖᓄᑦ ᒪᓕᒐᕐᓂ ᓱᕋᐃᔾᔪᑎᐅᖕᒪᑦ, ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᐊᖏᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓐᓂᕈᓂ ᓯᕗᓂᐊᒍᑦ,” ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑯᕆᐅᑉ ᐊᑐᕐᓯᒪᔭᖓ ᐊᑐᕐᑕᐅᒡᒍᓪᓗᓂ ᑎᒍᔭᐅᓯᒪᕝᕕᒃᑕᖃᙱᓗᐊᕐᓂᖓᓄᑦ ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥ. ᐱᒋᐊᖅᖢᓂ 2019-ᒥ, 2,400 ᐅᖓᑖᓃᑦᑐᑦ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᐃᓚᐅᓯᒪᓕᕐᑐᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᒃᑐᓂᒃ.


ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖅ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᔨ ᑖᓐᓇ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᑐᐃᓐᓇᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᖓᓂᒃ ᐊᐃᒪᔅᒥ ᓲᖃᐃᒻᒪ ᖃᓂᓐᓂᕐᓴᐅᖕᒪᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᒃᑐᑦ ᓄᓇᖓᓂ, ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᐳᕌᓱ-ᕕᐅᕆ ᐅᐃᕖᑐᑦ ᐊᐱᕐᓱᖅᑕᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᔪᓚᐃ         29-ᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


“ᒪᓕᒐᖅ ᐱᔪᓐᓇᖅᑎᑦᑎᓯᒪᖕᒪᑦ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖅ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᔨᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑐᒃᓴᓂᒃ ᐊᓯᐊᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᑎᑦᑎᔪᓐᓇᖅᖢᓂ ᓈᒻᒪᒐᔭᖅᐸᓐ ᖃᓄᑐᐃᓐᓇᖅ ᐱᔾᔪᑎᒋᔭᐅᔪᓄᑦ,” ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᑭᓯᐊᓂᓕ ᐊᐃᒪᔅᒧᑦ ᐅᐸᖃᑕᐅᔪᒃᓴᓂ ᐊᒥᓱᐃᑦ ᖃᖓᑕᔭᕆᐊᖃᕋᔭᕐᒪᑕ ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥ ᒪᓐᑐᕆᐊᒧᓐ, ᐃᓛᓐᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᓯᓂᒃᑕᕆᐊᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ, ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᑲᕐᕋᓂ 8-ᓂ ᐸᓯᒃᑰᕆᐊᖃᓕᕐᒥᓗᑎᒃ.


ᐊᒥᓱᑦ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᓕᕐᑐᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᒃᑐᓂ ᓈᒻᒪᒃᓴᓚᐅᙱᒻᒪᑕ ᐊᐃᒪᔅᒧ ᓅᑕᐅᓇᓱᒃᑐᒥ ᓲᖃᐃᒻᒪ ᐊᒃᑐᐊᓗᐊᕆᔭᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᕐᔪᐊᕐᒥ ᑎᒍᔭᐅᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᖃᑦᑕᓗᐊᕐᑐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᔪᓐᓇᐅᑎᖏᓐᓂ ᓱᕋᐃᓯᒪᓐᓇᓗᐊᖅᖢᓂ ᐳᕌᓱ-ᕕᐅᕆ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᔪᓚᐃ 10-ᒥ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖅ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᔨᐅᑉ ᒧᕆ-ᐋᓐ ᐸᑭᐊᑦ ᐊᖏᓚᕐᒥᔪᖅ ᑖᓐᓇ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓂᐊᕐᑐᖅ ᓅᑕᐅᒍᓂ ᐊᐃᒪᔅᒧᑦ ᓈᒻᒪᙱᓗᐊᕋᔭᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕋᓱᒃᑐᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᒪᓐᑐᕆᐊᒥᓐ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᖁᐃᓐᓇᖅᖢᓂᐅᒃ.


“ᐅᓇ ᓈᒻᒪᓛᖑᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᓲᖃᐃᒻᒪ ᒪᓐᑐᕆᐊᓪ ᐅᐸᒐᒃᓴᐅᓂᕐᓴᐅᖕᒪᓐ ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥᐅᓄᑦ,” ᐳᕌᓱ-ᕕᐅᕆ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


2022-ᒥ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐊᕕᓂᕐᓂ ᐆᒧᖓ ᐱᕋᔭᒃᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᓗᐊᔭᒧᑦ ᔮᓐ-ᑯᓘᑦ ᓚᑐᕋᕗᒡᒧᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐅᕆᓯᒪᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᖕᒪᑦ   60-ᓂ ᐱᐅᓯᕚᓪᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᔾᔪᑎᐅᓇᔭᕐᑐᓂ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᕆᓂᕐᒥᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᓂ ᓴᐳᔾᔨᓯᒪᓂᕐᒨᕐᑐᓂᒃ ᑕᒫᓂ ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥ.


ᐱᖁᔨᓯᒪᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᑐᑭᒧᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᔨ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᒥ ᐸᓯᔭᒃᓴᐅᑎᑦᑎᕙᑐᓂ, ᑖᒃᑯᐊᓗ ᐱᕋᔭᒍᑎᒋᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᖅᐸᒃᖢᑎᒃ, ᒪᓐᑐᕆᐊᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᕙᒡᓗᓂ ᐊᐃᒪᔅᒥᐅᙱᖔᖅᑐᖅ, ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᔨᓂᒡᓗ ᐊᒥᒐᕐᓯᕙᒃᖢᑎᒃ ᑕᐃᒪᓐᓇᓗ ᑭᖑᕙᕆᐊᕈᑎᐅᔭᖢᓂ.


“ᐅᓇ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐅᕈᑎᓅᖓᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᖅ ᑕᐃᒪᓐᓇᓗ ᐱᑲᔪᕈᑎᐅᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᕐᓴᐅᓂᐊᖅᖢᑎ ᑕᒪᓐᓇ ᑕᐅᕗᖓ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓂᐊᕆᐊᒃᓴᖓᓂᒃ,” ᐳᕌᓱ-ᕕᐅᕆ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᐃᓄᒋᐊᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᑎᑦᑎᓂᖅ ᐱᓇᓱᒍᑎᐅᔪᖅ $75 ᒥᓕᐊᓐᑖᓚᓂ ᓈᒻᒪᙱᓕᐅᕈᑎᐅᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᐅᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᑯᐸᐃᒃ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᖏᓐᓂ.

author: Austin C. McCoy
title: ICE and Data Centers Aren’t New, But Face Growing Pushback as They Intertwine
content:
A New Jersey township ordinance is the first in the US reflecting the link between the deportation regime and Big Tech.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation .

On July 13, residents of Neptune Township, New Jersey, voted to ban AI data centers and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) jails from being built in their town. While protests against the construction of AI data centers and ICE facilities have increased since Donald Trump’s reelection, the Neptune Township ordinance is the first in the U.S. reflecting a connection between the deportation regime and Big Tech.

Neptune residents’ move to oppose technofascism in their town also demonstrates the potential to form new coalitions, powered by grassroots organizing, for more democratic participation in local development. Ben Dziobek, executive director of Climate Revolution Action Network (CRAN), a New Jersey-based organization that helped mobilize support for the bans, told Insider NJ , “Banning ICE detention centers is the same fight as banning data centers … Neptune is deciding what it wants built in its town and what it doesn’t.”

Of course, the current upsurge in demonstrations against AI data centers and ICE immigrant jails is not in response to new phenomena. On the one hand, tech companies like Amazon and Microsoft have been building data centers for years, mostly to warehouse large amounts of data that governments, corporations, and consumers use for digital storage. However, the construction and operation of these new AI data centers raise questions about the undemocratic nature of economic development and Big Tech. Elon Musk’s xAI bypassed federal environmental regulations to build gas turbines for its Tennessee facilities. Meta worked covertly with some of Louisiana’s state elected officials to plan and build AI centers. And Trump, in his second term, has sought to restrict local and state regulation of AI, further greasing the skids for construction. These data centers pose environmental, health, and economic threats to residents and workers. They are linked to noise pollution and exorbitant levels of water and electric usage — and residents have complained of increases in utility bills.

On the other hand, ICE has relied on a network of hundreds of facilities since its formation in 2003. According to a 2024 Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse report on immigration , ICE held nearly 40,000 adults at the end of Joe Biden’s presidential term in January 2025. The Trump administration has sought to dramatically escalate ICE arrests and detentions to enact its white nationalist immigration agenda.

This craven drive to detain and deport as many immigrants as possible is fueling this administration’s attempts to expand its network of camps, including by converting closed prisons and warehouses into ICE facilities. Florida’s infamous South Florida Detention Center, also known as “Alligator Alcatraz,” is one of the most prominent examples of a swiftly built detention camp enacting this administration’s cruel immigration policy. People detained there complained of the inhumane conditions in which they were held, saying that they faced overflowing toilets and were denied prescribed medication and adequate food.

This prison, like some of the AI data centers, also threatens ecosystems and several endangered species in the Everglades. The construction of the South Florida Detention Center generated protests from Floridians and others opposing the construction of the facility and the conditions inside. In fact, protesters gathered for “Freedom Vigils” outside of “Alligator Alcatraz” every Sunday since August 2025 . The political and legal pressure from protesters, people being detained, environmental and civil rights groups, and elected officials forced its closure in June 2026.

The movement to stop data centers and detention camps during Trump’s second term has been relatively successful. Between March and June 2025, protests helped delay or stop 20 data center projects, Kristin Toussaint from Fast Company reports . Opposition to AI data centers continues to stymie Big Tech in 2026. Between January and March of this year, people across the U.S., from Arizona to Virginia , have obstructed or blocked more than $130 billion in data center development.

On the surface, the fight against data centers and detention camps might seem unrelated …

author: Unknown
title: DIY-фест «Тур ноу Футур» пройдёт под Белградом
content:
Планируется масштабная трехдневная встреча с 21 по 23 августа для активистов и левых мигрантов со всей Европы, а также из РФ и Турции. В организации мероприятия, проходящего в рамках большого турне по Европе, задействованы diy-медиа No Future , Фонд поддержки левых политзаключенных , клуб и бар « ЛОЖА », а также сербские анархисты, предоставившие свою площадку. От медиа No Future готовится презентация сериала про жен политзаключенных антифа из России и рассказ, как приготовить DIY чай.

«Как рассказал один из соорганизаторов феста, - пишет No Future . - Это только первая попытка повторить то, что крю делала в российских лесах до всего пиздеца. Мутить начали в июне, поэтому собрать супер лайнап из панк и хардкор команд оперативно не получилось — музыканты уже все по турам. Основной упор на лекции и нетворкинг и субкультурную движуху».

«В этом году мы решили сделать больше прицел на российскую левую эмиграцию и совместить ее немножко с субкультурной составляющей, чтобы приносить политический флер непосредственно в субкультуру, отходить от таких клише, как панк якобы вне политики. Мы хотим совместить приятное с полезным, поскольку все выходцы в целом из панк-движа, в панк-движе и остаются, и при этом активно занимаются политической деятельностью. Формат сдвинулся с музыкально-лекционного именно на лекционно-развлекательный», - объясняет Гриф из Фонда поддержки ЛПЗК в разговоре с No Future .

Он говорит , что намутили полную инфраструктуру (кемпинг, души, туалеты, веганская еда, алкоголь), а также дохера разных активностей: лекции, диджей-сеты, костры, кинопросмотры, бирпонг, панк-караоке, панк-квизы и спортивные ивенты.

«Тема политзаключенных будет обсуждаться как сейчас наиболее важная. В силу того, что в России мы не можем проводить особо каких-то политических действий, наша задача сейчас — сохранять кадры, которые попали в столь неблагополучную ситуацию. Задача — расширить круг знакомств российской миграции, подключить ребят, рассказать, показать, что жизнь продолжается, движуха движется, ну и конечно просто дать ребятам отдохнуть. Чтобы люди уезжали с чувством того, что не все так плохо, ты не один», - говорит Гриф, добавляя, что это попытка показать, как «люди даже в столь мрачные времена делают движ».

О месте проведения мероприятия организаторы сообщат отдельно в своих соцсетях. Подробности о встрече будут тут .

author: Corey Larocque
title: Just build it already!
content:
Sometimes money seems to flow so fast out of Ottawa or the legislative assembly that it’s hard to keep up.


That’s a concern one Nunatsiaq News reader recently pointed out about how often governments — especially the federal government — hold news conferences or issue news releases about spending. But they seem to make less of a splash once the money is spent.


“Enough of the press releases, the $100 million here and $300 million there, announcements,” the anonymous commenter said, using the pseudonym Think About It.


The comment appeared under a

news article

 about Crown-Indigenous Relations Minister Rebecca Alty’s July 23 announcement that the federal government is giving Nunavut $155 million to fund housing, post-secondary and health-care infrastructure.


That’s $81.3 million over 10 years to support housing and post-secondary projects and $74.1 million for health infrastructure over three years, to be allocated by the Government of Nunavut.


“Please just build some […] houses already,” the comment continued. The writer used some stronger language — a colourful adjective in front of “houses” — that conveyed their frustration.


The housing shortage, of course, has long been one of the biggest social issues affecting the North, including Nunavut and Nunavik.


Nunavummiut have been hearing about the territorial government’s Nunavut 3000 plan to build 3,000 new homes between 2022 and 2030. But the progress has been painstakingly slow.


Liberal politicians are always eager to tell the world about the money they’re doling out to Nunavut for this, that or the other thing. But there doesn’t always seem to be corresponding hoopla whenever whatever the money is spent on gets built.


Certainly, the frustration with seeing those politicians shovel money at housing without really seeing a noticeable change in the housing supply is understandable.


In recent months, federal cabinet ministers have made a string of funding announcements in a variety of areas that include housing, education, health care and energy.


On July 29, federal Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin announced $7 million for clean energy projects in Nunavut, Yukon and Northwest Territories. That includes nearly $3 million for solar and other energy projects in Resolute Bay, Chesterfield Inlet, Arviat, Cambridge Bay and Baker Lake, according to a news release from the Department of Natural Resources.


In April, Northern Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand announced

$13 million

 for four projects, including remotely operated vehicles to map the ocean floor around the Qikiqtaaluk Region.


Even Nunavut MP Lori Idlout got in on the action. Earlier that month, she

announced

 $108 million for upgrades to Iqaluit’s sewage system.


Don’t take this the wrong way. The money is great. Keep it coming!


But to the point made by the commenter on the article about Alty’s $155 million, it would be helpful if politicians were as enthusiastic about showing off the results of their spending as they are about announcing the spending in the first place.

title: Iraqi Islamic Resistance: Decision to halt attacks is temporary
content:
Abu Alaa al-Walaei, Secretary-General of the Sayyid al-Shuhada Brigades, issued a statement regarding the Iraqi Resistance Front’s (Iraqi Islamic Resistance) decision to suspend attacks against Saudi Arabia.


Al-Walaei said that the Iraqi Islamic Resistance’s decision to halt attacks on Saudi Arabia is temporary. He explained that the decision was made at the request of leaders of the Coordination Framework, particularly Hadi al-Amiri, Secretary-General of the Badr Organization.


Al-Walaei stressed that the option of retaliatory attacks remains under consideration. He stated that the timing, scope, and method of any response are still being evaluated, emphasizing that the option of retaliation has not been taken off the table.

title: Figen Yüksekdağ’dan çerçeve yasa açıklaması: “Özgürlüğümüz için çerçeve yasaya gerek yok, ama tarihi bir anlamı var”
content:
Eski HDP Eş Genel Başkanı Figen Yüksekdağ, “Benim hakkımda da Selahattin Demirtaş hakkında da AİHM kararları var. Çerçeve yasaya gerek yok ki bizim özgürlüğümüz için. Ama bu yasanın haksız yere cezaevinde tutulan siyasi mahpusların tahliyesinden çok daha büyük ve tarihi bir anlamı var" şeklinde konuştu.

İlke TV Genel Yayın Yönetmeni Sevda Çetinkaya, Kocaeli 1 No'lu F Tipi Yüksek Güvenlikli Kapalı Ceza İnfaz Kurumunda görüştüğü Figen Yüksekdağ'ın söylediklerini aktardı.

Yüksekdağ, gelinen aşamanın kendiliğinden ortaya çıkmadığını; arkasında çok büyük bedeller ödenmiş bir mücadele olduğunu söyledi. Yüksekdağ, “Adı çerçeve ama dar bir çerçeve. Kim istemez bunun daha geniş, daha kapsayıcı olmasını? Dün geçti elime metin ve okuduğumda ‘yine güvenlik kaygısıyla yazılmış bir metinle karşı karşıyayım’ dedim. Suç ve ceza kavramlarının içinden barışa yol arayan bir metin. Asla unutulmaması gereken bir şey var ama. Kürt meselesi Türkiye’de ilk kez doğrudan bir yasal düzenlemenin konusu haline geldi, tarihi bir eşik bu. 1921 Anayasası belgeleri ve o dönem Kürtleri inkar etmeyen anlayışın terk edilmesinden 100 yıl sonra bugün Kürtleri hukuk içine almanın yolunu açacak bir yasal bir düzenlemeyi konuşuyoruz” dedi.

Yüksekdağ, Demirtaş'ın ve kendisinin tahliye edilme olanağına ilişkin ise şunları söyledi: “Bizler zaten haksız ve hukuksuz yere içerdeyiz siyasi faaliyetlerimizden yargılandık ve ceza aldık. Benim hakkımda da Selahattin Demirtaş hakkında da AİHM kararları var. Çerçeve yasaya gerek yok ki bizim özgürlüğümüz için. Ama bu çerçeve yasanın benim de Selahattin beyin de haksız yere cezaevinde tutulan siyasi mahpusların tahliyesinden çok daha büyük ve tarihi bir anlamı var.”

author: Randi Beers
title: News Quiz Aug. 8 | Jump into the water
content:
Happy August! Are you reading beyond the headlines? Read on to find out.


1.

 Iqaluit city council voted last week to give free Aquatic Centre passes to 10 cancer patients. Why?


A.

 A group of youths was behind the initiative, saying they wanted to create a non-profit that spreads random acts of kindness across the city.


B.

 A pair of doctors at Qikiqtani General Hospital plans to incorporate exercise into their patients’ treatment plans, based on research that shows structured activity helps fight cancer.


C.

 Administration identified a surprise surplus of money, and council voted this would be a nice thing to do with it.


2.

 Why might people in Iqaluit be seeing RCMP on more ATVs this summer?


A.

 Officers asked for them because they are fun to ride.


B.

 It’s a new community initiative to spread safety awareness, and it also helps police get to areas they can’t access with a police cruiser.


C.

 The federal government paid for a fleet of ATVs for V Division, so they need to get used.


3.

 Photos will be on their way to Kugaaruk soon. What is significant about them?


A.

 They are part of aerial surveys of areas that have never been seen from this vantage point.


B.

 They are some of the first photos ever taken in Kugaaruk.


C.

 The photos depict traditional life in the area before a community was incorporated at Pelly Bay.


4.

 The Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp. released its most recent northern housing report last week. What proportion of their salaries are Iqaluit’s Inuit population putting towards a new mortgage, on average, in 2025?


A.

 60 per cent


B.

 65 per cent


C.

 70 per cent


5.

 Those walking down Ottawa’s Arts Corridor might notice a giant reproduction of a Sedna embroidery hanging along the route. The piece reinterprets the story of Sedna, but how so?


A.

 It retells the tale through a feminist lens.


B.

 Sedna’s story is retold as though she were a millennial living in modern, urban Canada.


C.

 The embroidery reinterprets her story as though she were not a monster, but misunderstood.


Answers:


An unidentified child and an adult peek into a seal’s breathing hole. (Photo courtesy of Jim Miller)


1.

 B — Structured exercise for colorectal cancer patients has been shown to lead to a 37 per cent lower risk of death and a 28 per cent lower risk of recurrence or developing other cancers, so two doctors at Qikiqtani General Hospital in Iqaluit are incorporating it as part of the treatment plan for 10 patients.


2.

 B — Although ATVs are legitimately more fun to drive than a traditional vehicle, that’s not why police are on them this summer. RCMP officers are using the ATVs to spread safety awareness about the vehicles, get closer to the community and access places they can’t get to in a traditional police cruiser.


3.

 C — Many of the photos show members of Kugaaruk’s Immingark family living a traditional life in the mid 1960s. Lucy Immingark is expected to receive them soon and plans to display them in the hamlet. She said the photos are significant to her because they show her father, her grandfather and many other people she grew up with.


4.

 C — Inuit in Iqaluit put aside a whopping 70 per cent of their household income towards a new mortgage in 2025, according to research released last week by Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp.


5.

 A — A giant replica of Gayle Uyagaqi Kabloona’s Sedna embroidery tells the sea monster’s tale through a feminist lens. She told Nunatsiaq News she wanted to tell a traditional story but examine women’s experiences as well. “As I got older, I noticed that a lot of the women in the traditional stories have some kind of violence done to them by the men in society, or their families, or their husbands, or somebody,” she said.
